The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.

CISA added CVE-2026-41709, the ESX insufficient-logging flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 on evidence of active exploitation, naming no actor (CISA KEV). CrowdStrike says WARP PANDA deployed several forms of malware in victims' VMware vCenter environments and that in several of these cases, as late as early 2026, the adversary exploited the ESXi command logging bypass CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day; it describes intrusions at U.S.-based entities that included the legal sector, and gives no indicators, no account of what goes unlogged and no date of first exploitation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-28). Broadcom's advisory rates the flaw 2.7 and carries no exploitation statement (Broadcom, 2026-07-29). CrowdStrike does not say how the actor obtained administrator rights on the host or whether the flaws of CVE-2026-59309 and CVE-2026-59310 were involved, so no link to them is drawn. Until the fix is installed, ESX logs from a period of administrator access are not reliable evidence of what was done; vCenter task and event records and syslog forwarded off the host are the sources to review.

First published 2026-05-15 · open finding →

Update29 Oct 2026 04:52 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryupdated_atprioritytagstechniquesentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; Dream Research describes such a chain used against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. The CVE record moves to exploited, the priority from notable to high, and the earlier statement that no source reports exploitation of this CVE is replaced. Removed from the text: the sentence that an attacker can modify any file the user can read (the Detection line still carries it) and, from the summary, the clause on Aikido's report of working Kubernetes exploits for the Dirty Frag family.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says in the entry that the flaw can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, naming no actor or victim (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Dream Research describes a chain of this kind from artifacts its tooling recovered: a custom, non-public PHP2Shell build, tailored to the management web server of one large vendor's firewall software that runs PHP 8.0.30, gives code execution as the nobody user, and the Fragnesia exploit then overwrites /etc/pam.d/su in the page cache so that su root succeeds without a password; Dream says SELinux confines the web server's domain from modifying system files and that the whole chain runs in one HTTP request in under 15 minutes (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). From about 19,000 internet-facing firewalls of that vendor that it found through a search engine, the attacker narrowed to 240 in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, rooted 24 and planted a PHP webshell on each; on the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed) it set up an outbound SSH tunnel kept up by a systemd service and an rc.local entry, rooted the organization's firewall management server through the tunnel, decrypted the LDAP service-account password with root access and sprayed passwords against a domain that had no lockout threshold (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). Dream could not tell whether any of the Active Directory attacks succeeded, does not name the vendor, calls the campaign apparently Chinese and AI-assisted and does not attribute it to a named actor (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Sources: Wiz Research, 2026-05-13 · Help Net Security, 2026-05-14 · Red Hat (RHSB-2026-003) · Red Hat Product Security · Aikido Security · FIRST.org EPSS API · Microsoft Security Blog · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog · Dream Research

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport; the new application's identifiers on the Trust Center page are unreadable here); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport, fourth run); ox-security (feed lists dated items but every article body is 403); previdian (listing feed 403, one featured CVE only); resecurity (empty JavaScript shell); golem-security (cookie wall); F5 K000163821 (my.f5.com is a JavaScript shell on every reader, so F5's exposure, mitigation and exploitation wording is unread); Juniper support portal (JavaScript shells); Broadcom per-product PHP2Shell pages (login-gated); the Cisco advisory's Snort rule links were not re-read after version 1.9; Palo Alto's PAN-OS hotfix status was re-read before the commit (19 of 20 released, only 11.1.7-h12 still carries an estimated date, 2026-10-30), so that build is the one to re-read at the next fire.

Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data. →
  2. 02PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited. Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove. →
  3. 03HPE ClearPass 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 are affected by PHP2Shell; a hotfix patch exists for each train. HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, lists ClearPass Policy Manager 6.14.0 and earlier and 6.11.15 and earlier as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each scored CVSS 3.1 9.8, adds the 6.12 train in its machine-readable record, and names a hotfix patch for 6.14.1, 6.12.8 and 6.11.16. HPE asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected instances are upgraded; the bulletin says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass, although CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 3Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 14

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLENATOB2

DeadTag: re-registered domains of defunct analytics and advertising tags redirect visitors of thousands of sites, among them to a page that serves the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, which compromise a vulnerable device when the page opens

Report URI and iVerify describe a campaign they name DeadTag: attackers buy the expired domains behind old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that still carries the tag runs the operator's script without the site owner changing or noticing anything, and the operator sells the visitors those tags bring in (Report URI, 2026-10-22). Report URI has identified more than 660 re-registered domains still embedded on thousands of sites and cautiously estimates 135 million visits a month (Report URI, 2026-10-22). The script is about 2 KB, does nothing for search engines, scanners and other bots, asks the operator's server what to do with each visitor and redirects the chosen ones, and Report URI found that the operator stopped answering when it probed from data-centre addresses or returned too often from residential ones; destinations include scam pages, a fake VPN pop-up and, for iPhones, a page that serves two exploit kits (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

One chain ends at a fake prediction-market page that picks the kit by the visitor's iOS version, Coruna for iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified "P7" variant of DarkSword for iOS 18.4 to 18.7; both attack the browser itself, so opening the page is enough to compromise a vulnerable device, and the spyware they install steals keychain passwords, crypto-wallet app data and device and account information and reports to one server; Report URI notes that Coruna and DarkSword are separate exploit kits that have been seen in different campaigns, and that here both send their stolen data to the same server, which it reads as one operator running both (Report URI, 2026-10-22). iVerify reads DeadTag as mostly focused on European domains rather than .com (iVerify, 2026-10-21), and saw the P7 variant reach an employee's device at a customer organisation through a malicious Instagram ad while the employee was scrolling in the app (iVerify, 2026-10-21). The kit operator does not rely on DeadTag alone: Report URI found DarkSword loaders on hundreds of online shops on one e-commerce platform, PrestaShop (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any public website that still loads a script from a third-party domain whose provider no longer operates it, where the browser fetches nothing useful and the page looks normal, and any iPhone on iOS 13 to 17.2.1 or 18.4 to 18.7 that opens such a page (Report URI, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Inventory the external script references of each public site and flag any whose domain has been re-registered or no longer belongs to its provider; Report URI recommends script monitoring that shows when a new script or domain appears on a page, and a Content Security Policy that controls which domains a site may load code from (Report URI, 2026-10-22). A security scanner usually sees only an empty response from the malicious script, because the operator answers only selected visitors.
Defender takeaway
Remove dead third-party tags from every site you run, enforce a Content Security Policy and keep iPhones on the current iOS, with Lockdown Mode for people who may be targeted; for an iPhone that may have opened an affected page, Report URI advises restarting it, changing the passwords stored in its keychain and moving crypto assets to a new wallet (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

threat28 Oct 03:54Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Report URI (Scott Helme) · iVerify Threat Intelligence Team
ROUTINENATOC3

ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment

The tracker DeXpose recorded on 2026-09-15 that SafePay had claimed an attack on ARA Lyss, the wastewater-treatment association at ara-lyss.ch, posting that the full leak would be published soon unless a company representative made contact (DeXpose, 2026-09-15). Inside IT reported on 2026-10-27 that SafePay has put the stolen data into the darknet, about 49 GB in the case of the Bernese association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, that the security firm Risikomonitor analysed it, and that the association's management declined to comment (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT and not verified independently, finds about 3,200 e-mail addresses and data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons; user folders and a data store with content up to March 2026 that hold 255 password hits, 195 of them very weak; bank statements and a transaction list with more than 100 payments by private persons with name and address; the full login data to the monitoring portals of the photovoltaic plants of another company's customers, stored on the same server; and a 2015 applicant list with birth dates, civil status, former employer and interview notes that was never deleted (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

BACS told Inside IT that SafePay, which relies on double extortion, is among the more active ransomware groups in Switzerland and, together with The Gentlemen, the third most active in 2026 after Akira and Payload, that it has no clear focus on Switzerland, and that it was first observed there in May 2025 (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). No source says how the attackers got in or that data was encrypted at the association.

Defender takeaway
A communal body or association should look for credentials, bank statements and applicant files on its own file servers before an attacker does: Risikomonitor found 255 password hits in files, another company's portal logins and a 2015 applicant list that had never been deleted, and those are what a published dump gives fraudsters (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

Sources: Inside IT (article with Risikomonitor's analysis) · DeXpose (leak-site tracker, claim record)

02Trending vulnerabilities3 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-48356exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source: an unauthenticated file upload attacked since March 2026, fixed for supported lines in July, and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-10-27

Sansec named the flaw PolyShell: a missing validation in Magento's REST API that lets unauthenticated attackers upload executable files to a store, using a polyglot (code disguised as an image) to pass the image check (Sansec, 2026-03-17). It reports that its Shield service has blocked exploitation attempts against 79.5% of the Magento stores it protects since 2026-03-16, with first attacks observed on 2026-03-19, and that the vulnerable code has existed since the first Magento 2 release (Sansec, 2026-03-17). On 2026-03-30 a mass wave uploaded webshells, spread backdoor scripts across several directories and injected a JavaScript loader into the CMS pages of 471 stores within one hour (Sansec, 2026-03-30).

Sansec dates a fix in Magento 2.4.9 to 2026-05-12, without a backport to the supported 2.4.8 and 2.4.7 lines, and the backport to those lines to 2026-07-14, in bulletin APSB26-73 (Sansec, 2026-03-17). That bulletin rates the flaw Critical at CVSS 3.1 9.6, lists 2.4.9 among the affected versions, names the 2026-jul builds, 2.4.9-2026-jul included, as the fix for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, and still says Adobe is not aware of any exploits in the wild (Adobe, 2026-07-14). CISA added CVE-2026-48356 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation and gives no detail (CISA, 2026-10-27; CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). Sansec's research of 2026-10-24 shows the operator behind the March wave still active: its newest loader domain, registered on 2026-10-06, sits in the CMS blocks of 83 stores, 60 of which already carried an earlier loader, and one of them, on Magento 2.4.7-p1, still lacks APSB26-73 and holds PolyShell webshells disguised as images (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

Exposure
Every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store without the 2026-jul fix, 2.4.9 included (Adobe, 2026-07-14); the anonymous guest-cart item routes need no credentials, and the upload becomes code execution on stock nginx for the oldest 2.x lines, on any non-stock nginx that hands every .php file to the PHP handler, and on Magento before 2.3.5 running on Apache without the engine switch set for that directory (Sansec, 2026-03-17).
Detection
Sansec calls any .php, .phtml or .phar file in the custom-options upload directory a strong indicator of compromise, and the uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17); also look for requests that add items to guest carts with embedded file data from unfamiliar sources (Sansec, 2026-03-17), script tags in the CMS block table and administrator accounts nobody created (Sansec, 2026-10-24).
Defender takeaway
Install the fix now, and treat a store that ran an unpatched build while internet-reachable since March as possibly compromised until its upload directory, CMS blocks and administrator accounts are checked, because an uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17), so the fix does not remove a shell already written (an inference), and deleting a loader script does not remove the access behind it (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

vulnerability28 Oct 03:54Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Sansec (PolyShell advisory) · Sansec (mass PolyShell attack wave) · Sansec (CMS block loader campaign) · Adobe (security bulletin APSB26-73) · CISA (alert, CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.27)
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, HPE Networking ClearPass Policy Manager: bulletin HPESBNW05171 lists the 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 trains as affected by the PHP2Shell flaws and names a hotfix patch for each (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, covers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the PHP flaws behind PHP2Shell, in ClearPass Policy Manager and scores each CVSS 3.1 9.8 with network access, no privileges and no user interaction (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Its affected-products note lists ClearPass 6.14.0 and earlier in the 6.14 release train and 6.11.15 and earlier in the 6.11 train, while its machine-readable record also lists the 6.12 train and gives 6.14.1, 6.11.16 and 6.12.8 as the boundaries; the bulletin does not reconcile the two (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). The fix is a hotfix patch for each train, 6.14.1, 6.12.8 (added in revision 3, which HPE says "exceptionally" includes 6.12.8) and 6.11.16, downloadable from the HPE Networking Support Portal; versions past end of maintenance are presumed affected and are not covered, and HPE has not assessed versions past end of support, which it says should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

HPE recommends confining the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN, or controlling them with firewall policy at layer 3 and above, and asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected ClearPass instances have been upgraded (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Other HPE Networking products and software versions it does not list are not known to be affected, and for Mist products the bulletin points to a Juniper reference advisory (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27); the bulletin itself says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Every ClearPass Policy Manager on the 6.14, 6.12 or 6.11 train without the hotfix patch; the guest portal and the management interfaces are the surfaces HPE asks to take off public access (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).
Detection
HPE gives no indicator and no post-patch check; CISA's PHP alert advises monitoring for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-21), which on a ClearPass node would be processes started by the web worker account (an inference, since HPE does not describe how ClearPass runs PHP).
Defender takeaway
Install the hotfix patch for 6.14.1, 6.12.8 or 6.11.16 on every node now, the remediation HPE's bulletin names, and take any guest portal or management interface reachable from untrusted networks off public access, as HPE asks (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).
Update30 Oct 2026 03:53 UTCrun 2026-10-30T0255Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

HPE's revision 3 of bulletin HPESBNW05171, dated 2026-10-29, updates its affected and resolution sections to exceptionally include ClearPass 6.12.8 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). A ClearPass 6.12.8 hotfix patch for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 is now named beside the 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 patches, downloadable from the HPE Networking Support Portal (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). The affected-products note of this revision reads 6.14.0 and earlier in the 6.14 train and 6.11.15 and earlier in the 6.11 train, while its machine-readable record gives 6.14.1, 6.11.16 and 6.12.8 as boundaries, and the wording of revision 2 that named 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 as versions providing some level of mitigation is no longer in the bulletin (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). The bulletin still says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass.

Sources: HPE Networking (CSAF advisory HPESBNW05171, revision 2, superseded at this URL by revision 3) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.27) · CISA (alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching) · HPE Networking (CSAF advisory HPESBNW05171, revision 3)
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Cisco Expressway, Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Duo Access Gateway and ISE Portal Builder: Cisco's final PHP2Shell advisory names Expressway 15.5.21 and Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0 as the fixes and knows of no malicious use against its products

Cisco's advisory cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq, published on 2026-10-21 and final at version 1.10 on 2026-10-30, lists Expressway, Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Duo Access Gateway and ISE Portal Builder as affected by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the PHP flaws behind PHP2Shell (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30). Expressway Series and Expressway Select Series (bug CSCwx37062) have fixed release 15.5.21 and a workaround described in the bug record; Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul and Unified Industrial Wireless Software (bug CSCwx37073) have fixed release 26.2.1.9, listed for November 2026, and a workaround, and there the attacker must be authenticated as an administrator, which lowers the CVSS 3.1 score to 6.6; Duo Access Gateway is fixed in 3.2.0; and ISE Portal Builder has a fix deployed with no customer action required (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30). The advisory gives no affected-version ranges and no workaround steps; its bug records carry platform-specific information, workarounds and fixed releases, and a product it does not list is, in Cisco's review, not affected (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

Cisco says it is aware that a public announcement is available and knows of no malicious use of the flaws against any Cisco product (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). For Expressway the PHP fix is 15.5.21 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28), while the release Cisco names for the unauthenticated root command execution on clustered units, CVE-2026-76466, is X15.5.20 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Every Expressway Series and Expressway Select unit and every Duo Access Gateway not on a release Cisco lists as fixed (15.5.21 and 3.2.0), since Cisco gives no affected-version ranges; the advisory names no version-check command and no component that runs the PHP; its bug records CSCwx37062 and CSCwx37073 carry platform-specific information (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).
Detection
Cisco publishes no indicator and reports no attack on its products, but lists Snort rules 67359 and 67360 as action links for the advisory (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); beyond that, CISA's PHP alert advises monitoring for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-21), which on these products would be processes started by the web worker account (an inference, since Cisco does not describe how they run PHP).
Defender takeaway
Move Expressway to 15.5.21 and Duo Access Gateway to 3.2.0, the fixed releases the table names (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); an Expressway already upgraded to X15.5.20 for the clustered-device flaw (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21) is not named as fixed in the PHP table, which lists only 15.5.21 (an inference from the table, not a Cisco statement), so apply the bug record's workaround until 15.5.21 is installed (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul has no fixed release before November 2026, so its workaround is the control until then.
Update29 Oct 2026 04:58 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_atcvessourcesevidencebody

Cisco published version 1.9 of the advisory on 2026-10-28 to update the fix availability date for Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul and Unified Industrial Wireless Software: release 27.1.1 is now listed for November 2026 instead of March 2027, and the workaround in bug CSCwx37073 remains the control until it ships (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). The other rows are unchanged, and Cisco still knows of no malicious use against its products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

Update31 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelsummarycvessourcesevidencebody

Cisco revised the advisory to version 1.10 on 2026-10-30, updating the fix status for ISE Portal Builder and the fixed release for Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul and Unified Industrial Wireless Software (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30). The table now lists release 26.2.1.9 (Nov 2026) for that wireless software instead of 27.1.1, and shows ISE Portal Builder as "Fix deployed, no customer action required" instead of offline for remediation; Cisco also added Webex Events to the products it confirms are not vulnerable (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30). Expressway 15.5.21 and Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0 are unchanged.

HIGHCVE-2026-61425 +11exploitedupdatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-61425, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access

First published 2026-07-26 · open finding →

Update28 Oct 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27 with two security fixes rated Critical, for the versions 2.20.4.1 and earlier (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-102788 is in the sort-by URL parameter of store and category post lists and CVE-2026-102789 is a missing permission check on the editor task that loads blog posts (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27); Balbooa's fixes are a strict allowlist validation for the sort-by parameter and a user edit-level check on the editor task (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). mySites.guru says the sort value previously went into the ORDER BY part of the database query and reads the second flaw as a second anonymous route to the same query. mySites.guru reports that the Joomla CNA scores both CVSS 4.0 9.3 and lists every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.4.1 as affected, and that only two PHP files differ between 2.20.4.1 and 2.20.4.2, one per fix (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

Both flaws read data: an anonymous visitor can extract the Joomla user table, with its password hashes, and every other table the site's extensions created. mySites.guru says about 95% of the Gridbox sites it monitors ran an affected version on the morning of the release, that sites on the Joomla 3 line stop at Gridbox 2.17.0.2, which has no fix for this year's flaws, and that there is no public report of exploitation yet (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27). Nothing here is reported exploited, unlike the July batches above; the version to be on is now 2.20.4.2.

Detection
In web access and database query logs, store or category list requests whose sort-by value is not one of the known sort keys, repeated anonymous calls to the Gridbox editor's blog-post task, and slow-query bursts from the web account; because the flaws only read, the post-patch check is credential hygiene on a site that was exposed, starting with administrator accounts nobody created, since the password hashes can be worked on offline.
Defender takeaway
Update to 2.20.4.2 now, communal and agency sites included, and move Joomla 3 sites to a supported Joomla (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).
Sources: mySites.guru · Balbooa · Balbooa (Gridbox 2.20.4.2 security update)

Verification. Iterations 1 to 7 each returned NEEDS_FIXES (their findings and remediations are in the record above) and the first CLEAN landed at the 8-iteration cap, so no confirmation pass was possible: the run publishes on that single CLEAN as a fail-open and the waiver is recorded. Open advisories, all pre-existing wording or length from earlier fires and left to the quality audit: the Gridbox entry's legacy em dashes, its re-floated high priority and the CVE-2026-61425 CNA score difference (9.4 against the discloser's 10.0), and the PHP entry's length on a non-deep-dive.

What this fire changed. Five new entries (Cisco PHP2Shell advisory, HPE ClearPass PHP2Shell, the CISA-listed Adobe Commerce upload flaw CVE-2026-48356, ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, DeadTag) and nine changelog records. The two that matter most: Palo Alto's advisory of 2026-10-27 now states active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces (PAN-OS entry notable to high, PHP entry stays critical with the statement added), and CISA's KEV listing of the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 on 2026-10-27 moved the Node2Shell entry to exploited and high.

KEV rows (kev-window.txt).

  • CVE-2026-111497: COVERED-STALE on two entries, both given update records (Node2Shell entry; the .NET entry, whose CVE record now carries exploited, cisa-kev and says Microsoft's own record still read not exploited on 2026-10-25).
  • CVE-2026-48356 (Adobe Commerce and Magento upload flaw, KEV 2026-10-27): NOT COVERED, shipped as a notable entry. It was first held back as borderline (CISA's listing and Adobe's bulletin give no exploitation detail, no constituency nexus); the verifier then found Sansec's PolyShell reporting, which the CVE record itself links: attacks since 2026-03-19, a mass wave on 2026-03-30 and the fix timeline (2.4.9 on 2026-05-12, supported-line backport 2026-07-14). The entry now rests on Sansec, Adobe and CISA together, and the store already carries four Adobe Commerce or Magento entries.
  • No RANSOMWARE rows.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md). ARX Group SA (Aurora leak-site claim): held, unchanged: S2 and S4 searched in German, Italian and English and read Inside IT, Netzwoche, SRF, Blick, ICTjournal, NZZ, RTS and swisscybersecurity.net; no ARX, SBB or ASTRA/USTRA statement and no Swiss press report exist, expiry 2026-11-07. The 2026-10-14 strike of the ARA Lyss row is overtaken by Inside IT's report of 2026-10-27 and the new ARA Lyss entry.

Supersessions and corrections. Palo Alto's statement replaces the PAN-OS entry's "no malicious exploitation" text and its availability-only score (8.7 to 9.2); the PHP entry's "no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise" now carries the Palo Alto exception. Camping.Care: a second customer's notice says the supplier is investigating the cause and does not mention PHP, so the entry now says the PHP link rests on SRF, Blick and TCS. Manno: the entry's "claim could not be corroborated, no dataset" statements are replaced by Inside IT's report that about 30 GB were published (single source, Risikomonitor's analysis unverified, rating B3). IDC Frontier: the seventh report names the cause, so "intrusion route not public" is replaced.

Contradictions and borderline includes.

  • Contradiction: Palo Alto's exploitation wording. An Internet Archive copy of the advisory taken 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC says "very limited exploitation", the page read 2026-10-28 says "active exploitation ... exposed to the internet", and the vendor timeline records no such change; the PAN-OS and PHP entries state both and tie neither to the 16:40 UTC revision.
  • Contradiction: Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 (2026-07-14, updated 2026-08-11) says no exploits are known for CVE-2026-48356, while Sansec reports attacks since 2026-03-19 and CISA lists the flaw as exploited; Adobe's CVE record scores it 9.3 where the bulletin says 9.6. The entry states both.
  • Contradiction: HPE HPESBNW05171 names ClearPass 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 as versions "providing some level of mitigation" in its workaround text, while its affected list covers 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 and below and its remediation names hotfix patches for both; the entry quotes the bulletin and does not resolve it.
  • Borderline include: Balbooa Gridbox CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, an unauthenticated read-side SQL injection with no exploitation report, folded into the July Gridbox entry as an update record (the store's pattern for later Gridbox batches, which moved its action to 2.20.4.2). Kept under the "otherwise" limb of PD-11 (b), the leg that holds being a two-file fix diff that hands over the technique; the July Gridbox flaws were exploited, these two are not reported exploited, and no Swiss nexus is established.

Single-source and reduced-confidence inclusions.

  • ARA Lyss-Limpachtal: Inside IT relays Risikomonitor's analysis; DeXpose carries the claim; C3, routine, no encryption mapped because no source states it.
  • Cisco, HPE ClearPass, Balbooa (with mySites.guru, on the Gridbox update): vendor first-party; Cisco and HPE carry cvss: n/a or the vendor's score only.
  • Adobe Commerce CVE-2026-48356: the exploitation history rests on Sansec's own telemetry and scans (a security vendor) with CISA's listing and Adobe's bulletin; confidence high, reliability B.
  • DeadTag: Report URI and iVerify published jointly, so one account from two vantage points, credibility 2.

borderline-drop lines.

  • Gotenberg CVE-2026-42589 (VulnCheck canary telemetry, 1,358 events): internal document-conversion service, five-month-old flaw, not in CISA KEV, no established constituency exposure.
  • Oracle October CPU, 90 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0 or higher (73 distinct CVE ids) against the 12 in the existing entry's title: the entry states the full tally, the CPU is applied as a whole and none is reported exploited; not widened. Oracle Alert CVE-2026-109618 rev 2 Oracle Communications rows: telecom signalling products, no nexus (Secure Backup and Solaris are already in the OT-products entry).
  • Cisco eMudhra informational (revised 2026-10-27): vendor-status churn on a covered entry that already carries the Cisco rows.
  • Chrome 156.0.8078.73/.74 (52 fixes, four Critical), Mozilla MFSA 2026-118 to 122, Apple iOS 27.2, 26.7.2 and 18.7.11 (162 CVEs), GLPI 11.0.9 and 10.0.27, Joomla extension releases of 2026-10-26/27, EUVD criticals (Pie Register, llama.cpp ggml-rpc, OpenRemote): none reported exploited, no constituency nexus.
  • Tailscale and headscale audit by Cyberdione Labs ("Tailworm", fixed in v1.104.4): needs an approved peer whose policy allows forwarding, no CVE, no exploitation, constituency exposure not established.
  • Yoba (Check Point, fake GitHub AI-app projects with DLL sideloading): commodity technique, no constituency specificity.
  • Arctic Wolf on Microsoft Teams external-chat impersonation: known technique, primary dated 2026-10-26 outside the window, Swiss relay only.
  • HMICFRS inspection of police and fire and rescue cyber posture: UK regulator report, awareness level, no Swiss obligation.
  • Kaspersky managed-Kubernetes isolation chain (provider anonymised, fixed), EDK II CVE-2026-97631 (the 2026-10-25 audit's reopen conditions are unmet), Popcorn Time updater (sinkholed since March, no exploitation), Sysdig pickle research, Bishop Fox PHP2Shell guidance (marginal delta on an entry that already carries KEV, public exploit and hardening): no change to what a Swiss SOC does.
  • Swiss Ice Hockey Federation MYSIHF (valid-account theft, private federation), BACS weekly review week 43 (WhatsApp account takeover, consumer fraud; week 42 was also not published): no public-sector nexus.
  • Moldova government digital services (about 750,000 records through unauthenticated services, no service or flaw named), University of Copenhagen test environment, GMO Onamae Desktop Cloud (Japan), Navigate360 / Canadian Crime Stoppers (investigation opened by the Privacy Commissioner), UNM Health, ENGIE, Medienwerkstatt Sulgen: out of nexus or no vector, actor or behaviour beyond the impact. Leak-site claims without victim or A/B-press confirmation (ECOM, SunTechnics Fabrisolar, Bristol City Council, OCMW Machelen, Alliance Police Nationale) stay out (PD-6).
  • Convertr / Plausible CE CVE-2026-8467 (Magecart skimmer, suspected entry): suspected only, out of nexus; a pointer for the next audit.

Sources. karimi-honeypot-data promoted to active (promotion_due). Two candidates added because published entries cite them: ellio-threat-research, jfrog-security-research. Not added: Eye Security Research and Eclypsium (S3 leads, unused), risikomonitor-news and hacksnack.ch (S2 and S4 leads, reliability C and D, relays only). Recipe notes recorded for hpe-networking-psirt (changes.csv), cisco-psirt (feed), paloalto-psirt (advisory JSON), inside-it-ch (__NEXT_DATA__), apa-ots, ransomware-live and databreaches-net. connectwise-trust-center and ec-digital-strategy-newsroom stay 403 on every transport; a 403 never demotes.

Registry. Added incident:ara-region-lyss-limpachtal-ransomware-2026-09, campaign:deadtag, tool:coruna and tool:darksword, the aliases Brotli2Shell, HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell on tool:node2shell, and seven product entities through sync_products.py (five from the new entries, Bun and Istio from the Node2Shell update).

Watchlist: products checked=0, hits=0; suppliers checked=0, hits=0 (no watchlists configured).

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport, third run); resecurity (empty JavaScript shell, newest post 2026-10-14 by search); golem-security (cookie wall); apa-ots (feed holds only the 15 newest releases, no lookback sweep possible); nau-ch, push-security, novee-security (nothing in the horizon; novee-security marketing only, demotion candidate); Juniper PHP2Shell reference advisory (Salesforce shell on every reader) and QNAP QSA-26-18 (reader returned navigation only) were not re-read, so any QNAP revision after 2026-10-27 is unverified; the Citrix community post is 403 on every direct transport and was read only through the reader.

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01PHP2Shell hits NetModule routers with no fix, macmon, Schneider, B&R, HMS, Wibu and Oracle products. Industrial, building and network-access vendors have published their own notices for the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Belden says all versions of NetModule NRSW, the router software of the Bern-headquartered NetModule AG, are affected with no patched release and advises disabling the web interface; macmon 6.x and 7.x, Schneider Electric Security Expert and Control Engineering, B&R APROL, HMS Netbiter, Wibu-Systems CodeMeter License Central and Oracle Secure Backup and Solaris 11 carry fixes or remediations at varying stages. →
  2. 02Gheist abuses stolen GitHub tokens to dump secrets through Actions; GitHub's hold covers public repositories only. Wiz Research has tracked since 2026-09-15 an automated campaign, Gheist, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to commit a secret-dumping Actions workflow to every repository each token can reach, more than 13,500 branches from more than 850 accounts. GitHub's approval hold of 2026-07-28 stops the workflow on public github.com repositories, but not on private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server, where Wiz saw the runs complete and the organizations' own workflows assume AWS roles on the attacker branches. →
  3. 03Camping.Care booking data stolen: TCS and a second campsite warn of WhatsApp fraud; PHP link not vendor-confirmed. TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 guests after data was stolen at Camping.Care, the Dutch supplier of the booking system for all TCS campsites; TCS confirmed the theft to SRF on 2026-10-26, SRF reports it in connection with the PHP security hole and Blick says the attackers used the two critical PHP flaws, though no source names a CVE or the entry point. Names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers are already used in fraudulent WhatsApp messages; TCS says account and IBAN data were not affected and the hole is closed. A second customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of the same fraud in a notice that says Camping.care is still investigating the cause and does not mention PHP. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 8Action items 11

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Camping.Care booking system (TCS Camping): customer and booking data stolen in connection with the PHP flaws, with real reservation numbers already used in WhatsApp fraud and 15,000 guests warned as a precaution

TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 guests as a precaution because the provider of its booking system, Camping.Care, suffered a data theft; TCS confirmed to the SRF consumer programme Espresso on 2026-10-26 that fraudsters could steal customer and booking information, and SRF reports the case in connection with the worldwide PHP security hole (SRF, 2026-10-26). Blick describes Camping.Care as a Dutch company whose booking system handles reservations for all campsites of the Touring Club Schweiz, writes, citing SRF, that the hackers used the critical PHP flaw to steal customer and booking data and that Camping.Care is not the only software supplier hit (Blick, 2026-10-26). No source names the CVE identifiers, the entry point, the date of the intrusion or an actor, and TCS says the hole has since been closed (SRF, 2026-10-26). The stolen data already in criminal use includes, among other data, names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers: guests received fraudulent WhatsApp messages that refer to existing reservations (SRF, 2026-10-26). TCS says account details and IBANs were not affected and that credit card data is not stored in the booking system (SRF, 2026-10-26). A second customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, told its guests in a notice (page date 2026-10-23) that Camping.care had informed it of WhatsApp messages to guests of several campsites that contain real booking information and a link, that Camping.care is investigating the cause and that booking data must be assumed to have been used without authorisation; the notice does not mention PHP, and Netzwoche points out that it does not say whether the attackers used one of the PHP flaws (Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23; Netzwoche, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
The guests who booked through the TCS campsite booking system, about 15,000 of whom TCS has warned, and any other customer of the Camping.Care platform, one of which, Campingplatz Hüttenberg, has warned its own guests; Blick says Camping.Care is not the only software supplier hit (Blick, 2026-10-26; Netzwoche, 2026-10-27).
Detection
The only signal the sources describe is on the recipient side, unsolicited WhatsApp messages that quote a real reservation with the correct name, telephone number and reservation number; no source gives intrusion telemetry from the supplier's systems (SRF, 2026-10-26).

Triage: TCS Camping sends no automated booking details, payment requests or reservation links over WhatsApp, so a WhatsApp message of that kind that quotes a genuine reservation is the fraud, however accurate its details (SRF, 2026-10-26).

Defender takeaway
For a booking, ticketing or citizen-portal application that a supplier runs on PHP, ask the supplier in writing whether its runtime was updated to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (CISA, 2026-10-26) and whether customer data was accessed before that, because SRF, Blick and a TCS spokesperson tie this theft to the PHP flaws (SRF, 2026-10-26; Blick, 2026-10-26; watson.ch, 2026-10-26), although a customer's notice says the supplier is still investigating the cause (Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23) and no source says how the intrusion happened; and tell the people whose data the supplier holds that a message quoting their real booking details is no proof that it comes from you.
Update28 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Netzwoche reported on 2026-10-27 that a second Swiss Camping.Care customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of WhatsApp messages about existing bookings that contain real booking information and a link; the campsite's notice carries the page date 2026-10-23 (Netzwoche, 2026-10-27; Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23). The notice says Camping.care informed the campsite of the messages, that Camping.care is investigating the cause and that booking data must be assumed to have been used without authorisation; it does not mention PHP, and Netzwoche points out that it does not say whether the attackers used one of the PHP flaws. The link to the PHP flaws therefore rests on SRF, Blick and a TCS spokesperson's statement to Keystone-SDA (watson.ch, 2026-10-26), not on the supplier.

Builds on: 2026-10-21/php-critical-release-pre-announced-cve-2026-109618-109619

incident27 Oct 03:53Zsingle-source · victim disclosureOpen finding →
Sources: SRF (Espresso) · Blick · CISA (alert, updated 2026-10-26) · Campingplatz Hüttenberg (guest notice, page date 2026-10-23) · Netzwoche · watson.ch (Keystone-SDA dispatch)
NOTABLENATOB2

Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens plant a secret-dumping workflow in every repository they reach; GitHub's July approval hold stops it on public github.com repositories but not on private ones or GitHub Enterprise Server

Wiz Research has tracked since 2026-09-15 a campaign it calls Gheist, after the user agent on its API calls, that uses stolen GitHub access tokens to create a branch and commit a workflow named sync-check in every repository each token can reach: more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts, from personal projects to private enterprise repositories (Wiz, 2026-10-25). Wiz traces the tokens to infostealer logs and earlier supply-chain compromises (Wiz, 2026-10-25). The push triggers the workflow, which prints the repository's secrets, and those of any deployment environment, into its own run log; GitHub masks secret values only when they appear verbatim, so a base32-encoded value prints in full, the tool downloads the log through the GitHub API and deletes the run seconds later, and because the secrets leave through GitHub's own API there is no attacker domain or connection to block (Wiz, 2026-10-25). In enterprise organizations the tool cycled through the tokens of several users and automation accounts within minutes and cloned private repositories before planting the workflow; hours later cloud credentials from the same organization were used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager (Wiz, 2026-10-25). Around 2026-10-19 the second variant added a job for repositories with a self-hosted runner that searches the host, and through the Docker socket its root filesystem, for tokens, private keys, environment files and Terraform state; Wiz calls the job buggy (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Since 2026-07-28 GitHub holds potentially malicious workflow runs in public repositories until a collaborator approves them, and every public Gheist run Wiz checked stayed held; the hold applies to public repositories on github.com only and not to GitHub Enterprise Server (Wiz, 2026-10-25; GitHub, 2026-07-28). In private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments Wiz saw runs on the attacker branches complete and be deleted, and cloud audit logs showed the organizations' own workflows running on those branches and assuming AWS roles (Wiz, 2026-10-25). As of 2026-10-24 Wiz called the attack ongoing and distinct from the earlier GhostAction campaign (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Exposure
Organizations whose developers or automation accounts hold GitHub tokens that an infostealer or earlier compromise could have exposed, above all with private repositories, GitHub Enterprise Server, cloud OIDC workflows or self-hosted runners (Wiz, 2026-10-25).
Detection
In GitHub audit logs, workflow runs on a branch named ci-sync- plus six random characters that were deleted within a minute of completing, and API activity with the user agent gheist; in cloud audit logs, role assumptions whose OIDC subject names such a branch, which shows Actions ran on an attacker branch even where GitHub logs are not collected; on self-hosted runners, the helper files Wiz lists (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Triage: the planted commit is unsigned but authored as the token's owner, so the author name alone proves nothing; one new workflow file with a fixed commit message on a branch the owner did not create is the pattern (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Defender takeaway
Rotate every secret available to a repository where a planted branch exists, revoke the tokens that pushed the commits and check their owners' devices for infostealers, treat a self-hosted runner host and its instance role as compromised if a planted branch ran there, and scope OIDC trust to protected branches or environments with required reviewers on environments that hold production secrets (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Builds on: 2026-10-10/ghostaction-fake-audit-workflow-git-history-credential-theft

threat27 Oct 03:54Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Wiz Research · GitHub (changelog)

02Trending vulnerabilities1 item

NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP2Shell in industrial, building and network-access products: Belden NetModule NRSW has no fix and macmon 6.x must move to 7.x, with notices from Schneider Electric, B&R, HMS Networks, Wibu-Systems, Johnson Controls and Oracle

Industrial, building and network-access vendors have published their own notices for the PHP runtime flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which CISA lists as exploited since 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). Belden says all versions of NetModule NRSW, including the latest mainline release 5.0.0.104, are affected and that no patched release exists; until one ships it advises disabling the web interface after confirming SSH access, with the CLI settings http.status=0 and https.status=0 (Belden, 2026-10-22). NetModule AG is headquartered in Bern, Switzerland (Belden, 2022-03-14). Belden's macmon 6.x and 7.x use PHP in the web interface: a patch for 7.x is in the service portal, 6.x must move to 7.x, and the HTTPS web interface and guest portal must not be reachable from the internet unprotected (Belden, 2026-10-22).

Schneider Electric lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize (remediation through ProLeiT support) and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, where its revision of 2026-10-26 gives an automatic update if the hosting virtual machine can reach the debian.org and sury.org repositories and a Schneider patch otherwise (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-26; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26). B&R says APROL up to R 4.4-65 is affected, with patches planned for 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-29 (B&R, 2026-10-23). HMS Networks says Netbiter firmware up to 3.00.10 can be exploited from the LAN or the USB port and that 3.00.11 fixes it (HMS Networks, 2026-10-23). Wibu-Systems lists the web interface of CodeMeter License Central and its extensions, with 5.2.2 released and a patch installer for 5.1.2 and 5.0.x (Wibu-Systems, 2026-10-23). Johnson Controls has released patches for several Illustra product lines and fixed Visonic PowerManage in 5.0.45 (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26). Oracle's Security Alert, revised on 2026-10-26, patches Oracle Secure Backup 19.1.0.0.0 to 19.1.0.1.0, Oracle Solaris 11 and eight Oracle Communications products for CVE-2026-109618 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) and says it will extend the alert as more patches become available (Oracle, 2026-10-26).

Exposure
A NetModule router running NRSW, a macmon server, or any other listed product whose web interface answers from a network that is not a trusted administrative one; the vendors name the web interface as the affected component (Belden, 2026-10-22; HMS Networks, 2026-10-23).
Defender takeaway
Disable the web interface of every NetModule NRSW router now, since no fixed release exists, and keep the web interfaces of the other listed products off untrusted networks until their patches are installed; install the vendor fix wherever one is listed, such as the macmon 7.x patch (Belden, 2026-10-22), Security Expert version 1.48.4.0 (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-26), Netbiter 3.00.11 (HMS Networks, 2026-10-23) and CodeMeter License Central 5.2.2 (Wibu-Systems, 2026-10-23).

Builds on: 2026-10-21/php-critical-release-pre-announced-cve-2026-109618-109619 · 2026-10-22/pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release · 2026-10-23/netscaler-php2shell-management-gui-fixes-2026-10-27 · 2026-10-25/qnap-synology-php2shell-qts-quts-hero-fixed-others-unfixed

vulnerability27 Oct 03:56Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Belden (security advisory PSIRT-10) · Schneider Electric (security bulletin SESB-2026-295-01, version 2.0.0) · B&R (cyber security advisory SA26P015) · HMS Networks (security advisory HMSSAR-2026-10-22-002) · Wibu-Systems (product alert, CodeMeter License Central PHP vulnerabilities) · Oracle (Security Alert Advisory, Rev 2) · SecurityWeek · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · Belden (acquisition of NetModule AG)

03Updates to prior coverage8 items

HIGHCVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Panorama: the PHP2Shell flaws affect every release through the management web interface, and Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces; all twenty hotfixes are out

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update27 Oct 2026 05:15 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstitle

Palo Alto Networks now records eleven PAN-OS hotfixes as released (10.2.13-h27, 10.2.16-h12, 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.4-h38, 11.1.6-h40, 11.1.10-h36, 11.1.13-h16, 11.1.16-h4, 11.2.10-h16, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.2.4-h1) with nine others due by 2026-10-30; CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, while Palo Alto still reports no malicious exploitation against its products.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory now records eleven PAN-OS hotfixes as released: 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.16-h4 and 11.2.10-h16 (revision of 2026-10-25), 11.1.4-h38, 11.1.6-h40, 11.1.10-h36 and 11.1.13-h16 (2026-10-26), and 10.2.13-h27, 10.2.16-h12, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.2.4-h1 (2026-10-27) (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27). Nine hotfixes still carry estimated dates from 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30, among them 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.10-h3 and four 11.2 lines, and the FAQ says 11.2.10-h16 carries only the PHP fix while 11.2.10-h17 carries the PHP and the Brotli fixes (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27). Huntress's analysis of 2026-10-26 reads the activity as scripted tooling steered by an operator, rates LLM involvement low to medium on its own telemetry, adds a detection for service principals that assign themselves or a sibling a directory role, and notes that Graph reads leave no Entra audit record.

Huntress published its analysis of what drove the 2026-10-15 activity on 2026-10-26, working from Entra sign-in and directory audit logs in the tenants it monitors. It says its telemetry aligns with Microsoft's Storm-0940 and ARTEX account without independently confirming it, that it is highly confident an operator, a person or an LLM, adapted the tooling between runs, and that its confidence that an LLM was involved in the escalation tooling is low to medium on its own telemetry and medium to high once Microsoft's attribution is included (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Its evidence for adaptation: a certificate upload that failed on a thumbprint mismatch ended one run with no retry, and the next run 55 seconds later retried the same error with growing waits until it worked; in a second tenant that refused removal of the Global Administrator role, the actor granted a different role to a sibling principal and the original service principal was then deleted (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Microsoft Graph reads are not recorded in the Entra audit log and no victim Huntress knows of had Graph activity logging enabled, so a clean audit log does not show that no Graph access took place (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Huntress recommends alerting when a service principal assigns itself Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator, deletes itself, or when one vendor principal grants a role to a sibling, and turning on Graph activity logs where licensing allows (Huntress, 2026-10-26).

Seoul Metropolitan Police announced on 2026-10-26 that it referred a 32-year-old gang leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23, with six accomplices investigated without detention, for taking 8.2 million personal-data records and internal files from more than 90 organizations since September 2025, among them cram schools, hospitals, golf courses, universities and large-company affiliates, and for sending extortion e-mails (Yonhap, 2026-10-26, translated from Korean). Yonhap counts 60 of the victims as hacked with AI and describes the system as the AI autonomous penetration-testing system used in the recent financial-sector data thefts without naming it, so the ARTEX name is BleepingComputer's (Yonhap, 2026-10-26). No encryption step is reported, and the police say AI lowered the barrier to entry and call this the first arrest in Korea in a large-scale hacking and personal-data theft case that exploited generative AI (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). The framework is therefore in use by a financially motivated criminal group as well as by the state-aligned actor Microsoft describes; no source reports a Swiss victim.

Brotli encoding is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later, the command show system setting brotli shows whether a firewall is exposed (Enabled: yes), and set system setting brotli-encoding disable is the vendor's interim mitigation; Palo Alto rates the urgency moderate and is not aware of malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26).

PHP rebuilt its Windows packages as 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 on 2026-10-26 with Brotli 1.2.1; the vulnerable decoder is reachable there through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled, which cURL leaves off by default (PHP, 2026-10-26). Verification & coverage notes

Window of 26 h (gap 24.0 h) on a Tuesday with one dominant story: CISA's KEV listing of the PHP2Shell flaws on 2026-10-26 and the first documented code execution against honeypots. The container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s); the previous fire (2026-10-26T0256Z-intel, publish ok) was on origin/main. A container restart at about 03:13Z killed the first four research sub-agents before any returned; they were re-spawned once at 03:15Z (their progress and checkpoint files are kept as *.attempt1.* under work/<run-id>/, used as leads only) and all four returned by 03:35Z, so the restart cost about eighteen minutes and no entry depends on the lost work.

  • Published (new, three): the TCS Camping and Camping.Care booking-data theft that SRF and Blick tie to the PHP flaws (notable, PD-11(c): the first Swiss-linked victim report of the exploited PHP flaws, a supplier-borne exposure with a transferable lesson for public bodies whose portals run on PHP suppliers; single-source-victim, TCS's own confirmation, B2); Wiz Research's Gheist campaign, stolen GitHub tokens planting secret-dumping workflows, with GitHub's own changelog confirming that its approval hold covers public repositories on github.com only (notable, PD-11(a) and (d)); and a PHP2Shell vendor-notice entry for industrial, building and network-access products, led by NetModule NRSW (router software of the Bern-headquartered NetModule AG, all versions, no fix, web interface to be disabled) and macmon 6.x/7.x, with Schneider Electric, B&R, HMS, Wibu-Systems, Johnson Controls and Oracle (notable, PD-11(b): no fix and an out-of-band response on an exploit-listed flaw; one entry per estate class as for QNAP and Synology, not one per vendor).
  • Updated (eight changelog records): the main PHP2Shell entry (update: KEV listing and Karimi's honeypot report; the statements that neither flaw is in KEV and that no source ties a confirmed compromise to the flaws were replaced where they stood, the 2026-10-26 section's sentence was narrowed to production systems, the main analysis was held at its previous 1,977 words); PAN-OS (update: nine hotfixes released, one action added); NetScaler (update: KEV listing, no fixed build in Citrix's bulletin); QNAP (update: QVR Surveillance and TVR OS resolved, QuMagie no longer listed); the Brotli entry (update: NCSC.ch advisory 13105, PAN-OS firewalls with Brotli inspection and decryption, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu; one action added); Apple CVE-2026-86950 (update: iOS 18.7.11 fixes iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation); ARTEX (update: Seoul police arrest of a criminal group's leader, BleepingComputer names the framework); ConnectWise Cloud Backup (improvement: Huntress's analysis, detections and the Graph logging gap).
  • KEV sweep: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (COVERED-STALE on four store entries) are dispositioned by the four updates above plus the new vendor-notice entry; no NOT COVERED or MENTION-ONLY row and no RANSOMWARE row (CISA marks ransomware use unknown). The KEV remediation deadline is not carried in any entry.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row stays held, unchanged and unappended: S4 re-checked it and the ransomware.live record still shows no press link, with no ARX, SBB or ASTRA/USTRA statement and no Swiss press report; the 2026-11-07 expiry stands.
  • Single-source: gheist-stolen-github-tokens-secret-dumping-workflows (Wiz telemetry, B2), original lab research; pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release (vendor's own product, A).
  • borderline-drop: PK Softech and Publica, EDÖB head Lobsiger's SonntagsBlick interview relayed by Inside IT and Ticinonline (2026-10-25 and 26) and Publica's re-stated "no darkweb publication", a conditional possible widening of the proceeding, a re-confirmed status and a breach-notification count; the entry already carries the formal investigation (S2 and S4, same drop as the previous fire).
  • borderline-drop: Medienwerkstatt Sulgen TG (Akira claim, victim confirms ransomware and copied data), private print firm, no public-sector customer stated, no vector or behaviour beyond the impact (incident floor), the only link is the actor already in the Publica entry; University of Copenhagen test-environment breach, out of nexus, no vector.
  • borderline-drop: Cisco Talos on attackers using 25+ legitimate platforms to mail the lure under the brand's own DKIM and DMARC (2026-10-21, first coverage from a rotational lookback), drafted as an entry and dropped after the first verifier pass: six-day-old vendor research with a vendor tally and consumer-retail examples, the lesson is a generic gateway-inspection point and a Tier 2/3 responder changes nothing in the next seven days because of it (PD-11, awareness only).
  • borderline-drop: Arctic Wolf Labs on more than 400 Teams external-chat helpdesk-impersonation cases (2026-10-26); the store carries six Teams-vishing entries and three already carry the external-access allow-list lever; the new content is one audit event name (ChatCreated) and a tenant-pattern description.
  • borderline-drop: CYFIRMA's PHP2Shell advisory (Lazarus-ecosystem actor, 216 hosts, closed I2P channel), single vendor, nobody can check the channel, confidence inconsistent between narrative and evaluation, no Swiss nexus (dropped by the previous fire too); Symantec's AI-honeypot "Skynet" capture and Semperis on Prince of Persia (both lookback), relevant only to bodies that expose model endpoints or indicator-led infrastructure tracking with no European case; Forever Security's planted AGENTS.md (2026-10-22), vendor-run reproduction, success rates are the vendor's claims, delivery of the file unknown.
  • out-of-window: CrowdStrike's report on four actors running Claude Code as an intrusion operator (2026-10-23, recovered through a Hacker News recap of 2026-10-26; the crowdstrike record was not in any slice), primary source three days before the window start and not a rotational lookback; offered to the audit.
  • borderline-drop: Risikomonitor's Swiss unpatched-domain figures (Inside IT, 2026-10-26); scope differs from the 2026-10-22 figure so it is not a trend; Fortinet FG-IR-26-186 and -187 revisions, Synology Hyper Backup "not affected", NetScaler Product Security (no new post readable), Tailscale "Tailworm", Wasmtime sandbox escapes, Chromium Mobile rows in MSRC, Sansec Magecart items, Plex and EG SiteGuard KEV additions (2026-10-20, out of window, consumer or Japan-specific), no delta for the reader or out of scope.
  • Contradiction: S1, S2 and S3 each framed the KEV listing and the honeypot report as separate items; they were merged into one update. S2 read CISA's due date of 2026-10-29 as a signal; it is a US federal obligation and is not carried (PD-13). The Phase 4 re-fetch of two pages read with guessed URL slugs returned 404 (corrected to the URLs in the findings; nothing was cited from a guessed URL).
  • Contradiction: the Palo Alto Brotli advisory (CVE-2026-111497) still shows 12.2.4-h1 and 12.1.7-h11 with 10/28 estimated dates while the PHP2Shell advisory, revised at 2026-10-27T04:03Z, lists both as released; the Brotli entry cites the Brotli advisory as stated and the PAN-OS entry the PHP2Shell one.
  • Candidate sources added: belden-psirt (first-party NetModule and macmon advisories, on no slice source) and karimi-honeypot-data (packet-level exploitation ground truth). Not added: arctic-wolf-labs (its item was dropped), forever-security (no feed, vendor interest) and hacksnack-ch (derivative SME news, offered by S2 and S4). Recipe notes from the source ledgers were appended to the matching sources/sources.json records, among them the BACS card-markup change that breaks the documented split, the Fortinet RSS reset, the SSD Disclosure recipe and the Help Net Security extract behaviour.
  • Reader credit: extract fell through to the metered reader for the CISA alert, the QNAP page and the Dark Reading articles; S4 reported two more on tcs.ch and news.ku.dk.
  • Audit hand-offs: the IDC Frontier entry does not cite the provider's sixth report of 2026-10-18; Eichstätt (Germany, municipal ransomware through an unnamed third-party vulnerability despite two-factor authentication, statements of 2026-10-22 and 23) fell about twelve hours outside the lookback and is a municipal lesson; the main PHP2Shell entry's main analysis (1,977 words) and several others touched this fire remain over the 550-word bound as carried debt, none grown by this fire.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, failing on every run since 2026-10-19); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport); community.citrix.com Tech Zone NetScaler post (403 on every transport for S1; a later extract read it, last updated 2026-10-22 and still saying fixes are planned for 2026-10-27, so whether they shipped is unconfirmed); rapid7 and cisa.gov all.xml discovery feeds (unreadable); lumen-black-lotus-labs (landing page without a post listing); php.risikomonitor.com (figures render client-side).
  • Watchlist: products checked=0, hits=0; suppliers checked=0, hits=0
  • Essential-coverage: all 21 essential records of S1 and S2 were attempted; none missed.

item.description:
• JPCERT/CC and NICT: attackers decompile the public app, then call internal APIs; AI platforms scan exposed web apps. JPCERT/CC (alert AT-2026-0030, updated 2026-10-23) and NICT describe a wave of personal-data leaks from Japanese web systems in which attackers analyse the published Android app to find API endpoints and keys and then call internal management APIs the app screens never use, place JSP web shells as .war files on application servers behind the public web server, and, per the latest update, run AI penetration-testing platforms (Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, ARTEX) against internet-facing web applications, WSUS servers included. No actor is named, JPCERT/CC says it confirmed AI used to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs, and Macnica could not confirm AI use. →
  • Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET fixes: hosts updated on 13 October still carry the Windows sockets flaw. Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. Brotli exposure needs an application that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data, which ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not do by default; CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27, although Microsoft's record still said not exploited on 2026-10-25 and no source reports an attack on .NET. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01JPCERT/CC and NICT: attackers decompile the public app, then call internal APIs; AI platforms scan exposed web apps. JPCERT/CC (alert AT-2026-0030, updated 2026-10-23) and NICT describe a wave of personal-data leaks from Japanese web systems in which attackers analyse the published Android app to find API endpoints and keys and then call internal management APIs the app screens never use, place JSP web shells as .war files on application servers behind the public web server, and, per the latest update, run AI penetration-testing platforms (Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, ARTEX) against internet-facing web applications, WSUS servers included. No actor is named, JPCERT/CC says it confirmed AI used to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs, and Macnica could not confirm AI use. →
  2. 02Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET fixes: hosts updated on 13 October still carry the Windows sockets flaw. Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. Brotli exposure needs an application that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data, which ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not do by default; CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27, although Microsoft's record still said not exploited on 2026-10-25 and no source reports an attack on .NET. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 3Action items 7

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLENATOA2

Japan's wave of personal-data theft from web systems: JPCERT/CC and NICT describe attackers who decompile the published Android app to find internal APIs, drop JSP web shells as .war files on application servers, and run AI penetration-testing platforms against exposed web applications and WSUS servers

JPCERT/CC's alert of 2026-10-08, updated on 2026-10-23, says that around September 2026 Japanese organisations disclosed a run of personal-data leaks through unauthorised access, and singles out an attack type that may be increasing: systems the operator never expected strangers to reach, such as business-intelligence tools and staff-management systems, were hit alongside public apps (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23). It does not tie them to one method and groups them in five: per-target scanning for known flaws and exposed configuration and backup files; unauthorised calls to application management APIs; the Metabase SQL injection CVE-2026-72898; .war files carrying a JSP web shell that runs commands passed in query parameters, placed on application servers reachable from the public web server; and, added on 2026-10-23, attempts through AI penetration-testing platforms it names as Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and ARTEX, including against exposed WSUS servers (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

In the API case the attackers analyse the published smartphone app to find endpoints and keys, then attack internal APIs the app screens cannot reach: changing user rights, creating accounts, toggling a header or sending malformed tokens to compare responses, and blind NoSQL injection to find account data; some use API keys stolen elsewhere (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23). NICT calls this an app-to-backend attack: the app need not be vulnerable, and backend authentication, authorisation or input-validation faults leak data (NICT, 2026-10-13). On attack servers JPCERT/CC found Android packages, reverse-engineering tools and a Python script that answers requests with HTTP 302 redirects and appears to have been used to test for server-side request forgery (JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21).

No source names an actor. JPCERT/CC says it confirmed that the attackers used AI to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs (JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21), while Macnica could not confirm AI use (Recorded Future, 2026-10-22). API-attack access also arrives through Tor exit nodes and residential proxies (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Exposure
An organisation that publishes a mobile app with a backend API, runs internet-facing web applications, or leaves BI tools, staff-management systems or WSUS servers reachable from the internet (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23); NICT asks operators to inventory public APIs and servers and check their access logs (NICT, 2026-10-13).
Detection
In API and web access logs, calls to internal or management endpoints from clients that never load the app screens, role-change and account-creation calls outside the admin console, one endpoint called in sequence with and without a header or with malformed tokens, blind NoSQL-injection-style probing of account lookups, and use of API keys extracted from the app; in web server telemetry, scans for exposed configuration and backup files and .war deployments to application servers (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Triage: the app's own User-Agent proves nothing, because JPCERT/CC saw attack requests carrying it; the endpoints called and the sequence (header toggling, malformed tokens, role changes) discriminate, and a TLS fingerprint that matches a generic Python client does not identify the attacker alone (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Defender takeaway
Treat the published app package as public and test the backend for authorisation gaps on internal endpoints (IDOR and BOLA), server-side request forgery, remote code execution and SQL injection (NICT, 2026-10-13). JPCERT/CC's measures are per-endpoint and per-method access control including non-public APIs, expiring least-privilege API tokens with fast revocation, rate limits on login, password reset, SMS and search, no long-lived secrets in apps, and no management functions on the internet (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23; JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21).

Builds on: 2026-08-09/metabase-unauth-sqli-zeroday-exploited-framework-tally · 2026-10-22/artex-storm-0940-agentic-llm-pentest-spraying-oauth-abuse · 2026-09-23/gambit-ai-agent-retail-skimmer-campaign-strix-cairn-hermes
