Sources: JPCERT/CC (alert JPCERT-AT-2026-0030, updated 2026-10-23) · JPCERT/CC Eyes (attack infrastructure investigation) · NICT CYNEX (threat intelligence team LETTICE) · Recorded Future Insikt Group

02Trending vulnerabilities1 item

NOTABLECVE-2026-111497 +3exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-111497 / CVE-2026-70197, Microsoft .NET: an out-of-band release fixes a Brotli decoder flaw and delivers the Windows sockets fix that the 13 October update did not contain, in 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 (CVSS 3.1 8.1)

Microsoft released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8, .NET 9 and .NET 10, with .NET 11 Release Candidate 3, on 2026-10-25 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). .NET Framework is not affected (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-111497 is a buffer overflow in the Brotli decoder that .NET uses and may let an unauthenticated attacker read or corrupt process memory, leading to information disclosure, denial of service or elevation of privilege (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25); Microsoft scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1, marked it publicly disclosed and not exploited on 2026-10-25, and rates it Exploitation More Likely (MSRC, 2026-10-25). Node.js fixed the same CVE on 2026-10-21 (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Microsoft says an application is exposed only if it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic response decompression that includes Brotli, or the BrotliStream and BrotliDecoder APIs, and that ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not decompress Brotli by default (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25).

The release also corrects two fixes of 2026-10-13: Microsoft says that release did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-70197 is a Windows-only out-of-bounds write: reusing one SocketAsyncEventArgs instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can keep an undersized cached native address buffer, and an unauthenticated attacker can then write out of bounds during ReceiveFromAsync (CVSS 3.1 8.1, high attack complexity) (dotnet/runtime #136445, 2026-10-25); the Security Update Guide rates it not exploited, not publicly disclosed and Exploitation Less Likely (MSRC, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-102870 is code execution in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger when a developer evaluates an expression that involves attacker-controlled application data (CVSS 3.1 8.8, user interaction required); it needs the standalone Server and DevServer package references updated, because updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute (dotnet/announcements #492, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-114148 is a local privilege escalation through incorrect file ownership in Linux tarballs (CVSS 3.1 7.8), affecting ASP.NET Core tarballs of .NET 8 and 9 and source-built tarballs of .NET 8 to 11 (dotnet/announcements #495, 2026-10-25). No source reports an attack on .NET, but CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27 (CISA, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A framework-dependent host shows its runtime with dotnet --list-runtimes, which must list 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14; self-contained applications and container images carry their own runtime and must be checked per artifact (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). The Brotli path is any code that enables request or response Brotli decompression or calls the Brotli APIs on untrusted data; CVE-2026-70197 needs Windows code that reuses one SocketAsyncEventArgs across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25; dotnet/runtime #136445, 2026-10-25).
Detection
No source describes an exploitation indicator. The telemetry that would show an attempt on the Brotli path is web access logs with a Brotli request content encoding on endpoints that decompress request bodies, followed by crashes of the hosting process.
Defender takeaway
Install the updated runtime on every .NET host, including Windows hosts patched on 2026-10-13, which still carry CVE-2026-70197 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25), and treat the Brotli flaw as exploited, as CISA lists it (CISA, 2026-10-27). SDKs installed through Visual Studio update when Visual Studio itself is updated (dotnet/runtime #136445, 2026-10-25). Where an update has to wait, Microsoft advises avoiding decompression of attacker-controlled Brotli data: remove the br entry from an existing request decompression configuration or Brotli from an existing automatic decompression setting, and do not add decompression where an application does not already use it (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25).
Update28 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelsummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

CISA added CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli decoder flaw this release fixes for .NET, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation", without describing the evidence (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26 (ELLIO, 2026-10-26); no source reports an attack on .NET, and Microsoft's own record marked the flaw not exploited on 2026-10-25 (MSRC, 2026-10-25).

Builds on: 2026-10-24/cve-2026-111497-node2shell-brotli-decoder-rce-nodejs-pypi

vulnerability26 Oct 03:36Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →

03Updates to prior coverage3 items

HIGHCVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Panorama: the PHP2Shell flaws affect every release through the management web interface, and Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces; all twenty hotfixes are out

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Correction26 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

The entry said Unit 42 had seen a proof of concept of the PHP flaws; Unit 42's brief, revised on 2026-10-25, no longer says so, and the statement is removed.

Unit 42's brief, revised on 2026-10-25, no longer says that it has seen a proof of concept of the PHP flaws (Unit 42, 2026-10-25).

Sources: Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP on Palo Alto Networks Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-23) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-24) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-25) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-27) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, 2026-10-27) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 (threat brief, revised 2026-10-25) · PHP (security advisory) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, Internet Archive copy of 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.27) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-29) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-29) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-30) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-30)
HIGHCVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

First published 2026-10-24 · open finding →

Update26 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidencesourcessummary

Envoy and Microsoft have shipped fixes for the same Brotli decoder flaw: Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 lists v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 for deployments with the Brotli decompressor configured, and Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14) covers applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

Two more vendors have shipped fixes for the same decoder flaw. Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 says a buffer overflow in its Brotli decompressor allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code with a crafted Brotli-compressed stream; it names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable, v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 as fixed, and limits the impact to deployments that have the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23). Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3) fixes the same CVE, and an application is exposed only when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic decompression or the Brotli APIs (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); .NET Blog, 2026-10-25 lists the fixed releases. No source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration against Node.js.

Sources: Node.js project · Node.js project (release v22.23.4) · Node.js project (release v24.22.1) · Node.js project (release v26.12.1) · Google Brotli · ENISA EUVD · Imperva Threat Research · OpenSourceMalware · Envoy Proxy (security advisory) · .NET Blog (Microsoft) · Microsoft (dotnet/announcements, CVE-2026-111497 advisory) · NCSC Switzerland (BACS, Cyber Security Hub advisory 13105) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status) · PHP (news archive, updated Windows builds for the Brotli fix) · Ubuntu Security (CVE-2026-111497) · CISA (alert, KEV additions) · ELLIO Threat Research Lab · Tenable Research · JFrog Security Research · Akamai Security Intelligence Group · Cisco PSIRT (advisory, Vulnerabilities in node.js Affecting Cisco Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, timeline of 2026-10-29) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0008.1)
CRITICALCVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

First published 2026-10-21 · open finding →

Update26 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelbodyevidenceimmediate_actionsourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it cannot confirm that the initial access is associated with them; the summary, the detection guidance and the 2026-10-24 section no longer carry that account. Priority stays critical: the scanning, attack attempts, public proofs of concept and VulnCheck's working exploit do not rest on the retracted report, and no source ties a confirmed compromise to these flaws.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 the update of 2026-10-23 in which it had reported post-exploitation by agentic attack platforms at a European government entity. Its brief now says that what its researchers saw was an attack against a European government agency executed in the context of a vulnerable PHP application, that this led them to believe it was exploitation of these flaws, and that it is unable to confirm that the initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs (Unit 42, 2026-10-25). The observations of the retracted update, including the command-batch markers and the Active Directory activity, are no longer part of the brief. The brief still recommends assessing exposure and patching immediately (Unit 42, 2026-10-25).

What remains documented is scanning and attack attempts, reported by Cloudflare, watchTowr, VulnCheck and others, and VulnCheck's working exploit for specific PHP builds; CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation, and no source tied a named CVE to a production compromise. The Hacker News article of 2026-10-25 relays the retracted account and carries no correction (The Hacker News, 2026-10-25).

04Action items7 items

  • Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • List every appliance and management server whose web interface embeds PHP (firewalls, network access control, wireless controllers, backup, storage and security consoles), take each interface off the internet and install its vendor's PHP2Shell fix, because Dream Research reports one appliance vendor's firewalls rooted through an exposed management interface.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager apply Broadcom's workaround, KB460732 on 9.1.1 and KB460734 on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, until its patch ships.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Install .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (11 Release Candidate 3 for the preview) on every host that runs .NET applications, including Windows hosts already updated on 2026-10-13, which still carry CVE-2026-70197; rebuild and republish self-contained applications and rebuild container images from the updated .NET images, because a runtime update on the host does not change a bundled runtime.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497 +3→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-26T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 2 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Quiet window over Sunday and early Monday (gap 24.0 h, window 26 h starting 2026-10-25T00:56Z). The four sub-agents returned 14 items; two were published as new entries, three existing entries received a changelog record and the rest were dropped or held. The container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s) and the previous fire (2026-10-25T0256Z-intel, publish ok) and the 2026-10-25 audit were both on origin/main.

  • Published (new): the out-of-band .NET security release of 2026-10-25 (the Brotli decoder CVE-2026-111497 plus corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870) at notable, because Microsoft says the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address two of its flaws and hosts patched that day stay exposed (PD-11(b), out-of-band limb); and the JPCERT/CC and NICT account of app-to-backend API attacks, web shells and AI-platform scanning in Japan at notable, first coverage from the jpcert-eyes rotational lookback (PD-7(d)), cleared under PD-11(d) as A-reliability primary technical analysis with behaviours a responder can check in API logs.
  • Updated: php-critical-release-pre-announced-cve-2026-109618-109619 (update: Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws; S1 and S3 both found it, no other lane and no press outlet did). Priority stays critical: the 2026-10-22 record that set critical rested on attack traffic, public proofs of concept and VulnCheck's working exploit, none of which depends on the retracted report. The retracted claim was removed from the summary, immediate action wording, sourcing note, Detection paragraph, the 2026-10-24 section, the evidence quote and the techniques T1003 and T1557, which only that account supported. cve-2026-111497-node2shell-brotli-decoder-rce-nodejs-pypi (update: Envoy's own advisory of 2026-10-23 and the .NET release; Bun and Istio rest on The Hacker News alone and were not carried). pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release (correction: the statement that Unit 42 had seen a proof of concept is no longer on Unit 42's page, so statement, quote and citation were removed; S3 and S1 disagreed on whether this entry needed a change, the page grep settled it).
  • KEV sweep: tools/kev_window_diff.py found 0 additions with dateAdded in the window and no ransomware-flag change on a store-covered CVE; S1 confirmed independently against catalogue 2026.10.23 (newest dateAdded 2026-10-23, CVE-2026-114625 and CVE-2026-110447, both covered). PHP2Shell is not in KEV.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row stays held, unchanged and unappended. S2 and S4 re-checked it today: the ransomware.live record is unchanged since 2026-10-23, there is no ARX, SBB or ASTRA statement and no Swiss press report; the hold condition is unmet and the 2026-11-07 expiry stands.
  • Single-source: cve-2026-111497-microsoft-net-oob-update-brotli-sockets-fix, vendor advisory for its own product (Microsoft's blog, four dotnet advisories and the Security Update Guide are one assessor), A2.
  • borderline-drop: Tailworm (Cyberdione Labs, 11 claimed Tailscale and headscale flaws, 2026-10-25); single uncoordinated report, proof of concept withheld, no independent reproduction, no CVE or fix, constituency use not established.
  • borderline-drop: OpenAI frontier-training containment disclosure (2026-10-25), own-environment account with no defender decision beyond fixes already shipped.
  • borderline-drop: Semperis on Prince of Persia (2026-10-22), single vendor, indicator-led, no European victim, no new endpoint behaviour.
  • borderline-drop: OPNsense PHP2Shell hotfixes 26.7.7, 26.1.11 and 26.4.2p4 (2026-10-21), out of window by five days and not a rotational lookback, no exploitation against OPNsense; the PHP entry already says to update the runtime on every host and image.
  • borderline-drop: CSIRT Italia alert AL01/261025 (2026-10-25), 81.9 % of Italian PHP services potentially vulnerable; a national exposure statistic that ACN says can include backported fixes; no new action.
  • borderline-drop: EDÖB head Lobsiger interview in the Blick (2026-10-24), possible widening of the PK Softech proceeding to the federal bodies; the Publica entry already carries the 2026-10-22 formal investigation and the widening is conditional.
  • borderline-drop: CYFIRMA PHP2Shell early warning v3 (24 October), single vendor, closed I2P channel nobody else can check, confidence inconsistent between narrative and evaluation, names the EU but not Switzerland.
  • borderline-drop: Chrome 156 stable (2026-10-20), about 6 h outside the record's lookback, no exploited flag, no store coverage.
  • borderline-drop: Drupal SA-CONTRIB-2026-253 (Monster Menus), needs an authenticated role, exploit maturity theoretical; PaperCut September bulletin additions, administrator-only; Atlassian October third-party bulletin, Atlassian rates the criticals lower risk.
  • borderline-drop: Medienwerkstatt Sulgen TG (Akira claim, 2026-10-23), private sector, out of window; ECOM and White & Case Qilin listings (2026-10-25), leak-site claims without a victim statement (PD-6), no public-sector nexus.
  • borderline-drop: French party and company leak wave of 23 to 25 October (PCF, La France insoumise, Renaissance, FSU, Alliance Police Nationale, Orange, Engie, ADMR, DEKRA), no shared vector or actor named, no Swiss nexus.
  • borderline-drop: ABC wipes devices after AdFection ad exposure (2026-10-23) (victim-side corroboration of a covered entry, no new behaviour; Quest Diagnostics, Capcom, Railway, Parkview, Yamato, Bathurst RSL and the Oberspreewald-Lausitz district administration) out of nexus, out of window or impact-only.
  • Candidate sources added: dotnet-blog (first-party .NET servicing channel; surfaced the out-of-band release that no slice source did), nict-cynex-lettice (named the app-to-backend attack, cited by JPCERT/CC) and datadog-security-labs (dated RSS, primary cloud-identity and supply-chain research); the S3 candidates macnica-security-research and S4's cyfirma-research were not added (Macnica is context for an entry that did not cite it; CYFIRMA's item was dropped). Twenty-one recipe notes from the source ledgers were appended to sources/sources.json. The transluce record is a single report, not a feed, and is a candidate for the next lifecycle review.
  • Jina reader credit: extract fell through to the reader on the two MSRC per-CVE pages in this run and, in S2, on three European Commission and Council of Europe pages.
  • Contradiction: S1 and S3 reported the PHP2Shell retraction as a correction; it was recorded as an update because it is an exploitation-status change in the world (Unit 42 withdrew its own claim on 2026-10-25), not an error in the entry as written.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, seventh consecutive failing run; status page read instead); ox-security (article bodies 403, feed only); schneier (feed 403); digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu (403 on every transport, not in slice); arx-group.ch and arxgroup.ch (no readable victim site); community.citrix.com Tech Zone NetScaler post (403, its 2026-10-27 fixed builds are not out yet); news.admin.ch /de/nsb (403).
  • Verification: three iterations of the single cti-verification definition, each covering every claim in scope (152, 152 and 151 claims checked). Iteration 1 found two truth findings (the retraction worded as an intrusion withdrawal; an unsupported "independently" about NICT), one missing citation, one Visual Studio gap and a priority question on the PHP entry; iteration 2 found four low-confidence wording findings; iteration 3 found two low-confidence unsupported-citation findings. All truth and editorial findings were fixed in the same iteration's remediation; the PHP priority challenge (F16) was declined with a recorded rebuttal and the verifier accepted it as a judgement call in iteration 2. The first spawn of iteration 3 was lost to a container restart at about 04:30Z (the working tree survived) and the iteration was re-spawned clean. The final verdict is NEEDS_FIXES with two truth findings, both fixed afterwards, so the fire published on the low-residual early exit (decision rule 5) and no confirmation pass followed; verification_residual_count is 2, the two F3 findings applied after the last pass and not re-checked by a fresh verifier. The next audit should give the PHP, Japan and .NET entries an independent pass.
  • Essential-coverage: all 21 essential records of S1 and S2 were attempted; none missed.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-25
item.description:
• PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR, TVR OS and Notes Station 3 fixed, QNE still unfixed. QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-28 (revision V1.2) the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS 1.0.5 and Notes Station 3 3.9.15 as resolved; QNE (ADRA) has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, with no fixed version and QNAP says to keep devices off the internet; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar. →
  • Public root exploit for a Linux page-cache write past the Dirty Frag fix; AlmaLinux kernels carry the fix, no CVE yet. Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. A reviewed patch is in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, AlmaLinux announced on 2026-10-28 that fixed kernels are in production for 8, 9 and 10, none of the six reports has a CVE, and two ksmbd reports that ZDI scores CVSS 9.0 matter only where the in-kernel SMB server runs; no exploitation in the wild is reported. →
  • Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key. SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR, TVR OS and Notes Station 3 fixed, QNE still unfixed. QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-28 (revision V1.2) the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS 1.0.5 and Notes Station 3 3.9.15 as resolved; QNE (ADRA) has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, with no fixed version and QNAP says to keep devices off the internet; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar. →
  2. 02Public root exploit for a Linux page-cache write past the Dirty Frag fix; AlmaLinux kernels carry the fix, no CVE yet. Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. A reviewed patch is in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, AlmaLinux announced on 2026-10-28 that fixed kernels are in production for 8, 9 and 10, none of the six reports has a CVE, and two ksmbd reports that ZDI scores CVSS 9.0 matter only where the in-kernel SMB server runs; no exploitation in the wild is reported. →
  3. 03Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key. SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks. →
Trending vulnerabilities 2Research, reports & policy 1Updates to prior coverage 14Action items 9

01Trending vulnerabilities2 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, QNAP QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the NAS web components before authentication; fixed builds of 2026-10-23, QVR Surveillance, TVR OS and Notes Station 3 now fixed, QNE (ADRA) still unfixed

QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP used in the web components of its operating systems and several of its applications, can be triggered before any application-level authentication, and could let an unauthenticated remote attacker execute code on the device (QNAP, 2026-10-24). Its revision of 2026-10-24 lists fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 for QTS (6.1.0.3656 and 5.2.11.3661), QuTS hero (h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656, which also covers h5.3.x, and h5.2.11.3661) and QuTScloud (c5.2.9.3661), while revision V1.2 of 2026-10-28 lists Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier as resolved by 3.9.15 and the table lists QVR Surveillance 3.0.3 and earlier on ARM32 models as resolved by 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.4 and earlier as resolved by 1.0.5 (QNAP, 2026-10-28). QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, and its fixed version is still to be announced (QNAP, 2026-10-22). QNAP's PSIRT says it has observed scanning and exploitation attempts against the flaws in the wild and blocked attempts against its own website, online store and cloud services (QNAP, 2026-10-22), and its advisory says it has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products (QNAP, 2026-10-24). PHP inside Container Station containers or third-party applications is not covered by QNAP's updates (QNAP, 2026-10-24).

Synology's advisory Synology-SA-26:14 rates its PHP 7.3 to 8.4 packages, Mail Station and Synology Calendar critical and lists fixed releases for each except the end-of-life PHP 7.3 package, which gets no fix; Synology says the PHP built into DSM is not exposed to external attack surfaces and considers the risk of exploitation very low (Synology, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
A QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud below the fixed builds, or a QNAP device running QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) below 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS below 1.0.5, Notes Station 3 below 3.9.15 or QNE (ADRA), whose management or web ports are reachable from outside, which QNAP ties to router port forwarding, UPnP and myQNAPcloud publishing; the management ports default to 8080 and 443 (QNAP, 2026-10-24). On Synology, a DSM with one of the listed PHP packages, Mail Station or Calendar installed (Synology, 2026-10-22).
Detection
QNAP's compromise check is a review of QuLog Center for unexpected logins or access and a Security Center and Malware Remover scan with current definitions; if compromise is suspected it says to disconnect the device and change all passwords (QNAP, 2026-10-24).
Defender takeaway
Update QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud, Notes Station 3, QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) and TVR OS now; for QNE (ADRA), which has no fix, remove internet exposure (port forwarding, UPnP, myQNAPcloud publishing), use a VPN for remote access and allow the management ports only from trusted subnets, which QNAP says reduces exposure without fixing the flaws and does not protect against local devices that are already compromised (QNAP, 2026-10-24). On Synology, update the listed packages; the PHP 7.3 package gets no fix (Synology, 2026-10-22).
Update27 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstitleaffected_productsentities

As of 2026-10-27 QNAP's advisory table lists QVR Surveillance 3.0.3 and earlier (ARM32 models) as resolved by QVR Surveillance 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.4 and earlier as resolved by TVR OS 1.0.5, while Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier and QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier remain in "Fixing" with the fixed version to be announced; QuMagie is no longer among the listed affected products, and the revision history still ends at V1.1 of 2026-10-24, so these table changes carry no dated revision (QNAP, 2026-10-27). QNAP still says it has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products (QNAP, 2026-10-27). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, as flaws in PHP rather than as a QNAP finding (CISA KEV, 2026-10-26).

Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-18 to V1.2 on 2026-10-28 ("Notes Station 3 Resolved Published"), and its table now lists Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier as resolved by Notes Station 3 3.9.15 (QNAP, 2026-10-28). QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier is no longer in that table: it has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, released on 2026-10-22, whose status is Fixing and whose fixed version is still to be announced (QNAP, 2026-10-22). Both advisories still say QNAP has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products, and QSA-26-19 repeats that until fixed versions are available the most effective protection is to keep the device off the internet (QNAP, 2026-10-22).

Sources: QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.1) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, affected-products table as of 2026-10-27) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.2) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-19, QNE (ADRA)) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · QNAP (statement on PHP2Shell) · Synology PSIRT (Synology-SA-26:14)
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Linux kernel ZDI-CAN-33367: a public local root exploit for an skb_zerocopy page-cache write that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with no CVE and no mainline fix, among six reports Trend Micro's ZDI copied to public lists, two of them ksmbd flaws scored CVSS 9.0

On 2026-10-21 Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative sent five Linux kernel reports and copied public mailing lists on every one, several with no fix in any released kernel; none of the six reports, the five kernel ones and a ConnMan report, has a CVE (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). ZDI-CAN-33367 matters most: skb_zerocopy() moves shared page-cache pages into a new socket buffer without the marker the Dirty Frag fix added, so IPsec ESP decrypts in place and an unprivileged local user writes attacker bytes into the cached copy of a read-only file, which gives root through a setuid binary or /etc/passwd; the public exploit needs unprivileged user namespaces and networking modules such as nlmon and act_pedit (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). TuxCare reproduced a root shell on AlmaLinux 8 to 10 (Dirty Frag fix installed), CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (AppArmor user-namespace restriction bypassed) (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). A reviewed patch from the netdev list is now in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, and a kernel with only the fix for CVE-2026-90049, a bug in the same function, is not covered (Sysdig, 2026-10-24; TuxCare, 2026-10-27). AlmaLinux has put fixed kernels into production (4.18.0-553.178.1.el8_10, 5.14.0-687.60.1.el9_8, 6.12.0-211.69.1.el10_2), and TuxCare's rebootless patch is out for EL9 and EL10, with EL8 ready and Debian and Ubuntu in progress (AlmaLinux, 2026-10-28; TuxCare, 2026-10-27).

Two reports concern ksmbd, the kernel's own SMB server, not Samba. ZDI-CAN-33774 is a pre-authentication race in the SMB1 or SMB2 handler choice: its public proof of concept leaks 28 bytes of kernel heap per attempt and can crash the kernel, ZDI labels it remote code execution, nothing public shows code execution, and a fix is queued in ksmbd-for-next (Sysdig, 2026-10-24; Phoronix, 2026-10-22). ZDI-CAN-33549 is an SMB Direct integer underflow that needs an RDMA interface, a writable share and an SMB Direct client, and its proof of concept crashes the kernel (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). ZDI scores both 9.0, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux does not include ksmbd by default (The Hacker News, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
A Linux host where a local user or workload can run code and unprivileged user namespaces are on (shared hosting, CI runners, container nodes, login nodes) on the distributions above. For ksmbd, look for the ksmbd module, the ksmbd.mountd daemon and a kernel-owned listener on TCP 445 (Sysdig, 2026-10-24).
Detection
The exploit is one unprivileged process that unshares into new user and network namespaces and writes sysctls, brings up an nlmon interface, installs XFRM state over netlink, adds an nftables NFQUEUE rule, attaches a tc pedit action with a redirect and then calls splice() into a socket on the loopback address; Sysdig says nothing legitimate does all of that from one unprivileged process, so syscall-level runtime telemetry sees it (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). The write lands in the page cache, not the file, so a disk-content integrity check does not show it.
Defender takeaway
Restrict unprivileged user namespaces where nothing depends on them (Sysdig says user.max_user_namespaces=0 should block the public exploit, untested by TuxCare, and breaks rootless containers and some build tooling), do not rely on Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction, set seccomp RuntimeDefault on Kubernetes pods and install the fixed kernel where your distribution has shipped it; unload ksmbd where unused and keep TCP 445 to trusted networks where it must stay (Sysdig, 2026-10-24).

NOTABLENATOB2

NTLM relay past required signing: SpecterOps and Blackfield re-authenticate a signed LDAP or SMB session with a relayed victim identity, and Microsoft fixed it in the September and October 2026 updates

SpecterOps and Blackfield show that NTLM relay to a server that requires signing works again when the attacker first owns a signed session and then re-authenticates it with the victim's identity, so the session keeps the attacker's signing key. For LDAP, the attacker signs a session to a domain controller with valid credentials or, where accepted, an anonymous NTLM context, coerces a victim over SMB, and sends the victim's relayed authentication with a malicious LDAP modification in one SASL record signed with the attacker's key; the controller checks the signature once, switches to the victim's identity and runs the modification with the victim's rights (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). The tested controller enforced LDAP signing and channel binding and the attack still worked over 389/TCP; the demonstration writes the resource-based constrained delegation attribute, and relaying a domain controller's machine account to another controller leads to DCSync and domain compromise (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). Blackfield shows the SMB counterpart: a server keeps the original signing key on re-authentication without checking that the identity matches, so on any host that requires SMB signing, domain controllers included, a relayed privileged authentication yields a privileged session still signed with the low-privilege key, provided the attacker can capture or coerce that authentication (Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

SpecterOps reported the LDAP flaw to Microsoft on 2026-10-06, received no response, and says the fix shipped in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update, KB5126646, while the SMB variant was patched quietly in September 2026 (KB5122882) (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). KB5126646 is the October update for Windows Server 2025 and KB5122882 the September update for Windows Server 2022 (Microsoft, 2026-10-13; Microsoft, 2026-09-08), so each release needs its own cumulative update of the month. Blackfield found no CVE or KB note for the SMB change, says similar changes seem to have reached the other supported versions in the following weeks without having traced every build, and warns that one or two end-of-life versions may never receive it (Blackfield, 2026-10-21). Both publish tooling; neither reports use in attacks (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23; Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Windows Server domain controllers and SMB servers without the September 2026 (SMB) or 2026-10-13 (LDAP) cumulative update of their release; SpecterOps tested Server 2016 domain controllers and above and says every Server 2022 and 2025 domain controller it tested accepted the relay with LDAP signing required (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). The LDAP variant needs a signed session the attacker controls, a victim coerced to authenticate over SMB and LDAP reachable on 389/TCP (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23).
Detection
Neither researcher publishes detection guidance. The demonstration ends in an LDAP modification of msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on the victim's own computer object, and msDS-KeyCredentialLink (shadow credentials) is the other write (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23), so directory-service change auditing on computer objects for those two attributes is where it surfaces, attributed to the victim's own computer account while the connection comes from the attacker's host. Patching does not remove values a relay already wrote.
Defender takeaway
Confirm that every domain controller runs the 2026-10-13 cumulative update of its Windows release and every Windows server the September one, because required signing did not stop this relay before them. SpecterOps also advises enforcing LDAP signing and channel binding together, restricting LDAP on 389/TCP where possible and reducing NTLM; Blackfield says SMB signing stays necessary but is not sufficient (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23; Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

Der Bund relays the step and adds that besides Publica the pension funds of Migros, Post and the City of Zurich obtain software from PK Softech (Der Bund, 2026-10-23). ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

ANSSI's director general, Vincent Strubel, told the French Senate foreign-affairs committee on 2026-10-21 that the attack rested on elementary security flaws, starting with refrigeration equipment directly on the internet and administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, and he dismissed analyses that tied it to vulnerabilities researchers had published over the previous two years (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21). Le Monde Informatique reports the same hearing and adds that the systems were reachable without a firewall or network segmentation and that the management interface was protected only by weak passwords (Le Monde Informatique, 2026-10-22). Neither outlet reports evidence beyond the testimony, and ANSSI names no actor; the account sits against Copeland's acknowledgment of a vulnerability in its end-of-life XWEB EVO controllers and the earlier report that ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in a Danish company's software, and no source reconciles them; the two outlets also differ on the date and the count, Public Sénat giving the night of 12 to 13 October and more than 700 supermarkets, Le Monde Informatique the night of 11 to 12 October and at least 300 Intermarché and Netto shops. Le Monde Informatique adds that ANSSI can alert and advise but has no means to impose connection rules on retailers (Le Monde Informatique, 2026-10-22), and Public Sénat reports that ANSSI ran a rapid check with health-sector players because laboratories and pharmacies that store vaccines use the same kind of refrigeration equipment (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21).

Forescout's Vedere Labs says on 2026-10-22 that the access vector, exploited vulnerabilities, attacker infrastructure, persistence and responsible actors in the French incidents remain unconfirmed, and that the reported changes, made in rapid succession, used ordinary supervisory functions (Forescout, 2026-10-22). Its tracking of hacktivist groups counts over 20 claimed attacks on refrigeration systems since January 2026, the most active being the pro-Russian groups Z-Pentest Alliance and NoName057(16) through internet-exposed human-machine interfaces, and its count of exposed services is 12,976 observations on 6,017 public addresses in 99 countries, with 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1 (Forescout, 2026-10-22). Forescout adds that the manufacturers' documentation presents internet remote maintenance through port forwarding as a supported option, so the exposure is not only an accident of configuration (Forescout, 2026-10-22).

The same page now says Debian, Devuan and Ubuntu OpenJDK packages need the keystore recreated by hand, because updating ca-certificates and ca-certificates-java does not refresh it, which replaces the earlier statement that updating the operating system's certificates suffices there (OpenJDK, 2026-10-24).

The Python Software Foundation announced CVE-2026-115557 on 2026-10-24: the ssl module now carries a denylist of known compromised certificates that is rejected whatever the SSLContext policy, so it works without revocation checking (Python Software Foundation, 2026-10-24). ENISA's record scores it 9.4 (CVSS 4.0) and lists CPython before 3.16.0 as affected, and the announcement names no release that carries the denylist (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-24). Cisco's informational advisory, version 1.1 of 2026-10-24, lists as impacted with remediation a TLS policy that blocks the known eMudhra issuers on Secure Firewall Management Center, Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1, ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2, 2026-10-23), Meraki MV Smart Camera Firmware (2026-11-18), IOS XR 26.4.1 (2026-11-30) and Ultra Cloud Core Subscriber Microservices Infrastructure 2026.04.1 (November 2026), keeps further products under investigation, and says Cisco PSIRT is not aware of malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-24).

eMudhra's board decided on 2026-10-22 to leave the global SSL/TLS certificate business, and its G1 RSA roots keep serving customers during the transition (eMudhra, 2026-10-22). The Hacker News relays Chrome's count of about 30,800 unexpired certificates under the emSign ECC Root CA - G3, which Chrome stops trusting on 2026-10-27, as of 2026-10-21, 99.9 percent of them issued through InCommon, and relays Chrome's point that standard ACME clients do not replace a certificate outside its renewal window unless they support ACME Renewal Information or someone steps in by hand (The Hacker News, 2026-10-22).

Single-source items and carve-outs: the Danfoss update's ANSSI account is testimony reported by two outlets (Public Sénat and Le Monde Informatique), no transcript was reachable, and the entry says so; the PHP update's Tenable and Siemens statements are first-party vendor advisories for their own products; the EDÖB's account of its proceeding is its own release, relayed by Der Bund; ReliaQuest's sequence is one vendor's lab result and is reported as such. No contradiction between sources needed a verification: contradicted entry.

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport including WebFetch, sixth consecutive failing run counting from 2026-10-20; the status page is the working route), apa-ots (Angular shell, no recipe), resecurity (JS shell), lore.kernel.org (proof-of-work challenge on every message page, so the ZDI postings were read through Sysdig, TuxCare, The Hacker News and Phoronix), consilium.europa.eu (403 everywhere, sanctions watch rested on WebSearch), rapid7-research feed (malformed XML, per-post extract works), edoeb-ch-press listing (stale cache, the release page reads), ahnlab-asec (listing via the reader is stale, WebFetch lists it), schneier (reader fallback only, two keys answered HTTP 402 before a third served). S2 and S3 each reached the metered reader through extract fallbacks on pages the direct transports could not read.

Candidate sources: two added (openjdk-vulnerability-advisories, the first-party advisory of record that published the second Java alert before any outlet; blackfield-ch, the Swiss researcher blog behind the independent SMB finding). Proposed and not added: csa-sg-alerts (a relay of vendor facts that surfaced items already dispositioned), publicsenat-fr (carried the ANSSI testimony; a general political outlet, revisit if it surfaces a second primary), pwn-watch (discovery lead only), status-connectwise (a per-incident pivot, not a rotation source). imperva-threat-research and opensourcemalware were promoted to active from sources.promotion_due. trendmicro-research got its feed back as rss_url and fetch_method: rss; 24 recipe notes from the sub-agent ledgers were appended.

Source health: tools/source_health.py probed 266 records; the first sweep flagged one, the new candidate blackfield-ch (its feed carries a single short item, below the content check's minimum, so the record was switched to the bridge method with the listing as the probed route), and the second sweep ended with no unsolved record.

Self-identification: this fire's main agent is Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) per the harness model line; the four research sub-agents reported Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) in their own return headers.

Audit note: the PK Softech and Publica entry now carries twelve changelog records and is the longest entry in the store; the previous fire's verifier already suggested consolidating its per-fund statements and splitting its first action, which stays audit work.

Verification loop: seven iterations of the single cti-verification definition, each a cold spawn that answered a claim ledger. Iteration 1 (226 claims) found 7 truth and 6 editorial defects and iteration 2 (159) found 3 and 4; iterations 3 to 6 (58 to 160 claims, post-fix scope) found 1, 1, 3 and 5 truth defects, mostly in the run record's own notes, and no iteration returned CLEAN. Every finding was fixed in the entries or the run record before the next pass. Iteration 7 (128 claims, 126 ok) found one low-confidence F3 (the Danfoss Forescout figure's denominator), fixed with the denominator named; with truth plus editorial at 1 and no F1 or F4, the fire takes the low-residual early exit (verification_residual_count: 1). The carried-forward F11 note on the summary length of the PK Softech, Danfoss and PHP2Shell entries was declined in every pass and stays audit work.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-24
item.description: • Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now. CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available. →
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now. CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available. →
Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 10

01Trending vulnerabilities1 item

HIGHCVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Node.js shipped security releases on 2026-10-21 for CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder it bundles: an invalid block switch was reported as a need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input to an eight-byte internal buffer (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory or remote code execution (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Imperva ran code carried in Brotli data against the official 24.22.0 image in its laboratory, through fetch() and through Express 5 and body-parser 2 request parsers, and the fixed 24.22.1 rejected the same input (Imperva, 2026-10-22).

CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation", naming no actor or victim (CISA, 2026-10-27). The only first-hand attack telemetry found is ELLIO's: on 2026-10-26 its sensors recorded one Brotli-coded request body of about 23 MB built against Node.js 24.22.0 on x86-64, although the chain got no shell against ELLIO's own copy of that build (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Tenable relays the report without confirming it, and Cisco and Palo Alto say they know of no malicious use against their own products (Tenable, 2026-10-26; Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

Fixes are in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; end-of-life lines are always affected, and because Node.js cherry-picked the fix without bumping the bundled version string, process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched and vulnerable builds alike (Node.js project, 2026-10-21; ELLIO, 2026-10-26). The decoder is Google's, so Bun (fixed in 1.4.4), Istio, the PyPI packages Brotli (fixed in 1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy and Microsoft .NET carry the flaw too (ELLIO, 2026-10-26; Tenable, 2026-10-26; OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23; Envoy, 2026-10-23; .NET Blog, 2026-10-25).

Exposure
A service on Node.js 22.x, 24.x or 26.x below the fixed releases that decodes Brotli from an untrusted party, either request bodies inflated by Express 5 or body-parser 2 or compressed responses that fetch() consumes from a server an attacker influences (Imperva, 2026-10-22); Python code that decompresses untrusted data with the PyPI packages (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23); Envoy with the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23); .NET applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager, critical on 9.1.1 with no patch yet (Broadcom, 2026-10-28); and PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).
Detection
In web server, proxy and WAF logs, requests that carry a Brotli content encoding to endpoints that parse bodies, followed by worker crashes or restarts; in ELLIO's lab most of 400 attempts against Express crashed the worker instead of returning a shell, and a patched build answers at once with HTTP 400 and ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Where systemd-coredump is enabled, each forced crash writes a core file that can hold other visitors' session cookies, tokens and key material, so restrict who can read it (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).
Defender takeaway
Replace the runtime, the two Python packages and any Envoy with the decompressor configured now, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited; where an update has to wait, reject Content-Encoding: br as NCSC Switzerland advises (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26) and, if the application accepts no compressed request bodies, set the body-parser inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26).
Update26 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidencesourcessummary

Two more vendors have shipped fixes for the same decoder flaw. Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 says a buffer overflow in its Brotli decompressor allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code with a crafted Brotli-compressed stream; it names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable, v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 as fixed, and limits the impact to deployments that have the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23). Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3) fixes the same CVE, and an application is exposed only when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic decompression or the Brotli APIs (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); .NET Blog, 2026-10-25 lists the fixed releases. No source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration against Node.js.

Update27 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytags

NCSC Switzerland (BACS) published advisory 13105 on 2026-10-26 on the Brotli decoder flaw: it names Node.js, Microsoft .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages and Bun among the affected dependents, rates the current exploitation status unknown with a proof of concept available, and gives as the temporary measure disabling Brotli decoding of untrusted data and rejecting Content-Encoding: br until patched, with services restarted and containers rebuilt after updating (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26).

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2 before 12.2.4-h1, 12.1 before 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.1.10-h3, and 11.2 before 11.2.4-h23, 11.2.7-h23, 11.2.10-h17, 11.2.13-h4 and 11.2.16-h1 as affected, but only on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have inspection of Brotli-compressed traffic and TLS decryption enabled on the dataplane; PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 and the management interface are not affected, and the hotfixes carry estimated dates from 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26). Brotli encoding is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later, the command show system setting brotli shows whether a firewall is exposed (Enabled: yes), and set system setting brotli-encoding disable is the vendor's interim mitigation; Palo Alto rates the urgency moderate and is not aware of malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26).

PHP rebuilt its Windows packages as 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 on 2026-10-26 with Brotli 1.2.1; the vulnerable decoder is reachable there through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled, which cURL leaves off by default (PHP, 2026-10-26). Ubuntu lists brotli fixes for 26.10 (1.2.0-4ubuntu0.1), 26.04 LTS (1.2.0-3ubuntu0.1), 24.04 LTS (1.1.0-2ubuntu0.1) and 22.04 LTS (1.0.9-2ubuntu0.1), marks 20.04 LTS as needing evaluation and its nodejs package on 20.04, which vendors Brotli, as vulnerable (Ubuntu, 2026-10-26).

Update28 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryprioritytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyaffected_productsentities

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation", naming no actor or victim (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded a public checker that maps hosts decompressing Brotli and then, on 2026-10-26, one Brotli-coded request body of about 23 MB built against Node.js 24.22.0 on x86-64, which ELLIO reads as adoption by an operator focused on mass exploitation; its own test of the attacker's chain against that build got no shell in 50 attempts, so a failed attempt shows as a worker crash (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Tenable relays the report and has not confirmed it (Tenable, 2026-10-26); Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their own products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of the nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and the other three, 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.10-h3 and 11.2.4-h23, due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

JFrog reproduced a remote crash of a ClickHouse server with one request carrying a crafted 23 MB body, with the fix merged but not released when it wrote (JFrog, 2026-10-25). Akamai gives a lever for Express 5 and body-parser 2 services that accept no compressed request bodies: set the inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26). A Node.js build is judged by its release version, because the bundled version string reads 1.2.0 on patched builds as well (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).

Update29 Oct 2026 07:03 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_atentitiesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008, issued on 2026-10-27 and revised as 0008.1 on 2026-10-28 to clarify the impacted products, lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected because it uses Node.js: a malicious actor with network access to SDDC Manager may exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code (Broadcom, 2026-10-28). Broadcom rates it critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, on SDDC Manager 9.1.1 only and important, 7.5, on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, none has a patch yet, and workarounds are in KB460732 for 9.1.1 and KB460734 for the others (Broadcom, 2026-10-28).

Palo Alto Networks' timeline of 2026-10-29 removes the estimated dates of 11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3 because those builds are released, so every PAN-OS hotfix listed for this flaw is now available (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

vulnerability24 Oct 03:33Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Node.js project · Node.js project (release v22.23.4) · Node.js project (release v24.22.1) · Node.js project (release v26.12.1) · Google Brotli · ENISA EUVD · Imperva Threat Research · OpenSourceMalware · Envoy Proxy (security advisory) · .NET Blog (Microsoft) · Microsoft (dotnet/announcements, CVE-2026-111497 advisory) · NCSC Switzerland (BACS, Cyber Security Hub advisory 13105) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status) · PHP (news archive, updated Windows builds for the Brotli fix) · Ubuntu Security (CVE-2026-111497) · CISA (alert, KEV additions) · ELLIO Threat Research Lab · Tenable Research · JFrog Security Research · Akamai Security Intelligence Group · Cisco PSIRT (advisory, Vulnerabilities in node.js Affecting Cisco Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, timeline of 2026-10-29) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0008.1)

02Updates to prior coverage9 items

NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Wiz Research independently reports an ARTEX-using actor overlapping with Storm-0940 against software vendors in October, and adds log signatures that mark the agent: source-map-then-route sequences, unsigned-JWT SSO probes and one-second-cadence spray bursts with a user agent per burst.

Wiz Research reports an actor using ARTEX-associated tooling, overlapping with Storm-0940, against IT and software vendors throughout October 2026, focused on Okta, Entra and Cognito and on Microsoft 365 integrations, with most attempts failing (Wiz, 2026-10-22). It describes the log signatures of the agent: source-map and OpenAPI downloads followed minutes later by calls to internal routes that appear only in those files, fabricated OAuth callback values, unsigned JWTs tried against more than 60 SSO route variants in two minutes, account-recovery and sign-up calls, and password-spray bursts of 20 to 60 minutes against Entra and Okta with a unique user agent per burst and a median gap of one second between attempts (Wiz, 2026-10-22). Wiz says chaining, automatic adaptation to rate limits and blocks, and tests against heavily scrutinised Microsoft OAuth flows separate the agent from a human operator (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Sources: Microsoft Threat Intelligence · Expel · CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations · Recorded Future Insikt Group · Wiz Research · BleepingComputer · Yonhap News Agency
HIGHCVE-2026-73570exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-73570, Zimbra Collaboration: a pre-auth command injection patched without a CVE in July is exploited, with probing before disclosure and root escalation, secret theft and cluster-wide movement observed

First published 2026-08-20 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:44 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the exploit chain in its lab and describes it stage by stage: an SMTP client sends a recipient address with an unclosed angle bracket, Postfix logs it to /var/log/zimbra.log as an illegal-address warning, Zimbra's bundled Swatchdog daemon matches a log line of the form "Service status change: <host> <service> changed from stopped to running", and the notification routine places the service field into a Perl backtick string that /bin/sh runs, giving code execution as the zimbra user, who can read every mailbox and send as any local identity (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Its practical finding is that several public proofs of concept write a payload that Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server; Elastic's own proof of concept proves execution with an out-of-band callback that changes nothing on disk, and it says upgrading to 10.1.20 or later is the only complete fix (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Its detection is a process sequence on one host within 30 seconds, a shell started by the Perl Swatchdog script with snmptrap in its command line followed by any child of that shell other than snmptrap; on a healthy host the notification shell starts only snmptrap, so any other child is the discriminator (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Where exploitation is found, Elastic lists standard indicators of remote code execution, phishing mail originating from the server, compromise of local databases, signing keys and LDAP exports, and less direct surfaces beyond the mail store (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Sources: Zimbra (vendor security advisories) · CERT-FR (ANSSI) · ENISA EU Vulnerability Database · The Hacker News · Microsoft Threat Intelligence · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog · Zimbra (10.1.20 release notes) · Zimbra (10.1.21 release notes) · NCSC Switzerland, Cyber Security Hub · ACN / CSIRT Italia (bulletin BL01/261005/CSIRT-ITA) · Elastic Security Labs
NOTABLECVE-2026-107656 +1updatedNATOA2

Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

First published 2026-10-23 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytags

Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20; the fix and the unexploited status are unchanged.

A public proof of concept exists for the FortiSIEM 7.5.0 flaw: Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and the exploit for CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20 (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20; The Hacker News, 2026-10-20). The fixed build, 7.5.1, and the port restriction are unchanged, and Fortinet's advisory still says the flaw is not known to be exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

Sources: Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-26-185) · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-26-180) · Help Net Security · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-26-141) · Horizon3.ai (CVE-2026-106173 deep dive) · The Hacker News
NOTABLECVE-2026-110264updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-110264, GitLab CE/EE: an unauthenticated code-execution flaw in the Org-mode renderer's regular-expression handling, fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 and backported to four older lines (CVSS 10.0)

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummaryentities

Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 on 2026-10-23 with fixes for the regular-expression engine bugs behind four GitLab flaws, this one included; any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to them, and Ruby has requested no CVE identifiers of its own.

The Ruby project published an advisory on 2026-10-23 and released Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 with fixes for the bugs in its Onigmo regular-expression engine behind four GitLab flaws: CVE-2026-89078 (a double free when parsing a pattern fails after an alternation), CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-97229 (an integer overflow in the size of a compiled pattern) and CVE-2026-110264 (an overflow of internal IDs in a pattern with many repeats) (Ruby, 2026-10-23). Ruby's table gives the first release of each series that carries each fix: the fix for CVE-2026-110264 first appears in 4.0.9, so 4.0.8 is not enough, and 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 carry all of them; GitLab fixed its own servers by patching the Ruby it ships (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

The advisory widens the exposure beyond GitLab to any Ruby application that compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls, says Regexp.timeout does not protect against these bugs and that limiting pattern length does not reliably protect, and says Ruby has not requested CVE identifiers of its own and that operators should track the issues under GitLab's identifiers (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

Sources: GitLab (Critical Patch Release 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, 18.11.13) · GitLab security (detection: Org-mode render error burst) · GitLab security (detection: Onigmo native worker crash) · Ruby (ruby-lang.org news, Regexp compilation fixes related to GitLab's CVEs)
HIGHupdatedNATOB1

TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix

First published 2026-10-21 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

TeamUpdraft says the attacker entered its site with a compromised key and suspects AI-accelerated tooling, and asks users to check the sites listed in their UpdraftCentral account; Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21 after 1.26.13 shipped and reads UpdraftPlus Premium as leaving the account password stored in the site database and backups.

TeamUpdraft's updates of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 say the attacker used a compromised key to access its site, that there is no evidence the attacker still has access, and that the speed of the exploits and the initially faulty backdoor plugins suggest AI was used to accelerate the attack, which is the vendor's inference and comes with no technical evidence (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19). It asks users to look at the sites listed under their UpdraftCentral account for any they did not knowingly connect since 2026-10-19, says it is seeing a pattern of unexpected Editor roles, and stresses that UpdraftPlus Premium users should check for unexpected plugins and new administrators even if they never used UpdraftCentral (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19).

Nethemba reports that the attacker kept going after the fix: on 2026-10-20 it tried the secret triggers of already removed backdoors on at least six sites of four administrators, and on the morning of 2026-10-21 it sent UpdraftCentral commands to two of Nethemba's sites after 1.26.13 had been released, blocked by Nethemba's own blocking plugin, with the keys no longer existing (Nethemba, 2026-10-19). A site that has a stolen key and neither updated nor deleted it by hand therefore stays exposed, and a removed backdoor is still probed. Nethemba also reads the code of UpdraftPlus Premium as storing the teamupdraft.com account password in the site database as entered and deleting it only after add-ons are claimed with a token, so it can stay in the database and in backups; a reader found it on all three of their premium sites and in backups going back to 2022, and Nethemba on one of its three, while the vendor says it is removed after the first connection and Nethemba has not found the samples it analysed reading it (Nethemba, 2026-10-19).

Sources: TeamUpdraft (post updated 2026-10-23) · Patchstack · Nethemba (living post, updated to 2026-10-23) · BleepingComputer
HIGHupdatedNATOA2

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

First published 2026-10-09 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT has put numbers on its exposure in a letter of 2026-10-23 to its roughly 17,000 active insured and 10,000 pensioners (IPCT, 2026-10-23). PK Softech told it in the late afternoon of 2026-10-14 that the authorities had established that personal data were taken from the supplier's servers, without saying which funds the data belonged to, and the fund's checks to date found among the documents on the attacked server data of about 1,800 persons, held there for two ongoing projects of spot checks and recalculations (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 1,700 are persons who left the fund through resignation or death in 2024 and 2025: surname, first name, postal address, date of birth, AHV number and insured number, the exit-benefit amount and the receiving fund with its bank account (IBAN), and the personal IBAN for about 50 who were paid out directly, with no e-mail address or telephone number (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 80 are insured persons on a disability pension whose passive pension data was being updated: name, date of birth, AHV number, insured number, passive insured salary, passive retirement assets, degree and start of invalidity, with no contact data (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

The fund says it has no certain evidence that these data were taken but that it appears plausible, that savings capital and pensions of all insured are untouched, that the cantonal administration's IT centre hosting the fund's infrastructure was not breached, and that it filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and was recognised as private plaintiff, while the Federal Prosecutor's Office and the federal police investigate (IPCT, 2026-10-23; Ticinonline, 2026-10-23). It decided to send the letter to all insured because its information is partial, the analyses are still evolving and it may never have certainty, and it asks them to watch for unexpected e-mails, calls and messages over the coming weeks and never to disclose passwords, access data or personal data unless sure of the requester (IPCT, 2026-10-23). The letter names PK Softech's other customers as Publica, large cantonal public funds such as Bern and Zurich and company funds such as Migros and Post, for hundreds of thousands of insured persons in total (IPCT, 2026-10-23).
