LiteLLM 1.107.0: the PyPI wheels and the official Docker images carried a credential stealer and a dormant remote-code loader that Python starts at every launch, published through the maintainers' own release workflow with stolen developer tokens

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 replaces the earlier log-leak hypothesis: a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker an organization owner's GitHub CLI token on 2026-10-10, eleven days before the release, and Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running that day.

The maintainers published a root-cause post on 2026-10-23 that supersedes the earlier hypothesis that the tokens were read from the logs of an internet-exposed internal deployment: their request logs show the first token came from a different service, an experimental agent platform whose master key had been committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The attacker used the key on 2026-10-10 to obtain an organization owner's GitHub CLI token, so access began eleven days before the release, and the same day throwaway branches in two repositories ran workflows that posted CI secrets to an external capture endpoint and were deleted minutes later, yielding the tokens of two further maintainers (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Socket found the same activity independently from the repository's Actions performance metrics, including a second run on 2026-10-12 that took 14 further secrets, and says it has not established how the attacker first obtained access (Socket, 2026-10-23). On 2026-10-21 three credentials did different jobs: the owner's token overrode branch protection and later force-pushed the history clean, a second maintainer's token approved the production gate and a third maintainer's token deleted the run records, after the maintainers had relaxed the release rule earlier that week so that any two engineers could trigger and approve a release (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The maintainers say they are revoking every token tied to every internal system and vendor platform, and that the attacker's activity on other systems focused on upstream inference API tokens (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Other vendors report no successful exploitation. CrowdStrike has not observed any in the wild or in its honeypots and expects a reliable exploit only against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23); Wordfence knows of no compromise among the more than 74,000 attempts its firewall intercepted (Wordfence, 2026-10-22); and Sophos corrected on 2026-10-22 its earlier report of successful exploitation to scanning and a small number of failed attempts, one of them a blocked attempt to deliver a likely Mirai-derived botnet variant (Sophos, 2026-10-22). Verification loop: three cti-verification passes, all NEEDS_FIXES, with truth plus editorial counts of 12, 5 and 2, and every claim in each pass's scope answered against the ledger (306, 315 and 253 claims). Iteration 1 found a mis-assigned footnote on Cisco's Duo and URWB rows, the Panorama and WF-500 table wording and dating on the Palo Alto advisory (its timeline dates the WF-500 correction to 2026-10-23, not 2026-10-24), a fourth Threat Prevention condition, a tense error on the IPCT letter, a Fortinet citation that did not carry the not-exploited clause, Nethemba's blocking plugin as a second blocker, an unhedged Publica sentence, Unit 42's missing foothold qualifier and a missing Exposure line on the Publica entry; all were fixed. Iteration 2 found the Panorama fix incomplete (the advisory's mitigation text names Panorama), a Patchstack time zone, a stale run-record sentence and two missing citations; all were fixed. Iteration 3 found two low-confidence wording defects (TeamUpdraft's key-cutoff sentence after the vendor's own page changed, and a Fortinet clause that attributed cron to a second file) and two advisories; it exited under the low-residual rule (truth plus editorial of 2, no F1 or F4), and all four were fixed after the pass without a further independent read, so verification_residual_count records the final pass's 2. Declined advisories: the Fortinet record type (improvement stays, the proof of concept predates the entry) and the Publica entry's length (consolidation is the audit's job). The Splunk CVE-2026-76268 drop was logged as a deliberate drop after the first pass flagged it as a missed angle; passes 2 and 3 found no missed angle.

Publish note for the audit: the Publica/PK Softech entry now carries eleven changelog sections and about 71 KB; the verifier suggests consolidating its per-fund statements and splitting its first action.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-23
item.description:
• Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November. Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited. →
  • Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights. Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date. →
  • FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed. Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November. Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited. →
  2. 02Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights. Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date. →
  3. 03FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed. Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 5Updates to prior coverage 4Action items 11

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLENATOB2

MythicRatatoskr: ESET documents a Go backdoor that hides its command server inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, and a UAC-0099 to Sandworm access handoff that ended in a Group Policy wiper attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics firm

ESET reports that on 2025-07-16 UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company through a spearphishing attachment: a scheduled task ran a PowerShell payload, the MATCHBOIL downloader deployed the MATCHWOK backdoor, and the next day a previously undocumented Go backdoor, MythicRatatoskr, arrived, which ESET ties to that chain with high confidence because of the timing (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). Further copies reached other machines through an OpenSSH SFTP server, and a SOCKS5 server appeared on some of them (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). About two months later, on 2025-09-17, the SDelete utility was deployed through Active Directory Group Policy, which ESET calls standard Sandworm tradecraft and assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access; ESET could not say which group operated MythicRatatoskr, and it sets the pair beside the earlier Gamaredon and Turla collaboration (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

The backdoor is built on the user-space yggstack, so it needs no tunnel interface or privileges to join the Yggdrasil mesh, an encrypted IPv6 overlay in the 200::/7 range: it picks three peers at random from an embedded list of public peers and then speaks JSON over HTTPS on port 443 to a command server that has an address only inside the mesh, and some samples wait ten minutes before connecting (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). It runs as a Windows service with an updater-style name, and it exfiltrates files and screenshots over the mesh without staging them (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). ESET notes that hosting the command server in the mesh may prevent network security tools from detecting the outbound connections to it and that blocking the public peer addresses is a viable mitigation (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Windows estates whose users can open email attachments from outside and whose egress to arbitrary internet peers is not filtered; there is no product vulnerability, and ESET has not seen the backdoor anywhere else (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).
Detection
In egress and DNS logs, connections to the public Yggdrasil peer addresses, since the mesh traffic looks like ordinary outbound connections and the peer list is the handle; in service-creation and process telemetry, a new Windows service with an updater-style name that runs a Go binary from a system or user folder, a scheduled task that runs a PowerShell payload from a temporary folder after an attachment is opened, and an OpenSSH SFTP server appearing on a workstation; and for the destructive stage, Group Policy objects that deploy SDelete or a similar wiper and mass file overwriting after a long quiet period (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Triage: ESET notes that legitimate users adopt Yggdrasil for resilient connectivity, research and hobby networking (ESET Research, 2026-10-22), so a single mesh connection needs a business-owner check; a mesh peer connection together with a service named like an updater, as ESET found the backdoor's service to be (ESET Research, 2026-10-22), is the stronger combination.

Defender takeaway
Where the mesh has no business use, block egress to the public Yggdrasil peers and alert on Group Policy changes that deploy wiper-class tools; the observed victim is Ukrainian and ESET describes UAC-0099 as targeting Ukrainian governmental, financial and media organizations, so the lesson transfers as tradecraft, in particular that initial-access activity by one group preceded a destructive stage by another two months later (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Builds on: 2026-10-09/talos-ai-analysis-evasion-instructions-aimed-at-llm-triage

threat23 Oct 03:40Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: ESET Research (WeLiveSecurity)
NOTABLECVE-2022-21894 +1exploitedNATOB2

BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it

Kaspersky GReAT reports that in early 2026 it found BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus, used against diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan after the attackers held administrator privileges: an installer takes an RC4-encrypted package and its key as command-line arguments and drops files to the system and UEFI partitions that exploit Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker-controlled Machine Owner Keys, so arbitrary EFI files load despite Secure Boot (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky ties the exploitation to Baton Drop alone; CVE-2023-24932, the flaw Microsoft's revocation guidance is titled for, appears in its post only as the one a UEFI component in ESET's FishMonger report might exploit (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). The bootkit injects a kernel driver, signed with a certificate its issuer has since revoked, that disables process, thread and registry callbacks and ETW providers of security products; the user-mode payloads were a RAT that uses Google Drive, OneDrive or Yandex.Disk for command and control and a sideloaded loader (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

The targeted machines were fully patched. Microsoft's fix revokes the Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate only when an administrator sets a Secure Boot registry flag and runs the Secure-Boot-Update scheduled task (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22); Microsoft's own article says the mitigations in the updates of 2024-07-09 and later are not enabled by default and the Enforcement Phase date is still to be announced (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30), and Kaspersky says that phase has not been implemented and the certificate's expiry on 2026-10-19 does not stop the vulnerable binaries loading unless it is on the forbidden list (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky attributes the campaign to APT41 with medium confidence, resting on the identifier "xdd" shared with a kernel implant in ESET's June 2026 FishMonger report, DLL sideloading and OLLVM (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any Windows device that boots with Secure Boot, has the updates of 2024-07-09 or later and has not had the revocation steps applied; Microsoft's check is that the forbidden-list (DBX) variable contains Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011, which a PowerShell test returns as True once the revocation is in (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).
Detection
The installer needs administrator rights, so the hunt starts with the administrator-level intrusion that precedes it; the behaviors Kaspersky describes are process creation of an executable from a program-data subfolder that takes an encrypted data file and a key as arguments, file writes to the EFI system partition by processes that are not servicing, kernel driver loads signed by an unfamiliar or revoked certificate, a signed executable renamed to look like an updater that loads a sideloaded DLL, and non-browser processes talking to consumer cloud storage (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Because the driver disables security-product callbacks and ETW providers, quiet host telemetry after a reboot on a machine that ran the installer is not evidence that nothing ran, although Kaspersky found that the driver's tampering routines, written for Kaspersky and Avast products, failed to interfere with Kaspersky products (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
A patched Windows fleet is not protected against this class until the revocation is applied, so decide which devices get Microsoft's procedure and in what order; Microsoft warns that the revocation cannot be reverted while Secure Boot is in use, that BitLocker recovery keys should be backed up first, and that recovery and install media must be updated (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).

Builds on: 2026-06-17/fishmonger-i-soon-ports-its-sprysocks-backdoor-to-windows-wi · 2026-07-14/eset-forgotten-uefi-shims-secure-boot-bypass

threat23 Oct 03:39Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Kaspersky GReAT (Securelist) · Microsoft Support (KB5025885)
NOTABLENATOB2

M365 token spray and replay: Huntress tracks a 10-week campaign that replays stolen post-MFA tokens from rented hosting within minutes, registers rogue Entra devices, wipes and re-registers MFA methods and hides mail with inbox rules of one to three characters or punctuation only

Between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 Huntress detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events across 79 victim organizations that replayed stolen sign-in tokens instead of guessing passwords (Huntress, 2026-10-22). The tokens came from adversary-in-the-middle relays behind fake sign-in pages, from device-code phishing and from social engineering during a genuine sign-in; a relay passes the real login page and MFA prompt through and keeps the token Microsoft issues afterwards, so its holder does not face MFA again (Huntress, 2026-10-22). Replay followed within minutes, after 12 minutes on 2026-07-21 and four minutes on 2026-09-22, from one of six addresses in a single rented range used in turn, so blocking one address stops at most one phase (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

A scripted replayer with the user agent node requests tokens with the Microsoft Office and Microsoft Authentication Broker client applications against Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and the Device Registration Service and joins 48 rogue Entra devices named DESKTOP- plus exactly eight uppercase hexadecimal characters, where the Windows default is seven alphanumeric characters; a browser-session replayer uses current Chrome or Edge through the OfficeHome client (Huntress, 2026-10-22). What outlives a password reset is the persistence: in 19 organizations the victim's MFA methods were wiped and a new authenticator registered within three hours, the rogue devices stay in the directory until deleted, and hidden inbox rules with names of one to three characters or punctuation only, created from VPN or other rented addresses, moved mail to RSS Feeds, RSS Subscriptions or Conversation History or deleted it, one keyed on payroll and bank terms (Huntress, 2026-10-22). Conditional Access blocks reported as AADSTS53003 fire only after authentication has succeeded, so they signal a valid credential, and ranking tenants by failed attempts points responders at the wrong ones (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any Entra tenant where users can sign in to Microsoft 365 from unmanaged networks and Conditional Access does not require MFA or block for all users, all cloud apps and all client app types unconditionally, or where the device-code flow is open; Huntress names no victim, sector or country (Huntress, 2026-10-22).
Detection
In Entra sign-in logs, OAuth2:Token and Cmsi:Cmsi requests from hosting infrastructure that use the Microsoft Office or Authentication Broker client with a node or bare Mozilla/5.0 user agent, above all those that touch user mailboxes or the Device Registration Service; in the Entra audit log, device registrations from hosting addresses with the DESKTOP-plus-eight-hex name shape and MFA methods deleted and re-added within minutes; in Exchange audit data, inbox rules with the short names described above, especially created through the REST API (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Triage: a node user agent with an Office client identifier can be legitimate automation, so Huntress focuses on sign-ins that touch user mailboxes or the Device Registration Service from hosting infrastructure, and it says the device-name pattern is rare but not unique to this campaign, so a device should be confirmed before it is deleted (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Defender takeaway
Revoke sessions as well as resetting the password, because the access token lives about 90 minutes after a reset, then audit devices, MFA methods, inbox rules and newly consented enterprise applications; as controls, require MFA or block for all users, all cloud apps and all client app types unconditionally, restrict the device-code flow with authentication-flow policies, and disable user consent to new applications (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Builds on: 2026-10-18/connectwise-cloud-backup-skykick-m365-app-credential-abuse · 2026-10-19/ics-calendar-invite-phishing-auto-added-outlook-gmail · 2026-10-22/artex-storm-0940-agentic-llm-pentest-spraying-oauth-abuse

threat23 Oct 03:39Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Huntress

02Trending vulnerabilities5 items

HIGHNATOA2

Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: critical and high-severity fixes in FortiOS 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 and 7.2.14, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with the advisories withheld until 2026-11-10

Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, scheduled for 2026-10-22 and following recent releases for FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). Fortinet says the releases fix vulnerabilities found through its frontier-AI-assisted testing programme, that they include critical and high-severity fixes, and that customers should treat them as a priority change rather than routine maintenance, because AI tools can help adversaries reverse-engineer patches and build working exploits in hours or days, patch differences show where the weakness sits, and AI can chain lower-severity flaws (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). The public advisories will appear only at the next Patch Tuesday, 2026-11-10 (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). NCSC.ch's advisory describes the fixes as ones that might allow attackers to gain unauthorized control over affected security infrastructure and lists the current exploitation status as unknown (NCSC.ch, 2026-10-22).

Fortinet's tables name these affected and fixed versions: FortiOS 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (fixed 8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.7 (7.6.8), 7.4.0 to 7.4.12 (7.4.13) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.13 (7.2.14); FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.7 (7.6.8), 7.4.0 to 7.4.11 (7.4.12) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.12 (7.2.13); FortiMail 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.6 (7.6.7), 7.4.0 to 7.4.8 (7.4.9) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.9 (upgrade to the 7.4 branch or later); FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 to 8.0.3 (8.0.4) and 6.6.0 to 6.6.10 (6.6.11) (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). FortiSASE updates automatically, FortiManager Cloud may need a manual update, and public-cloud instances follow their cloud partners' release processes (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). heise online lists the same fixed builds and the same 2026-11-10 disclosure date (heise online, 2026-10-22).

The FortiMail rows are identical to the fix table of Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-175, an unauthenticated path traversal in the FortiMail IBE webmail service (CVE-2026-104286) that Fortinet reports as exploited in the wild (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-10-01). Those FortiMail builds therefore already fix a flaw under attack, and the post does not say whether they carry further fixes; for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator no source states exploitation.

Exposure
FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator on a version listed above; Fortinet tells customers to inventory every FortiManager and FortiOS instance and to start with those reachable from the internet (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). Its tables name no row for FortiOS 7.0 or 6.4, and the post does not say whether those branches are affected (Fortinet, 2026-10-21).
Detection
Fortinet advises watching logs for unusual administrative access and unapproved configuration changes before and after patching, which means administrator authentication and configuration-change records on the firewalls and the management servers (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). With no CVE details published, no flaw-specific indicator or post-compromise check exists yet.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade internet-facing units first, inside the change windows of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 that Fortinet suggested, after backing up configurations (FortiMail units still below the fixed builds are exposed to the exploited flaw, not only to the unknown ones); until the advisories of 2026-11-10 there is no identifier to match a scanner finding or an alert against, so the fixed-version list is the only scope statement. Where an upgrade has to wait, restrict administrative HTTPS and SSH to trusted addresses or disable them on external interfaces, keep FortiManager administration off the internet and manage devices out of band, and enforce MFA for every administrator account (Fortinet, 2026-10-21).

Builds on: 2026-10-16/peerstitch-fortigate-implant-cve-2025-61624-fortimanager · 2026-10-02/cve-2026-104286-fortimail-path-traversal-zero-day-kev

vulnerability23 Oct 03:38Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Fortinet (CISO Collective blog) · NCSC.ch Security Hub (advisory 13092) · heise online · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-26-175)
HIGHCVE-2026-114625exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-114625, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem: an SQL injection lets any authenticated user, down to the Enterprise Read Only role, act as a superuser operator, and Arista says it is actively exploited (CVSS 3.1 9.9)

Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 covers CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9, CVSS 4.0 9.4, CWE-89 SQL injection) in the on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO): on an affected system any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local "superuser operator", which includes access to functionality intended for internal use only and not for remote access (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista states that it detected the issue and that it is known to be actively exploited, and the advisory names no actor, victim count or start date (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). The prerequisite is network access to the VCO web interface and a valid session on the VCO portal; the lowest role that suffices is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in tenant role, the interface is exposed by default and no configuration prevents the exposure (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Affected are VCO 5.2.x before 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x before 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.x before 6.4.2.12, and end-of-support releases were not assessed; hosted and dedicated VCO were affected and are already patched, while VeloCloud Gateway and VeloCloud Edge are not affected (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista's recommended resolution is the upgrade, and for an unsupported release train it points customers to its support centre to discuss upgrade options (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22); its CSAF file records the CVSS 3.1 score and the same interim measures, and describes the flaw as "VeloCloud Orchestrator Remote Code Execution (VCO RCE)" where the advisory page names an SQL injection that grants operator privileges; Arista does not say how the two descriptions relate (Arista Networks CSAF, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
An on-premises VCO on one of the three trains above, reachable at its web interface by anyone who holds a portal login of any role, a customer-tenant account included; Arista's list is by train, so compare each Orchestrator against the three fixed releases (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Web access logs of the VCO for requests with unusual URL-like path components, encoded characters, references to local or internal services and high request rates; outbound connections from the VCO host that the Orchestrator does not normally make; backdoor daemons and web shells on the host; and recent administrator activity for changes nobody made (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista asks operators to preserve the web, application, system and database logs and the file-system timestamps before remediation where feasible, and its advisory does not say that the upgrade removes a foothold that is already there (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Triage: a session authenticated as a low-privilege tenant account, Enterprise Read Only above all, that reaches operator-only or internal-only functions is the signal, because legitimate operators act from their own accounts; Arista lists attacker source addresses in its advisory (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade the Orchestrator to a fixed release of its train now, restrict the web interface to administrative networks in the meantime, and on any Orchestrator that was reachable and unpatched keep the logs first and then check the host for backdoor daemons and web shells.

Builds on: 2026-09-23/cve-2026-93952-arista-velocloud-orchestrator-exploited · 2026-07-28/cve-2026-16812-arista-velocloud-orchestrator-exploited

vulnerability23 Oct 03:31Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Arista Networks (Security Advisory 0199) · Arista Networks (CSAF for Security Advisory 0199)
NOTABLECVE-2026-107656 +1updatedNATOA2

Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical advisories for security-operations products on 2026-10-13. FG-IR-26-185 describes an authentication bypass through an alternate path or channel in the FortiSandbox GUI that a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger with crafted HTTP requests, listed as CVE-2026-107656 with CVSS 3.1 9.6 and an impact of unauthorized code or command execution (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). FG-IR-26-180 describes a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service ("arbitrary file write in grpc phQueryMaster") that lets an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code or commands through specially crafted packets, listed as CVE-2026-106173 with CVSS 3.1 9.4 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). Both pages state that neither flaw is known to be exploited, and both carry temporal vector strings with an exploit-code maturity of functional (FortiSandbox) and high (FortiSIEM) that the advisories do not explain (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

For FortiSandbox, versions 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 and 4.4.0 through 4.4.9 are affected and 5.0.7 and 4.4.10 fix it; 5.2 is not affected; FortiSandbox PaaS 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 is affected, and every PaaS 4.4 version must migrate to a fixed release (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). The ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). Defused reported exploitation of three FortiSandbox flaws in June, CVE-2026-39813, CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089 (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16), and the build that fixes CVE-2026-25089 is 5.0.6 on the 5.0 branch and 4.4.9 on 4.4 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09), so a unit patched for that flaw is not patched for this one. For FortiSIEM only 7.5.0 is affected and 7.5.1 fixes it; 7.6 and FortiSIEM Cloud are not affected, and Fortinet's workaround is to restrict access on tcp port 27918 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20: the phQueryMaster gRPC service listens on tcp 27918 on every interface and does not request a client certificate, so any remote client can reach its SendQueryResult method, whose query-id metadata is joined into a file path without validation, and a NUL byte in it discards the suffix the service appends, which turns the write into an overwrite of a chosen file (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20). Horizon3 uses it to replace a health-check script that a cron job runs every 60 seconds, which gives code execution within a minute (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20; The Hacker News, 2026-10-20). Fortinet's advisory says the flaw is not known to be exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
FortiSandbox appliances, virtual machines and PaaS instances on the affected ranges whose GUI an unauthenticated client can reach, and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 nodes where tcp port 27918 is reachable from outside the deployment (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).
Detection
Fortinet publishes no indicator or post-compromise check for either flaw (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). The behaviors to look for follow from the mechanisms: on FortiSandbox, administrator-level GUI actions that have no matching login event, and on FortiSIEM, connections to tcp port 27918 from addresses outside the deployment followed by new files or processes on the node. Horizon3 found no application logs that would reveal exploitation and advises inspecting the write and modification timestamps of a script that a cron job runs, such as the charting health-check script, and of other files of interest such as the license tool, for any that do not match the surrounding files (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20).
Defender takeaway
Move FortiSandbox to 5.0.7 or 4.4.10 (PaaS 4.4 migrates) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 to 7.5.1, treating the FortiSIEM upgrade or the port restriction as out of cycle now that a proof of concept is public; a FortiSandbox at 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 still needs this upgrade (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). Fortinet's only workaround is for FortiSIEM, restricting access on tcp port 27918 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13); it names none for FortiSandbox, where limiting GUI access to an administrator network is the usual precaution rather than a Fortinet instruction.

A public proof of concept exists for the FortiSIEM 7.5.0 flaw: Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and the exploit for CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20 (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20; The Hacker News, 2026-10-20). CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version; fixed in 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and the FIPS and NDcPP builds

NetScaler Product Security says NetScaler is affected by the two PHP memory-safety flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 because the NetScaler Management Portal uses PHP and that all supported software versions are affected; the post, last updated on 2026-10-27, now says Citrix has released fixes for all supported versions (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21). Citrix describes both as critical flaws in PHP that could let an unauthenticated attacker execute code in the context of the affected PHP process, each rated 9.2 under CVSS 4.0: CVE-2026-109618 is memory corruption when PHP handles an out-of-memory condition during request processing, and CVE-2026-109619 is stale request state that persists after memory is released and is reused by a later request (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21). The affected surfaces are the NSIP GUI, any SNIP configured to permit management access and the cluster IP GUI in a cluster; NetScaler Console (service and on premises) and NetScaler SVM are not affected (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21).

Citrix's bulletin CTX697263, revised on 2026-10-27, now urges customers to install NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.49 or later, 13.1-64.32 or later of 13.1, ADC 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS or later, and ADC 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 or later, and lists NetScaler Console as not impacted (Citrix, 2026-10-22); CERT-FR's notice of 2026-10-27 gives the same first fixed builds (CERT-FR, 2026-10-27). Citrix tells customers to restrict GUI and API access on those addresses to trusted administrative hosts or narrowly scoped management networks, to keep management interfaces off the internet behind jump hosts or tight ACLs, and to review every address that permits GUI or API management and verify that it is not broadly reachable (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Every NetScaler ADC and Gateway on a supported version whose NSIP, a management-enabled SNIP or the cluster IP answers on its GUI or API from a network that is not a trusted administrative one; a SNIP or VIP can also carry application traffic, so Citrix tells customers to scope ACLs to management protocols and ports (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21).
Detection
Connections to the management GUI and API from addresses that are not the administrative hosts, which is also the test of whether the ACLs hold; Citrix's post publishes no detection guidance and does not say whether NetScaler has been attacked (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21).
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed builds now, appliances whose management addresses are reachable from outside the administrative network first; the PHP project's own fixed releases do not help an appliance owner, because the fix ships in Citrix's package. Until a build is installed, apply the management ACLs and keep a recovery path such as console access in case a rule blocks administration (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-21).

HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 72 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 (initial release 2026-10-22) fixes 72 CVEs in the wireless operating systems AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways managed by HPE Networking Central, AOS-10 access points (AOS-AP) and AOS-8 Instant access points (AOS-IAP) (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). By the CSAF's CVSS 3.1 scores, 33 of the 72 rate 9.0 or higher (eight at 10.0, ten at 9.8, ten at 9.6, one at 9.4 and four at 9.3); the 19 rated 10.0, 9.8 or 9.4 need network access and no privileges, and the other 14 are reachable from the adjacent network (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). The named mechanisms include authentication bypasses and command injection in the AOS-10 interface and in the PAPI protocol, a buffer overflow and a command injection in the AOS-8 PAPI protocol that arrive as crafted packets on its UDP port, an authentication bypass in the AOS-8 SSH daemon, and SQL injection in the web-based management interface (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE says the flaws were generally found by its internal security research, that it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code as of the release, and that customers are strongly urged to patch; for some of the critical rows exploitation also needs preconditions outside the attacker's control, which the bulletin does not itemise (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).

The bulletin and its CSAF name AOS-10 10.8.x up to 10.8.1.1, 10.7.x up to 10.7.2.6 and 10.4.x up to 10.4.1.13, and AOS-8 8.13.x up to 8.13.3.0 and 8.10.x up to 8.10.0.23; fixed builds are AOS-10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7 and 10.4.1.14 and AOS-8.13.3.1 and 8.10.0.24 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE's workaround is to restrict the CLI and web-based management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN, controlled by firewall policies at layer 3 and above with accounting controls (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any HPE Networking mobility conductor, controller, gateway, access point or virtual machine that runs a listed version; HPE says every compatible hardware model is affected and that its own hardware list is illustrative only, so the check is the software version, not the model (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). HPE presumes versions past end of maintenance affected and says installations past end of support should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). The named surfaces are the CLI and web management interfaces and the PAPI access-point management protocol on UDP port 8211 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Management-plane access and accounting logs for logins and sessions from outside the management segment, and network flow data for PAPI traffic on UDP 8211 or controller management ports from segments that carry users or guests. HPE publishes no detection guidance, so no post-compromise check is defined (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade controllers, gateways and access points to the fixed build of their train, management and PAPI-exposed units first, and apply the management-segment restriction at once where the upgrade has to wait; HPE says it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code, so the order follows exposure of the management and access-point protocol paths rather than a known campaign (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).
Correction25 Oct 2026 14:04 UTCrun 2026-10-25T1308Z-auditsummarycvessourcesbody

HPE's CSAF does not list wider affected ranges than the bulletin text: both name AOS-10 10.8, 10.7 and 10.4 and AOS-8 8.13 and 8.10 up to the stated builds, and neither carries a 10.6, 10.3 or 8.12 range (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). What HPE adds instead is that versions past end of maintenance are presumed affected and installations past end of support should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). The CSAF scores 33 of the 72 flaws at CVSS 9.0 or higher, ten of them at 9.6, and 14 of the 33 are reachable from the adjacent network, not 34, eleven and 15 (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

First published 2026-10-21 · open finding →

Update23 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

BACS told Keystone-SDA and SRF on 2026-10-22 that no attack in Switzerland attributable to the two flaws is known to it, while stressing that unrecognised or unreported incidents cannot be excluded and that it has no reliable figures on affected websites, shops and internal applications (SRF, 2026-10-22; watson.ch, 2026-10-22). It also said that PHP-based applications of the federal administration were affected, that the responsible bodies were told to update, and that it has no complete overview of the update status (watson.ch, 2026-10-22; Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

The shutdowns were large and mostly short. The Basel host Cyon took all of its more than 100,000 customer websites offline for some hours and says everything has run again since the morning of 2026-10-22; the University of Geneva's site was still unreachable that afternoon, and Basel-Stadt still had pages offline at midday and says it found no data outflow (SRF, 2026-10-22). Neuchâtel disabled all PHP-based sites, ne.ch and many commune pages among them, its IT department installed the fix, and the EPFL gave its members access to its services by VPN while its site stayed down (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). Risikomonitor's live view counts 576,549 checked Swiss web servers, 540,169 already patched and 20,231 (3.5 %) still affected, with the PHP version hidden on the other 16,149 (Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

In the United Kingdom, a minister told the House of Lords on 2026-10-22 that 32 government services were unavailable and four partly unavailable, largely from precautionary measures while updates and mitigations were applied, and that the government knows of no confirmed compromise of central government systems, an assessment she extended to the wider public sector (UKAuthority, 2026-10-22; The Register, 2026-10-22). The Register adds that government sites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland and the Netherlands were also taken offline as a precaution and that the NCSC sent 50,000 warnings (The Register, 2026-10-22).

Attack activity began before the release. Inside IT, citing a post by Cloudflare's chief executive, reports millions of attack attempts, the first at 07:43 UTC on 2026-10-21, more than six hours before the release, and relays that AWS threat intelligence recorded an exploit attempt against a honeypot on 2026-10-17 from a commercial anonymisation network, proofs of concept and attempts by several actors from 2026-10-21, and advises an operator who cannot exclude a compromise to start the investigation at least from 2026-10-17; whether the attempts would have succeeded on real systems is open (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). The Register likewise reports that AWS says attackers were exploiting the flaws four days before disclosure (The Register, 2026-10-22).

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

First published 2026-10-09 · open finding →

Update23 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

Tamedia's Tages-Anzeiger reported on 2026-10-21 that PK Softech AG had confirmed in writing to Publica that it deleted the data, and that this apparently did not happen: its summary says the company reported in January that it had deleted the information on former Federal Councillors and agents, "but this was false" (translated from German; Tages-Anzeiger, 2026-10-21); the article is paywalled. Inside IT, working from the Tamedia research, dates the written confirmation to January 2026 and says PK Softech confirmed it held no personal data in plaintext and had deleted the data of the 2019 migration, that Publica confirmed the sequence (after the Xplain case it asked the supplier to delete all legacy data, including that of the 2019 migration, and received written confirmation), that Publica is clarifying why personal data presumably lay on the servers regardless, and that PK Softech did not answer and does not comment on individual customer relationships (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). 20 Minuten reports the same sequence and notes that PK Softech received the data in 2019 in a migration for Publica (20 Minuten, 2026-10-22).

Inside IT also relays, from Tamedia, that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed that data was extracted by the Akira ransomware group, which still threatens to publish or sell it; 20 Minuten writes that according to findings so far Akira stole the data (Inside IT, 2026-10-22; 20 Minuten, 2026-10-22). This is a reported confirmation of the actor by an authority, but it reaches the reader second-hand through the paywalled Tamedia article: the Federal Prosecutor's Office is not quoted directly, and Publica's own page, in its entry of 2026-10-20, still says it is clarifying whether data of Publica left and whose (Publica, 2026-10-20).

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT says through Corriere del Ticino, relayed by Ticinonline on 2026-10-20, that potentially all of its insured could be involved but that there is no evidence yet that their data was actually taken; it has filed a complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office and is preparing a letter to the insured warning of telephone and e-mail fraud (Ticinonline, 2026-10-20). TicinoNews adds, from its own information, that a folder labelled IPCT with the data of a few hundred insured persons was on the supplier's server, while IPCT, which has about 27,000 affiliated persons, says it has no certainty yet that data of its insured is involved (TicinoNews, 2026-10-21).

Sources: Swiss Federal Administration (admin.ch) · PK Softech AG · watson.ch · Netzwoche · Netzwoche (running story, update of 2026-10-21) · Bernische Pensionskasse (BPK) · Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse (BLVK) · Pensionskasse Post · Inside IT (AWP) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes) · cash.ch (AWP) · Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes), page updated through 2026-10-21 · Cybercrimepolice (cantonal police platform) · SwissCybersecurity.net · Inside IT · NZZ · Blick (SonntagsBlick) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled; summary lines readable) · 20 Minuten · Ticinonline (relaying Corriere del Ticino) · Istituto di previdenza del Cantone Ticino (IPCT, letter to its insured) · Ticinonline · TicinoNews · EDÖB (Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner), press release · Der Bund (Tamedia) · Publica (newsletter of 2026-10-22, Cyberangriff auf Softwarelieferanten: Was wir wissen und was nicht)

04Action items11 items

  • Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.
    FindingPK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had…→
  • If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
    FindingPK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had…→
  • Upgrade every internet-facing FortiOS (8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 or 7.2.14), FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.12 or 7.2.13), FortiMail (8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9; 7.2 moves to 7.4 or later) and FortiAuthenticator (8.0.4 or 6.6.11) now rather than in the November cycle, saving the configuration first; where the upgrade has to wait, restrict HTTPS and SSH administration to trusted addresses or disable it on external interfaces and keep FortiManager administration off the internet.
    FindingFortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes…→
  • Upgrade every on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 or 6.4.2.12 (or later in its train) now and, until then, restrict its web interface to trusted administrative networks; before upgrading, preserve the web access, application, system and database logs and the file-system timestamps, then check the host for backdoor daemons, web shells and unexpected outbound traffic.
    FindingCVE-2026-114625→
  • Check every FortiSandbox that was upgraded to 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 after the exploited-flaw advisories of this year: those builds are still affected by CVE-2026-107656 and need 5.0.7 or 4.4.10; on FortiSIEM 7.5.0 install 7.5.1, or until then restrict access to tcp 27918 as Fortinet's workaround says.
    FindingCVE-2026-107656 +1→
  • In every Entra tenant, list the devices registered since 2026-07-14 whose names are DESKTOP- followed by eight uppercase hexadecimal characters, the authenticators that were deleted and re-registered within minutes, and the inbox rules whose names are one to three characters or punctuation only or that move mail to RSS Feeds, RSS Subscriptions or Conversation History, and remove what nobody created; then revoke the sessions of any affected user, because a password reset leaves the devices, MFA methods and a roughly 90-minute access token in place.
    FindingHuntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed…→
  • Install NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS or 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 (or later) on every appliance whose NSIP, a management-enabled SNIP or the cluster IP answers on its GUI or API, internet-reachable ones first; until each has its build, restrict GUI and API access on those addresses to trusted administrative hosts with ACLs, keeping NetScaler Console access working.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Upgrade every HPE Networking (Aruba) Mobility Conductor, Controller, Gateway and access point on AOS-10 or AOS-8 to the fixed build of its train (10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, 10.4.1.14, 8.13.3.1 or 8.10.0.24), and until then confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN behind firewall policy, as HPE advises.
    FindingCVE-2026-79844 +18→
  • Update every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation, starting with standalone Java runtimes, including those already updated on 2026-10-21 (Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-114820 or the OpenJDK update), pip 26.2.2 or later in every Python environment, Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, and the CA bundles and base images the incident tracker lists, rebuild container images that embed an older bundle, then confirm with curl against the tracker's test host that the client rejects the certificate.
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +2→
  • Replace before 2026-10-27 every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3, by hand where the ACME client does not support ACME Renewal Information, because standard ACME clients do not replace a certificate outside its renewal window.
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +2→
  • Apply Cisco's remediation for the products its eMudhra advisory lists as impacted: a TLS policy on Secure Firewall Management Center that blocks the known eMudhra issuers, Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1 and ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2) now, and Meraki MV Smart Camera Firmware (2026-11-18), IOS XR 26.4.1 (2026-11-30) and Ultra Cloud Core Subscriber Microservices Infrastructure 2026.04.1 (November 2026) when they ship; other Cisco products are still under investigation.
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +2→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-23T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 8 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Window: gap 24.0 h from 2026-10-22T0256Z-intel, window 26 h, developing-story window 72 h. The container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s) and the first fetch of origin/main was current. A Friday-morning fire in the second day of the PHP2Shell story: the new signal is downstream (vendor impact statements, the Swiss and UK public-sector picture, diverging exploitability assessments), a vendor-confirmed exploited SD-WAN controller flaw, two out-of-cycle vendor releases (HPE Aruba, Fortinet), and three identity, boot-chain and C2 tradecraft reports.

KEV sweep (work/2026-10-23T0256Z-intel/kev-window.txt, catalogue 2026.10.21): no KEV addition inside the window, nothing NOT COVERED, no RANSOMWARE row; S1 read the live catalogue three times and confirmed it. Neither PHP CVE and not CVE-2026-114625 is KEV-listed.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): no open row, nothing carried or added; the Beyond Gravity row stays struck because S2 found nothing newer than 2026-10-15.

Published (8 new): cve-2026-114625-arista-velocloud-orchestrator-sqli-exploited (high: vendor-confirmed exploitation, any tenant login, no KEV listing; Arista is first-party and the only source, hence single-source; the two earlier VeloCloud entries are declared in references[]), hpesbnw05162-hpe-aruba-aos-8-aos-10-72-cves-19-unauth (notable: 19 unauthenticated network rows at 9.0 or above in one bulletin, HPE knows of no exploitation or public code; clears PD-11(b) through the number of unauthenticated rows on a management plane and campus wireless estates, a one-clause judgement), netscaler-php2shell-management-gui-fixes-2026-10-27 (notable: own entry because the product, the surfaces and the fix date are NetScaler's; declares the PHP entry and the PAN-OS entry in references[]; lookback item, source dated 2026-10-21 20:23 UTC), fortinet-hardening-release-fortios-fortimanager-fortimail (high: out-of-cycle critical and high fixes the vendor urges at once, advisories withheld to 2026-11-10, exploitation unknown; techniques[] carries T1190 on the vendor's statement that internet-facing devices come first and the interim measure restricts administrative interfaces, no CVE ids exist yet), fortinet-fortisandbox-fortisiem-pre-auth-critical-fixes (notable: first coverage of the Fortinet PSIRT bundle of 2026-10-13, found through the verifier's coverage pass, two unauthenticated critical rows, FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass at 9.6 and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 path traversal to code execution at 9.4, neither listed as exploited; the FortiSandbox ranges include the builds that fixed the three flaws reported exploited in June, which is the non-obvious defender hook; references the June FortiSandbox entry and the hardening entry), m365-token-spray-replay-rogue-entra-devices-mfa-wipe (notable: Huntress only, behaviour-rich identity tradecraft against the Microsoft 365 estate the constituency runs), blackx-uefi-bootkit-baton-drop-revocation-default-off (notable: a state-actor bootkit whose enabling condition is a default-off Microsoft control; actions[] empty because the revocation is a fleet programme, not a do-now task; references the FishMonger and UEFI-shim entries because CVE-2023-24932 appears in the store) and mythicratatoskr-yggdrasil-mesh-c2-uac-0099-sandworm-wiper (notable: Ukrainian victim of 2025, kept for the mesh-C2 detection hook and the access-handoff-to-wiper pattern; ground (d)). Updated (4, all type: update): the PK Softech entry (the supplier's January deletion pledge apparently not kept, a second-hand report that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira, the Ticino fund IPCT), the PHP2Shell entry (BACS: no known Swiss attack but federal PHP applications affected, the UK Lords figures, AWS's 2026-10-17 first attempt as relayed, Sansec's and Red Hat's cautious exploitability assessments against VulnCheck's exploit, vendor impact statements; priority left at critical because attack traffic is observed, authorities order the update and VulnCheck holds a working exploit, with no compromise confirmed), the eMudhra entry (Java: Oracle alert and OpenJDK advisory for CVE-2026-91403, NCSC.ch 13091) and the PAN-OS entry (the advisory's 2026-10-23 hotfix estimates for PAN-OS 12.2 to 10.2, WildFire WF-500 and WF-500-B and Panorama still undated). PHP2Shell on Cisco Expressway stays a one-clause statement on the PHP entry: it is a different finding from the CVE-2026-76466 entry, so no changelog record was written there.

Borderline drops: borderline-drop: YOOtheme Pro 5 image handler CVE-2026-102785 — unauthenticated CVSS 4.0 10.0 but no exploitation reported and no constituency deployment shown; a vendor-ordered immediate update and a package-diff write-up do not clear PD-11 (written, then cut at verification iteration 1); borderline-drop: Splunk October bundle SVD-2026-1007 to 1013 — scheduled bundle, grouped hardening rows with no stated prerequisites, no exploitation, regular patch cycle; borderline-drop: ISC BIND CVE-2026-94300 and two DoS flaws — CVSS 8.1 with high complexity, needs a captured signed GSS-TSIG message, no exploit known; borderline-drop: Roundcube 1.6.20 and 1.7.5 — about twenty fixes, authenticated paths, no exploitation statement; borderline-drop: Chrome 156 and the Edge Chromium batch — no exploitation reported, routine browser cycle; borderline-drop: MikroTik CVE-2026-89035 — unreviewed CVE record plus a BSI marker, no vendor advisory, so a no-fix claim cannot be cited to the vendor; borderline-drop: Siemens October Patch Day via CISA ICSA-26-295 — no exploitation, no constituency deployment shown; borderline-drop: EFK audit of the federal Microsoft 365 tenant — oversight audit, no near-term defender decision; borderline-drop: Swiss Government Cloud tender — procurement, non-security; borderline-drop: Beyond Gravity — no development since 2026-10-15, the struck row's re-open condition is unmet; borderline-drop: Ebury 1.8.3 on 333 Tor exit relays — no constituency nexus (relay operators and hosters); borderline-drop: CVE-2026-99999 PwnEscape (Linux KVM guest-to-host) — needs an attacker-controlled guest, no exploitation, no workaround, regular kernel cycle; borderline-drop: DeadTag expired-tag domains — vendor-driven research, no government nexus, the exploit-kit leg was dropped by earlier fires; borderline-drop: Rapid7 Q3 2026 quarterly report — statistics without a defender takeaway; borderline-drop: Hunt Intelligence Graylog and X-Road activity in Ukraine — Ukraine-only victims, Log4Shell public-PoC chain; borderline-drop: P3 and Navigate360 anonymous-tip breach — no Swiss customer shown, out of nexus; borderline-drop: Railway environment-variable exposure — no vector or actor yet and no Swiss nexus, preliminary report due 2026-10-23 midday ET, a later fire re-gates it; borderline-drop: NEC sub-contractor credential abuse (Japan) — out of nexus, lookback item; borderline-drop: Capcom, Onamae Desktop Cloud, the AfD mail leak and the US, Australian and Japanese incidents S4 listed — out of nexus, no transferable technique; borderline-drop: Ircantec forum-sale claim and Medienwerkstatt (Akira claim, mis-tagged DE) — claims without victim confirmation, PD-6; worth a re-check next fire. out-of-window: Sophos IR vishing plus SSPR abuse with a Primary Refresh Token session — primary dated 2026-10-19, window_hours=26, not a rotational-lookback item; the audit may want it, as it may Talos "Parasitizing trust" (2026-10-21, trend piece, dropped for recency and novelty).

Single-source items and carve-outs: the Arista, HPE, NetScaler and two Fortinet entries are first-party vendor advisories for their own products (NCSC.ch and heise restate Fortinet and add no independent assessment); Huntress, Kaspersky (the campaign and attribution, with Microsoft's KB independently confirming the default-off revocation) and ESET are single research sources; the Arista exploitation statement has no independent corroboration yet. Contradictions and unconfirmed claims reported, not resolved: Inside IT relays Tamedia that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated the data, Publica's own page of 2026-10-20 still says it is clarifying, and no prosecutor text was found; Sansec and Red Hat judge PHP2Shell exploitation harder than VulnCheck's weaponized exploit shows; Huntress gives 303 successes in 29 organizations and later 232 in 28 for one address, so no count from that passage is used.

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport including WebFetch and the reader, third consecutive run; ConnectWise coverage rests on search and the CCCS feed). Outside this window and with no store entry, for the audit's re-sweep: SAP Security Patch Day 2026-10-13 and the two non-exploited publicly disclosed October Microsoft zero-days. The Fortinet PSIRT bundle of 2026-10-13 (FortiSandbox, FortiSIEM) was first covered by this run after the verifier flagged it. Tages-Anzeiger has no full-text transport (lede and bullets only), so the Tamedia reporting rests on relays. The jina reader pool had three of four keys at HTTP 402 (operational note only). sources.promotion_due was acted on: expel, php-net-news and ssd-disclosure moved to active.

Candidate sources: one added, arista-security-advisories (the PSIRT behind three exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator advisories this year; extract plus the CSAF route). Suggested and not added under the one-per-run guide: isc-bind-security-matrix, ukauthority, 20min-ch, tio-ch, pwn.ai, CBC News Investigates; novee-security and air-security are noted for demotion at the next audit.

Entity registry: four entities registered (campaign:m365-token-spray-replay-huntress-2026, malware:blackx-uefi-bootkit, actor:apt41, malware:mythicratatoskr; attributed-to, affects relations sourced to the entries that state them) and eight product entities synced. BlackLotus is named only as a comparison and stays unkeyed.

Self-identification: this fire's main agent is Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) per the harness model line; the four research sub-agents reported Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) in their own return headers.

Verification loop: five cti-verification passes, all NEEDS_FIXES, with truth plus editorial counts of 16, 9, 3, 3 and 1 and every claim of every pass walked against the ledger (303, 282, 222, 284 and 165 claims in scope, all answered). Iteration 1 found the stale PAN-OS state (the advisory gained hotfix estimates three minutes after the entry was written), a VulnCheck sentence the page had since reversed, two stale eMudhra statements, the FortiMail overlap with the exploited CVE-2026-104286 entry, a Frontaliere Ticino aggregator citation, the YOOtheme entry (dropped: no constituency nexus, no exploitation), a PHP2Shell update on the Cisco Expressway entry that did not belong to that finding (reverted, one clause stays on the PHP entry), and the Fortinet PSIRT bundle of 2026-10-13 (new entry). Iterations 2 to 4 removed overstatements the fixes themselves introduced or exposed (a location and a decryption condition no source states, an uncited workaround, an exploited status on CVE-2023-24932, undated present-tense statements, store-internal wording, an eMudhra Update section that repeated the main analysis, the HPE exploitation attribution). Iteration 5 left one low-confidence F3 (from unnamed sources, fixed after the pass and not re-verified) and one advisory (extra ATT&CK ids on the Mythic entry, one added). The loop ended by the early exit of the decision rules (truth plus editorial at most 2, no F1 or F4), so verification_residual_count is 1 and no CLEAN confirmation applies; entries_dropped_by_verification is 1 (YOOtheme). One advisory finding was declined with a rebuttal: the NetScaler entry keeps the name PHP2Shell, which Sansec, VulnCheck, watson.ch and The Register use for these flaws, while its own cited source (Citrix) says two PHP memory safety vulnerabilities.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-22
item.description:
• Palo Alto reports active exploitation of PAN-OS management interfaces via PHP2Shell; all 20 hotfixes now out. Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-21 now says, as read on 2026-10-28, that active exploitation has been observed targeting the PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation, rates the flaw Critical with urgency Highest (CVSS-B 9.2) and lists every release of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 through the management web interface (the HTTPS web UI and the XML API service). All twenty hotfixes are released (one for each maintenance line from 10.2.7 to 12.2.4, as read on 2026-10-30); the advisory names no actor or victim, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. →
  • Group-IB: k0t takes edge devices in bulk and decrypts FortiGate configurations offline; enable private-data-encryption. Group-IB and NyxLab report a campaign by an operator they track as k0t that finds exposed FortiGate, FortiWeb and PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices in bulk, exploits FortiWeb CVE-2025-64446 and GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 or brute-forces FortiGate logins, downloads each FortiGate configuration and decrypts its stored LDAP, Active Directory and administrator secrets offline with the default FortiOS key, which cannot be seen on the appliance. Group-IB then sees hands-on Active Directory work, remote-management persistence and exfiltration, and victims that later appear on the Qilin and The Gentlemen leak sites; it assesses the operators as probable initial-access brokers but says the link to either group is unconfirmed. →
  • Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique. Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases. Expel independently saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration, enrol Okta Verify and sign in to applications, and CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the same framework. Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Palo Alto reports active exploitation of PAN-OS management interfaces via PHP2Shell; all 20 hotfixes now out. Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-21 now says, as read on 2026-10-28, that active exploitation has been observed targeting the PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation, rates the flaw Critical with urgency Highest (CVSS-B 9.2) and lists every release of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 through the management web interface (the HTTPS web UI and the XML API service). All twenty hotfixes are released (one for each maintenance line from 10.2.7 to 12.2.4, as read on 2026-10-30); the advisory names no actor or victim, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. →
  2. 02Group-IB: k0t takes edge devices in bulk and decrypts FortiGate configurations offline; enable private-data-encryption. Group-IB and NyxLab report a campaign by an operator they track as k0t that finds exposed FortiGate, FortiWeb and PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices in bulk, exploits FortiWeb CVE-2025-64446 and GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 or brute-forces FortiGate logins, downloads each FortiGate configuration and decrypts its stored LDAP, Active Directory and administrator secrets offline with the default FortiOS key, which cannot be seen on the appliance. Group-IB then sees hands-on Active Directory work, remote-management persistence and exfiltration, and victims that later appear on the Qilin and The Gentlemen leak sites; it assesses the operators as probable initial-access brokers but says the link to either group is unconfirmed. →
  3. 03Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique. Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases. Expel independently saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration, enrol Okta Verify and sign in to applications, and CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the same framework. Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 3Updates to prior coverage 4Action items 9

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLECVE-2025-64446 +2exploitedNATOB2

k0t: Group-IB and NyxLab describe a probable access broker that mass-exploits FortiWeb and PAN-OS GlobalProtect, brute-forces FortiGate and decrypts stolen FortiGate configurations offline with the default key, with victims later listed by Qilin and The Gentlemen

Group-IB and NyxLab describe a campaign by an operator they track as k0t (Group-IB lists CryptoFeel as a potential alias, and Scrooge as a likely collaborator and possible alias) that enumerates internet-facing VPN and firewall appliances in bulk and attacks the product directly, chiefly Fortinet firewalls and Palo Alto GlobalProtect portals (Group-IB, 2026-10-21). A custom script exploits CVE-2025-64446 against FortiWeb, a relative path traversal that lets an unauthenticated attacker run administrative commands, or brute-forces exposed Fortinet devices as a fallback (Group-IB, 2026-10-21; CISA KEV, 2026-10-21). Against PAN-OS it exploits CVE-2026-0257, the GlobalProtect authentication bypass, with a forged authentication-override cookie (Group-IB, 2026-10-21). On a compromised FortiGate the tool downloads the configuration and decrypts its secrets locally with the default FortiOS key, the weakness tracked as CVE-2019-6693, recovering LDAP and Active Directory bind and, Group-IB says, administrator credentials, although Fortinet's advisory excludes the administrator's password and says FIPS-CC devices are not impacted; unless private-data-encryption is set, the device falls back to that known key (Group-IB, 2026-10-21; Fortinet, 2019-11-19).

After access the operators work by hand with NetExec, Impacket, Kerbrute, relayed PetitPotam and Mimikatz, keep access through OpenConnect, MeshCentral agents, AdaptixC2, Atera and AnyDesk, and exfiltrate with Rclone to Wasabi and MEGA (Group-IB, 2026-10-21). Group-IB sees victim overlap with the Qilin and The Gentlemen leak sites and assesses the operators are probably initial-access brokers, but says no relationship is confirmed, and it found indications of a possible connection with the FortiBleed cluster alongside negligible overlap in the compromised credentials (Group-IB, 2026-10-21). CISA lists all three CVEs in KEV, with ransomware use marked known for CVE-2026-0257 and CVE-2019-6693 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Internet-reachable FortiGate administrator and VPN logins, FortiWeb up to 8.0.1, 7.6.4, 7.4.9, 7.2.11 or 7.0.11 on its branch (Fortinet, 2025-11-14), and PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals and gateways below the per-branch fixed builds (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-05-13); every FortiGate except FIPS-CC models is exposed to the offline decryption step once its configuration has been downloaded unless private-data-encryption, available from FortiOS 5.6.11, 6.0.7 and 6.2.1 and off by default, is enabled with an operator-defined key, which Fortinet warns can cause install errors and split-brain on FortiManager-managed or HA FortiGates until FortiManager 6.2.7 and FortiGate 6.2.6, 6.4.4 or 6.6.0 and later (Group-IB, 2026-10-21; Fortinet, 2019-11-19).
Detection
On edge appliances, unexpected local administrator creation, configuration exports, trusted-host changes, repeated authentication failures, lockout-and-retry patterns and administration from unusual source addresses; on directory infrastructure, the NetExec, Impacket and relay pattern against domain controllers; on endpoints, remote-management agents and dual-use tools without an approved owner. The decryption leaves no trace on the appliance, so a patched or cleaned device may already have yielded its secrets (Group-IB, 2026-10-21). After upgrading FortiWeb, Fortinet advises reviewing configuration and logs for unexpected changes and unauthorised administrator accounts, and until then disabling HTTP and HTTPS on internet-facing interfaces (Fortinet, 2025-11-14).

Triage: OpenConnect, MeshCentral, Atera, AnyDesk and Rclone are legitimate tools, so Group-IB advises judging execution context, installation source, operator account, destination and timing rather than tool names (Group-IB, 2026-10-21).

Defender takeaway
Enable private-data-encryption with an operator-defined key on every FortiGate and rotate the directory and administrator secrets stored in any configuration that may have left the device, because patching or rebuilding does not undo a copy already decrypted; Group-IB also advises investigating lockout events and raising the lockout time against brute force (Group-IB, 2026-10-21).

Builds on: 2026-05-30/cve-2026-0257-palo-alto-pan-os-globalprotect-pre-auth-authen · 2026-06-18/fortibleed-73-932-internet-facing-fortigate-devices-exposed
