CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)

First published 2026-10-14 · open finding →

Update17 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceactionsbody

Microsoft's Exchange Team now gives a workaround for the instability that the October 2026 Windows Server updates can cause on Exchange servers: it advises against uninstalling them and says setting the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and rebooting has solved the cases it assisted. It adds that DAG members losing quorum are among the reported symptoms and that the Exchange security updates are not the cause.

Microsoft's Exchange Team has published guidance for Exchange servers that become unstable after the October 2026 Windows Server updates. Since 2026-10-13 it has seen reports of OWA failing with MapiExceptionMdbOffline (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142; event ID 1006 in the Application log), mail queues growing during the day, DAG members unable to reach quorum and a reboot helping only temporarily; Exchange 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition can all be affected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17). It says the issues are not related to installing the October 2026 Exchange security updates and that any Exchange version running on an affected Windows build can be hit; KB5126646 (Windows Server 2025), KB5126655 (2022), KB5126651 (2019) and KB5126868 (2016) can cause the failures after some time, and the impact varies with Exchange load, so some servers may never see a problem (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Microsoft's recommendation is not to uninstall the October 2026 Windows Server updates and, from an elevated command prompt on the Exchange server, to set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc to 65536, reboot, monitor, and raise the limit if the problem recurs; it says this has solved the customer cases it has assisted (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Sources: Microsoft Security Response Center · Microsoft Exchange Team

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

First published 2026-10-09 · open finding →

Update17 Oct 2026 03:35 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH), the City of Zurich's pension fund, has moved from checking to confirming. Its notice of 2026-10-15 says its inquiries so far indicate that personal data of PKZH insured persons was also stolen in the attack, and that this data had been used in tests for the planned system switch (PKZH, 2026-10-15); its FAQ adds that data was taken from PK Softech's system, including personal data of insured persons and of pensioners (PKZH, 2026-10-15). Inside IT reports that PKZH currently uses another software provider and plans to move to PK Softech's system in 2027 (Inside IT, 2026-10-16); PKZH's own FAQ says the system it uses to manage assets and pay pensions is not affected and dates the move to the beginning of 2027 (PKZH, 2026-10-15). The page still carries its earlier line that PKZH is checking whether its data is affected next to the confirmation (PKZH, 2026-10-15). It says a switch of this kind has to be tested with data that reproduces the real pension relationships as completely as possible, that PK Softech is contractually bound to protect and keep the data confidential, and that whether it met that duty is being investigated (PKZH, 2026-10-15).

Which data was stolen is still being clarified; in the worst case the fields are first name, name, date of birth, AHV number, address, private and business e-mail and telephone, insured earnings and retirement assets, civil status, partner details and IBAN (PKZH, 2026-10-15). PKZH was told on 2026-10-13 that data of its insured persons might be affected, has filed a criminal complaint and has reported the incident to the data-protection office (PKZH, 2026-10-15). It says a payout needs a signed written request and an identity check and that a change of bank details is checked additionally, so the data alone cannot trigger one, but that criminals can use it to appear credible (PKZH, 2026-10-15).

Pensionskasse Post's notice of 2026-10-15 says the investigation has shown that personal data did leave, and that it remains unclear whether data of its insured persons is affected, though that is possible (Pensionskasse Post, 2026-10-15). It does not repeat its earlier statement that its data at PK Softech is anonymised, and lists name, address, date of birth, AHV number, contact details, e-mail address and pension data as data that could be affected (Pensionskasse Post, 2026-10-15). The access vector, the actor and any ransom demand were not public in any source read as of that date.

Improvement17 Oct 2026 03:34 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencebody

The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.

The root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published on 2026-10-15 and rated High on GitHub's advisory database as GHSA-fhw5-mpvj-x89m (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15). Its description reads "Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.4 mishandles the manner in which the dsinvoked broker trusts DSCache configuration data, leading to privilege escalation to root, as exploited in the wild in October 2026." (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15), the same step Volexity describes as abusing the dsinvoked service's trust in the shared DSCache store (Volexity, 2026-10-13).

The record names only 22.8R2.4 as affected and states no fixed build; Volexity wrote that Ivanti was working on a fix for release in the coming weeks (Volexity, 2026-10-13), and no source read says whether any build now fixes it. First published 2026-10-06 · open finding →

Update17 Oct 2026 03:34 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Atlassian, the assigner, rejected the CVE record for CVE-2026-21589 on 2026-10-16, giving only the generic reason that its publication may have been a false positive or a mistake; ENISA's EUVD record mirrors it and still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15. Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID with the same fixed versions, and no source says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow, so tooling keyed on the ID can lose track of an exploited flaw.

ENISA's EUVD record EUVD-2026-92807 for CVE-2026-21589, which names Atlassian as the assigner, was updated at 20:39 UTC on 2026-10-16 and now describes the record only as "This CVE's publication may have been a false positive or a mistake. As a result, we have rejected this record." (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16). The same record still lists exploitation since 2026-10-15 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16).

The flaw itself is unchanged: Atlassian's advisory, as read on 2026-10-17, still uses the ID, lists the same fixed versions and carries no note of the rejection (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). No source read says why the record was rejected or whether a replacement ID will follow. The consequence is for tooling: a scanner plugin, SIEM enrichment rule or ticket keyed on the ID, or on a feed that drops rejected IDs, can stop reporting a flaw that is exploited, so track it by Atlassian's advisory and the fixed versions above until a replacement ID appears.

  • borderline-drop: DD-Automation (S2; Safepay claim) - a sub-supplier of the contractor that runs the conveyor technology at the Army logistics base; the Army says no interfaces exist and site security is unaffected, the only source is Inside IT, and the one technique id (T1657) would rest on the leak-site claim alone.
  • borderline-drop: Eichstätt ransomware, the Berlin Landesnetz closure statement, Fehmarnbelt contractor FLC, the BAE-run US Bankruptcy Noticing Center outage (S2, S4) - incident floor: no vector, actor or behaviour beyond the impact, so no honest technique mapping. S3's Norwegian armed-forces rental-car lead was not followed: its primary was not reachable and it carries no Swiss nexus.
  • borderline-drop: alleged Qilin member extradited from Japan to Germany with the Synnovis attack folded into the case (S4) - a law-enforcement item with no reported change in the group's activity and no defender decision.
  • borderline-drop: GreyNoise proxyjacking, Symantec's Aoki infostealer, Forescout's ROMULUS (an update-of on the covered ChatGPT ClickFix entry with no new decision), Fox-IT's Cobalt Strike corpus, XBOW's Chrome chain (S3) - marginal for this constituency.

Single-source: the Exchange entry stays single-source (Microsoft is the vendor and the only observer); the AOMEI entry is multi-source (GTIG and METAL are independent first-hand observers) at B1. Reduced-confidence inclusions: none.

Contradictions: CVE-2026-111357's description says exploited in the wild in October 2026 while CISA's ADP data on the same CVE record says Exploitation none; the entry cites Volexity and the GitHub advisory text for the exploited status and does not repeat the CISA field because the CVE Services record is not a citable source. The PKZH page still carries the earlier line that it is checking whether its data is affected next to its confirmation; the entry reports the confirmation and the fields still being clarified.

Priority and ground calls: AOMEI is high rather than notable because GTIG names Switzerland among the victim countries and the decision is a hunt over a bounded period; it is not critical (no exploitation of a constituency system is shown and the vendor's servers are reported repaired). The Atlassian and Ivanti records leave priority unchanged (high, critical); the Exchange record leaves notable; PK Softech stays notable. The Next.js, NGINX, PwnEscape and Vghost drops follow the PD-11(b) limb: no exploitation signal and no mechanics that force the timeline. The Exchange update is update rather than improvement because Microsoft's workaround is a new vendor development, not a re-read of material already published.

Candidate sources: manageengine-metal added (S3), co-primary for the AOMEI entry; no feed exists, the landing page and reports read with extract. Not added: qurium, tencent-zhuque-lab, forescout-vedere-labs (S3; their items were dropped), br24-bayern (S2; no feed probed) and internet-watch-impress (S4; its only item was dropped), which the next audit may revisit. drupal-security promoted to active (promotion_due, three contributing runs). Recipe notes from the sub-agents' coverage gaps were folded into 25 source records, trail-of-bits moved from webfetch to its direct feed, and cash-ch-awp, the one UNSOLVED row of the health check, got a health_cmd on the news sitemap; the second health sweep reports 246 probed, 245 relevant and 1 stale, and no UNSOLVED row.

Rotation: slices were ranked on the rotation cursor; the previous two fires had attempted 109 records, and excluding them as a belt-and-braces removed 23, 23 and 29 candidates from the S1, S2 and S3 pools. S4's pool of breach sources had all been attempted by the previous two fires, so its 14 oldest by cursor were allocated anyway. All 21 essential records were attempted. The S3 slice carried 122 to 148 h lookbacks.

Coverage gaps: ivanti-advisory-hub (JavaScript shell on every transport, as in the previous fire), the BSI WID-SEC advisory page (an Angular shell; the CVE text came from the GitHub advisory page instead), the EUVD human page (an Angular shell; the rejection text is read from the record's data and is the one quote the gate could not machine-check), two metered-reader credits spent when extract fell through to the reader for BeyondTrust and Wordfence pages (S1), databreaches-net posts (reader fallback), fuitesinfos and hackernews (listing windows shorter than the lookback). No other unrecovered failure.

Verification loop: three cold passes of the single verifier definition, findings per iteration 22, 11 and 5 (truth 9, 4 and 2), all remediated or declined with a reason in the record. Iteration 1 corrected an attribution of METAL's reproduction, a missing citation per clause on PK Softech, a stale PaperCut fixed-version statement (the September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11) and two run-record counts; iteration 2 found a stray template token in the AOMEI Triage line and a handful of hedges. Iteration 3 returned NEEDS_FIXES with two low-confidence one-clause truth findings (a Previdian timeline time on the Atlassian entry and a lines-versus-sections count on the AOMEI entry) and no F1 or F4, so under the early-exit rule both were applied and the run publishes without a fourth pass; verification_residual_count is 2 for that reason. Declined with reasons: PK Softech priority stays notable, the long sourcing notes and the PK Softech consolidation are left for the audit, and the actor-chosen task names stay as behavioural anchors.

Dates and telemetry: GTIG's AOMEI page carries 2026-10-15 in its JSON-LD and visible dateline but a page-meta published_time of 2026-10-16T21:02Z, and The Hacker News reported it on 2026-10-16; the entry cites it as 2026-10-16 and the window gate passes on that date. S2's return header counts 27 web searches and 130 bridge fetches, its findings file 24 and 120; the header is recorded in sub_agents.

Operational notes: files over 1 MB under work/2026-10-17T0256Z-intel/ (S1's 47 MB Microsoft October CVRF working copy, two copies of the CISA KEV JSON and the quote-check page bodies) were deleted before commit; all are re-fetchable public data and the findings that used them are in the findings files. Stop-hook nudges to commit arrived repeatedly mid-run and were not acted on (nothing is committed before Phase 6). A background-job cd in one deep-read command ran three fetches from the wrong directory; they were re-run with absolute paths. Entry timestamps were set from the container clock, which was re-read before each record.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-16
item.description:
• BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset. BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown. Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30, and a Metasploit module now implements the chain. →
  • Unit 42: a memory-resident FortiGate implant rides an exploited FortiOS flaw that has no fix on 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4. Unit 42 describes a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as CL-STA-0954 (UNC5820), that began with the FortiManager flaw CVE-2024-47575, exfiltrated the configurations and cryptographic material of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and later used the FortiOS CLI auto-script path traversal CVE-2025-61624 to install PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 implant that patches the logging and IPsec daemons in memory and leaves no persistent binary on disk. Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 lists CVE-2025-61624 as known exploited and gives no fix for FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, only a move to a fixed release, so those branches stay exposed to an attacker who already holds a privileged administrator account. →
  • Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit with PHP prepend persistence, a sudo password trap and mail searches. Unit 42 reports CL-UNK-1211, a cluster of unknown nation-state or criminal affiliation that between October 2025 and April 2026 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, focusing on Linux servers to run reconnaissance and keep persistent access for intelligence collection. Its scripts carry AI-style reasoning comments, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work; the intrusions used PHP web shells with auto_prepend_file persistence on Plesk hosts, a replaced .bashrc that traps sudo passwords, SUID root shells, searches of mail directories and log cleanup. Unit 42 names no victim or country, does not say how the web shells were first placed, and is the only source. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset. BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown. Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30, and a Metasploit module now implements the chain. →
  2. 02Unit 42: a memory-resident FortiGate implant rides an exploited FortiOS flaw that has no fix on 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4. Unit 42 describes a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as CL-STA-0954 (UNC5820), that began with the FortiManager flaw CVE-2024-47575, exfiltrated the configurations and cryptographic material of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and later used the FortiOS CLI auto-script path traversal CVE-2025-61624 to install PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 implant that patches the logging and IPsec daemons in memory and leaves no persistent binary on disk. Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 lists CVE-2025-61624 as known exploited and gives no fix for FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, only a move to a fixed release, so those branches stay exposed to an attacker who already holds a privileged administrator account. →
  3. 03Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit with PHP prepend persistence, a sudo password trap and mail searches. Unit 42 reports CL-UNK-1211, a cluster of unknown nation-state or criminal affiliation that between October 2025 and April 2026 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, focusing on Linux servers to run reconnaissance and keep persistent access for intelligence collection. Its scripts carry AI-style reasoning comments, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work; the intrusions used PHP web shells with auto_prepend_file persistence on Plesk hosts, a replaced .bashrc that traps sudo passwords, SUID root shells, searches of mail directories and log cleanup. Unit 42 names no victim or country, does not say how the web shells were first placed, and is the only source. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 2Updates to prior coverage 8Action items 12

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLECVE-2025-61624exploitedNATOB2

PEERSTITCH: a memory-resident FortiGate implant installed through the FortiOS CLI path traversal CVE-2025-61624, which Fortinet lists as exploited and leaves unfixed on FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, after a FortiManager compromise exposed the configurations of 500+ firewalls

Unit 42 investigated a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as cluster CL-STA-0954, that began with CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance: the attackers registered a rogue virtual FortiGate, then exfiltrated an archive with the running configurations, cryptographic material and database files of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42 recovered the configurations' reversible-ciphertext credentials by brute force; the attackers later logged in over SSL VPN with legitimate credentials and pushed packet-capture settings to downstream firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

For root they used CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal in the FortiOS CLI system.auto-script engine that lets an authenticated administrative account read and write arbitrary files as root (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). That installed PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 injector that attaches with ptrace to the logging daemon miglogd and the IPsec daemon iked, allocates a 16 KB read-write-execute region, NOP-patches three fixed offsets and links the daemons through /proc memory so that tagged VPN sessions skip default FortiOS validation; it leaves no persistent binary on disk, opens no listening port and makes no outbound connection of its own (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Command and control ran through the firewall's own Apache mod_md ACME module, whose DNS-01 challenge handler executes Node.js with parameters from an attacker-run ACME server and so opens a reverse shell (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 covers the CLI path traversal in FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager, lists it as known exploited, and for FortiOS gives fixes only in 7.6.5 and 7.4.10, telling users of 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4 to migrate to a fixed release (Fortinet, 2026-04-14).

Exposure
FortiOS on 7.2, 7.0 or 6.4, which have no fixed build, or on 7.6.0 to 7.6.4 and 7.4.0 to 7.4.9, with administrators who can reach the CLI (Fortinet, 2026-04-14); and a FortiManager below 7.6.1, 7.4.5, 7.2.8, 7.0.13, 6.4.15 or 6.2.13 that is reachable on TCP 541 from untrusted networks, where the intrusion began (Fortinet, 2024-10-23; Unit 42, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Management-plane audit records of the FortiManager (device registrations, archive creation, TCP 541 sessions from outside the management network); FortiGate administrator and VPN logs for SSL VPN logins with valid credentials from new external addresses and for administrator accounts that match nobody in the estate, such as an unexpected FortiGateCloud account; gaps in forwarded syslog, because the actors stop the logging daemons before running scripts; and unexplained packet-capture settings (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42's hunting guidance adds the memory maps of miglogd and iked (anonymous 16,384-byte rwxp regions), text-segment integrity at three fixed offsets, cross-process open and write on /proc/<pid>/mem, signal-11 crashes of miglogd, iked or syslogd in the crash log, and configuration revisions holding auto-script objects with ../ in the name (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Triage: legitimate FortiManager work also creates and deletes auto-scripts and adds devices; the report's signals are ../ in an auto-script name, a device registered from outside the management network, and accounts that match no administrator or tenant the organization created.

Defender takeaway
Plan the move off FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, where Fortinet offers no fix for an exploited root escalation (Fortinet, 2026-04-14), and limit who can reach the administrative CLI meanwhile; after any suspected FortiManager compromise treat every managed device's credentials and certificates as compromised and rotate them, because the stolen trust material stays valid until it is rotated (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: 2026-06-18/fortibleed-73-932-internet-facing-fortigate-devices-exposed

threat16 Oct 04:22Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-26-122) · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-24-423)
NOTABLENATOB2

CL-UNK-1211: an AI-assisted intrusion set against government Linux web and mail servers persists through PHP auto_prepend_file, steals sudo passwords with a fake prompt and reads mail stores, and tries to pass as a red-team exercise

Unit 42 reports a campaign it tracks as CL-UNK-1211 (UNK: affiliation undetermined) against government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, concentrating on Linux servers for persistent access and intelligence collection (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). It names no victim or country and does not say how the web shells were first placed; the recovered tools include a custom Go scanner for CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). The scripts carry conversational, step-by-step comments in the style of an AI model, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work, an inference rather than a confirmed finding (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

On the hosts, the attackers ran PHP web shells under the php-fpm parent process and rewrote auto_prepend_file in every PHP configuration under /etc/php/ and /opt/plesk/php/, so a planted file runs first (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They replaced a .bashrc with a copy that, in one instance, aliases sudo to a fake password prompt that logs the input, searched configuration and history files for credentials, escalated with LinPEAS and the public PwnKit exploit (CVE-2021-4034), left root-SUID shells under hidden names and injected an SSH key into authorized_keys (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They moved laterally with sshpass and hard-coded credentials and through an MSSQL double hop using xp_cmdshell, and kept access with SysGoRAT, a Go trojan that takes commands over WebSocket, plus the revsocks and pysoxy proxies and GSocket's gs-netcat, which ran from /dev/shm under a fake kernel-thread process name (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). On government mail servers they enumerated /var/qmail/mailnames/, counted mails in Maildir folders to pick targets and searched mail headers for social-media messages; they tried to exfiltrate database dumps over netcat and to public file-hosting platforms, to delete authentication, history, mail and system logs and to kill endpoint security processes, timestomped scripts with touch -t, and planted a red-team marker string and a pentest-style password to pass as an authorised exercise (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Linux web and mail hosting estates of government or state-affiliated bodies, in particular Plesk-managed PHP stacks and their /var/qmail/mailnames/ mail directories, which the attackers enumerated and searched; the report does not say how the attackers got in (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).
Detection
From the described behaviour: file-integrity monitoring on PHP configuration directories for any auto_prepend_file that points outside the application tree; shells or interpreters spawned by php-fpm or web server workers; writes to shell startup files, authorized_keys and any new sudo alias; PHP or web-server access to the mail store; new systemd units, five-minute cron entries and hidden-name SUID-root binaries; outbound WebSocket, GSocket or file-hosting connections from servers; touch -t changes, bursts of deleted history and mail logs, and pkill sequences that name EDR agents.

Triage: Plesk or PHP hardening can legitimately set auto_prepend_file and administrators do define sudo aliases; the report supports these discriminators: a prepended file with a vendor-like name outside the application tree, an alias that prompts for and logs the password, a log file named after another product, and red-team marker strings that no change record explains.

Defender takeaway
Audit every PHP configuration for auto_prepend_file, privileged accounts' startup files for a sudo alias and authorized_keys for unknown keys, and the file system for root-SUID binaries under hidden names; ship authentication, mail and web logs off-host so local log cleanup cannot erase them; patch PwnKit and keep Linux EDR self-protection alerting.
threat16 Oct 04:21Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42
NOTABLENATOB2

AdFection: Citizen Lab and Confiant document zero-click Candiru spyware delivered through targeted online ads from the ad-tech firm Discover-Tech, with ad impressions on defence-ministry, armed-forces and NATO networks

Citizen Lab reports that in 2024 and 2025 at least 45 devices at the news network Al Jazeera were targeted in zero-click attacks that it links with high confidence to Candiru spyware delivered through ads bought by Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm that presents itself as an ad company (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). An ad carries a script tag that calls Discover-Tech's ad-decision server with the user's cookie or mobile advertising identifier; the server decides, apparently from the source address and the identifiers, whether the device is eligible, and returns JavaScript only if so and a zero-byte response otherwise, which keeps malicious code and pointers to it out of what ad vendors can inspect (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). In Al Jazeera's network logs an infected device first contacted Discover-Tech infrastructure, which indicates an ad impression, then a Candiru validator server that checks the device, and finally a Candiru command-and-control server; a Windows implant that Al Jazeera isolated from a compromised device and Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant, working from ad-delivery telemetry from April to September 2026, describes a cloaked payload that fingerprints the device and opens an encrypted channel, and found a hand-off to Candiru-attributed infrastructure, with Belgium by far the most targeted country at 56 percent of the global hits in the period; it has not captured a full exploit chain (Confiant, 2026-10-15).

Citizen Lab's analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows ads on almost 200,000 websites and apps in four months, including on devices in networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and intergovernmental organizations such as NATO; an impression alone does not prove targeting or infection (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle (Liftoff) and Eskimi disconnected Discover-Tech after the disclosure (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Any device that renders third-party ads in a browser or an app, on staff whose phones or workstations an espionage buyer would want, such as defence, security and diplomatic staff; no source reports an infection in Switzerland, and neither report mentions it (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).
Detection
In per-device web-proxy, DNS and egress logs the reported signature is contact with Discover-Tech infrastructure, which marks an ad impression, followed by a connection to a validator server and finally to a command-and-control server, the sequence seen in Al Jazeera's network logs (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant adds that the ad-delivered SDK resolves an operator-chosen domain over DNS-over-HTTPS and reaches it by raw IP, so it never appears as a plaintext DNS query or connection hostname and stays invisible to DNS-based monitoring and blocklists (Confiant, 2026-10-15). On a Windows endpoint, the implant Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking, so a new COM registration that points at an unfamiliar DLL is the artifact to look for.

Triage: ordinary ad tags also call identifier-bearing endpoints and sync user IDs; the reported discriminators are the eligibility gating, with an empty reply for ineligible devices and code only for chosen ones, and the validator-then-command-and-control sequence (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
The delivery is zero-click and needs no user action, and Citizen Lab says there is currently no consistently safe way to expose users and networks to targeted ads; its control is to block online advertising at the organization's gateway and on work-issued and edge devices (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).
threat16 Oct 04:19Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Citizen Lab · Confiant

02Trending vulnerabilities2 items

CRITICALCVE-2026-102764exploitedupdatedNATOB1

CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation (CWE-290) in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; every version up to 26.2.3 is affected (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). Google's Threat Intelligence Group found in an incident response that ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited the flaw as a zero-day in late August 2026 (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust dates the exploitation of one hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance to 2026-08-29 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). GTIG warns that ARMORY CASTLE and others have historically exploited broadly once a flaw is public (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust lists government among the actor's documented targets (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). On 2026-10-30 Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis in which one forged message makes an internal file-transfer service write a PHP file into the site's public directory, run as the site's operating-system user, and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain (Rapid7, 2026-10-30).

After the exploit GTIG saw SAWFLY, a lightweight PHP web shell that evaluates attacker-supplied code as the appliance's unprivileged site account; the actor then made a root-owned SUID copy of the system shell, tried to dump the appliance's native secrets vault, and persisted through a boot-time script that adds a passwordless-sudo line to the sudoers template, so the escalation survives reboot and configuration reset (GTIG, 2026-10-15). It deleted appliance logs throughout, raised an account's Jump Item and Team permissions from No Access to Administrator, and exposed BARECLAW, a custom SOCKS5-over-WebSocket tunneler, by editing the HAProxy configuration (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Self-hosted Remote Support appliances on any version up to 26.2.3 without the BT26-05-RS patch; apply the patch manually unless the instance is subscribed to automatic updates in its /appliance interface, and a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). SaaS tenants were patched by 2026-10-09 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust says its patch was built and tested for Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access, though its advisory names only Remote Support as impacted (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The actor deletes on-appliance logs, so use other copies: forwarded syslog for user changes that raise a Jump Item or Team role to Administrator and for account or API-account changes without a change ticket; authentication logs for administrative /login success from residential-broadband or commercial-VPN address space; reverse-proxy or WAF logs for unknown .php paths and WebSocket upgrades from non-support addresses; file transfers by accounts whose roles changed (GTIG, 2026-10-15). Rapid7's successful request was an extensionless URL, since the web server answers a direct .php request with 404, so a rule that matches only .php requests misses it (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Patching does not evict the actor, so GTIG advises redeploying any appliance of confirmed or unknown status from a clean, fully patched image and rotating credentials in dependency order (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Triage: an administrator changing Jump Item roles or signing in from a new network under a change ticket is routine; BeyondTrust's signal is a privileged session from a residential or VPN address tied to no administrator or ticket (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
Patch every self-hosted appliance now, then treat each one that was internet-reachable on an affected build since late August as potentially compromised until reviewed, and redeploy from a clean image any whose status is confirmed or unknown (GTIG, 2026-10-15).
Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain, with PHP and Unix Command targets (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). An anonymous customer session, started through the public customer connection, sends a message whose source address carries a reserved local router ID; the appliance's customer worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component, which exposes an internal file-transfer service with its native filesystem provider. Rapid7 used it to write a PHP file into the site's public directory and ran it as the site's operating-system user (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). The successful request was an extensionless URL, because the web server answers a direct .php request with 404 and maps an extensionless URL to the existing file, so detection that only searches for requests ending in .php would miss it; the appliance's thin-scc logs record file-transfer stream creation and rejected requests (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Rapid7 tested Remote Support 24.1.2 and says other affected releases and fixed builds have not been established; BeyondTrust's advisory remains the reference for affected and fixed versions (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Builds on: 2026-07-08/beyondtrust-rs-pra-preauth-bypass-cve-2026-40138-cluster · 2026-06-05/verdantbamboo-unc5221-warp-panda-an-18-month-china-nexus-int

vulnerability16 Oct 04:16Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant · BeyondTrust (advisory BT26-05) · BeyondTrust (blog) · Rapid7
NOTABLECVE-2026-108097 +1NATOA2

CVE-2026-108097, Drupal core (SA-CORE-2026-014): a critical Field UI code-execution flaw reachable through contributed modules, at least one without login; fixed in 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19, with no fix for end-of-life branches (Drupal risk 19/25)

The Drupal Security Team's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 rates CVE-2026-108097 Critical, 19 out of 25 on Drupal's own scale, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module: the vulnerability is not directly exploitable with core alone, but multiple serious exploit paths exist with contributed modules and at least one known path needs no authentication (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14). The advisory names no module that opens a path; The Hacker News reads the mechanism from the fix, where Field UI's table element ran whatever PHP callable each row carried in its #region_callback property through call_user_func_array with no check, bypassing the renderer's rule against untrusted callbacks, and 11.4.10 no longer calls it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Fixed releases are Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below, and Drupal 8 and 9 are end of life and get no fix, which The Hacker News counts at 28.5 percent of the sites reporting a core version in the week of 2026-10-04 (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The advisory records no public exploit at publication, but the Security Team's pre-announcement of 2026-10-12 told sites to reserve time "because exploits might be developed within hours or days", and in May Drupal reported exploit attempts within two days of a core SQL injection advisory that CISA then added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The contributed Entity List module has its own critical code-execution advisory, SA-CONTRIB-2026-218, under the same conditions, at least one known path needing no authentication, and 3.0.10 fixes it (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14); the flaw is CVE-2026-108099, and updating core does not update the module (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Drupal core on 10.6.x below 10.6.19, 11.3.x below 11.3.19 or 11.4.x below 11.4.10, or on an end-of-life branch from 8.9 to 11.2, with the Field UI module installed (the Standard install profile installs it) and a contributed module or custom code that exposes the vulnerable functionality, which the advisory does not name; Drupal Steward, a web application firewall service run by Acquia, Pantheon, Ironstar and Skpr, blocks some known vectors but not every one (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The advisory publishes no exploit artifact. The result of the flaw is PHP code running as the web server's user, so as an inference from that, watch web access logs for unusual requests to routes that contributed modules provide, PHP worker process lineage for shells, curl or interpreters spawned by the web server, and new or modified PHP files under the web root and the Drupal files directory. An exposed site updated only after the fix was public needs that file-integrity review in addition to the update.
Defender takeaway
Update core to the fixed release of its branch now, internet-facing sites first, because the flaw's mechanism is readable from the public fix and Drupal itself warned that exploits could follow within hours or days; where a site cannot be updated at once, uninstall Field UI, which removes the field management and display admin pages until the update (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). Custom code that set #region_callback on a field_ui_table row stops working after the update, so test the manage fields and manage display pages (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Verification & coverage notes

Window: gap 24.0 h from 2026-10-15T0256Z-intel, window 26 h, developing-story window 72 h; the container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s). Five new entries (BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-102764 critical; Drupal core SA-CORE-2026-014 high; AdFection, CL-UNK-1211 and PEERSTITCH notable) and eight changelog records, seven update and one improvement (the Exchange OWA caveat, which does not re-float its entry): PAN-OS 11.2.16 published; the CISA KEV listing of the Atlassian flaw; the AhsayCBS hotfixes, KEV listing and Bitdefender MDR intrusions (notable to high); CERT-FR's lateral-movement alert on Ivanti Connect Secure; Microsoft's Exchange outage notice after the October Windows updates; the police fraud-call warning and BVK statement on PK Softech; IDC Frontier's fifth report; Sansec's BlockStrap reproduction for the Adobe October entry. No deep dive: nothing cleared the bar. The previous record's publish_status is ok.

Operational event: a container restart at about 03:16Z killed the first S1 to S4 spawns 19 minutes in. S3 had written six valid items; S1, S2 and S4 had only progress lines. All four were re-spawned as resumptions with incremental findings writes, each carrying its progress lines as leads; the sub_agents blocks show the original started_at and the final ended_at, so durations span the restart. One continuation per domain was not needed afterwards. The main-agent clock stayed correct (verified after the restart).

KEV sweep (work/2026-10-16T0256Z-intel/kev-window.txt): one addition in the window, CVE-2026-21589 (Atlassian), COVERED. Its entry stated attempts only and said in a dated section that the flaw was not in KEV, so the listing shipped as an update record (PD-13 exploitation-status change). No RANSOMWARE rows. The AhsayCBS pair (KEV 2026-10-14, covered as exploited by the 2026-10-15 fire) needed an update for a different reason: Ahsay's own hotfixes and its admission that the earlier patches were incomplete, which the entry still described as "no fixed release named".

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): the one open row, Beyond Gravity, was re-gated with a dated note appended. SRF reports (single outlet, anonymous sources, 2026-10-15) that the company and the Confederation assume China is the attacker, and the Council of States' oversight committee chair said the committees were told of a data outflow; the company says the origin is not confirmed. S4 recommended a short notable entry and S2 left the choice to the main agent. Held instead on two grounds, relevance first: with no vector, behaviour or data class public there is no exposure test, detection or hunting step a Tier 2/3 reader could take from an entry, so under PD-11 it is a headline rather than actionable knowledge; and no evidence-bound ATT&CK mapping exists, so an incident entry would FAIL the gate's non-empty techniques[] rule; the row expires 2026-10-20 and is struck then unless a vector, behaviour or data class is named.

Its transferable lesson (a multi-tenant alerting supplier is a single point of failure) is not yet a decision.
  • borderline-drop: Juniper October 2026 Junos bundle, 23 of about 154 CVEs at CVSS 9.0 or above including three unauthenticated J-Web authentication bypasses and an httpd overflow (S1), no exploitation per Juniper SIRT, exposure needs web management configured, the vendor pages are a JavaScript shell; the 2026-10-15 fire made the same call.
  • borderline-drop: Nutanix CVE-2026-84731 (pre-auth cluster-admin bypass on port 9440, fixed in AOS and Prism Central 7.6.0.8, 7.5.2, 7.3.1.18; PoC validated at disclosure, none public), Znuny CVE-2026-93483 (fixed since 2026-09-16, applies only where the HTTPBasicAuth backend is configured), Splunk CVE-2026-76268 (Patroni REST API on search head cluster members), Next.js out-of-band RCEs (narrow preconditions, two without CVE), AnyDesk Linux CVE-2026-109390 (public exploit, direct TCP/7070 only, fixed 2026-06-23, no exploitation), Windows DNS CVE-2026-62878 (DoS-only PoC), Fortinet FortiSandbox and FortiSIEM (Known Exploited No; dropped on 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15) (S1), none exploited, none an out-of-band decision on its own mechanics; re-gate on exploitation or a public exploit.
  • borderline-drop: PwnEscape CVE-2026-99999, a Linux kernel guest-to-host escape (S3), local vector inside a guest, a lab result, fixed in stable kernels, no exploitation reported.
  • borderline-drop: FortiBleed Swiss exposure scan (S2; one trade-press relay, reachable interfaces not compromises), QuartzLine (S3; no public Mandiant document, second source an AI-agent-authored blog), KELA's Silent Ransom Group chat analysis (S3; authenticity unverified), the swarmcha.se Tencent agent fleet (S3; no constituency nexus), YAM Store, ARTEX and UAT-6275 (S3; dropped by the 2026-10-15 fire on the same facts), the Microsoft October Patch Tuesday residual (S1; none exploited, the five Outlook preview-pane RCEs rated Exploitation Less Likely), Le Tampon Qilin claim, Park Dental 8-K (S4).
  • Left out of the PK Softech update: Stiftung FAR (S4, S2). Inside IT lists it as a potential victim, blue News relays CH Media that FAR's IT partner is a different provider than Publica's, FAR is a private foundation and its own notice was not found (bzbasel.ch is 403 on the direct, extract and reader transports).

Single-source: 2026-10-16/cl-unk-1211-ai-assisted-intrusions-government-linux-hosts and 2026-10-16/peerstitch-fortigate-implant-cve-2025-61624-fortimanager are single-source (Unit 42 is the only observer; PEERSTITCH also cites Fortinet's own advisory for the CVE) at B2. Reduced-confidence inclusions: none.

Contradictions: Ivanti's affected 25.x line differs between sources (Rapid7 and the entry: 25.1.2.2 and prior; the Canadian Cyber Centre: 25.2.2 and prior; CERT-FR lists only the 25.1.1.x and 25.1.3.x lines); Ivanti's own advisory is a JavaScript shell on every transport, so the entry discloses the difference instead of picking a side. The AhsayCBS announcement is dated 2026-10-12 in the page markup, though the extractor drops that dateline and reports a stale 2023 meta date; Huntress dates the hotfixes to the same day.

Priority and ground calls: BeyondTrust is critical on the bar (exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-nexus actor, unauthenticated, remote-support appliance, persistence survives reboot and configuration reset, GTIG expects broad exploitation, patch available); Drupal is high although unexploited because the Security Team's own pre-announcement warns of exploits within hours or days, the flaw has a known unauthenticated path and Drupal is the CMS behind many public-sector sites; PEERSTITCH stays notable because CVE-2025-61624 needs an administrator account and the intrusion is from 2024, although Fortinet lists the flaw as known exploited and has no fix for FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4; PEERSTITCH was published 2026-10-14 about 3 h before the window and is first coverage (Unit 42 was in no earlier slice). AhsayCBS moves to high: KEV-listed, the vendor's patches were incomplete and the fix is partner-only. The Atlassian flaw was already high.

Candidate sources: drupal-security added (S1), its health flag cleared in the same run by switching the recipe to the all-advisories RSS feed. Not added: nutanix-security-advisories (the Nutanix item was dropped), noma-labs, rogueauthority-org and watch-impress (S3 and S4; recipes unverified or a low-reliability publisher), which the next audit may revisit. No promotion_due rows.

Rotation: the digest built; S1 to S3 slices were ranked on the rotation cursor and 91 records attempted by the previous two fires were excluded as a belt-and-braces. S4's pool of 13 breach sources had all been attempted by the previous two fires, so its 12 oldest by cursor were allocated anyway; the S3 slice carried 121 to 148 h lookbacks.

Coverage gaps: ibm-support-security-bulletins (no listing or feed reachable; the PSIRT blog feed is malformed XML), socket-dev-blog (no post list, feed 404), the Juniper support portal and hub.ivanti.com (JavaScript shells), bsi-de (the CSAF page WID-SEC-2026-3976 returned 404 although the RSS item exists), rapid7-research (malformed feed XML, not in a slice), citizen-lab (RSS lagged), the Beyond Gravity company release and the Stiftung FAR notice (not found), bzbasel.ch (403 on the direct, extract and reader transports) and linfo.re (403 on every transport).

Verification loop: eight cold passes of the single verifier definition, findings per iteration 29, 23, 10, 7, 5, 4, 6 and 3, all remediated or declined with a reason in the record; no pass returned CLEAN, so the loop ended at the iteration cap and the run publishes fail-open. Iteration 8 (full ledger, 259 of 259 claims answered) found one truth defect, a false clause in the Adobe sourcing note (the solution table rates both fixes priority 2, as the summary does), which was corrected through the entry's existing changelog record together with two telemetry mismatches in this record; those last corrections were verified by the main agent against Adobe's page and the sub-agent ledgers but not by a further cold pass, hence verification_residual_count: 1. Later passes found mainly run-record statements and low-confidence sourcing questions; the entries' claims were stable from iteration 5 on.

Operational notes: stop-hook nudges to commit arrived repeatedly mid-run and were not acted on (nothing is committed before Phase 6). tools/source_health.py printed one UNSOLVED row, drupal-security, fixed in the same run. The harness offers no TodoWrite tool, so the phase plan lived in these notes. Entry timestamps were re-set once after a clock check showed several changelog at values ahead of real time.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-15
item.description:
• Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update. Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780. →
  • Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it. CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected. →
  • Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 now published. Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround and the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet; 11.2.16, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, was published on 2026-10-15, so every train now has a fixed build. →
