TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update. Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780. →
  2. 02Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it. CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected. →
  3. 03Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 now published. Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround and the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet; 11.2.16, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, was published on 2026-10-15, so every train now has a fixed build. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 3Updates to prior coverage 2Action items 8

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLENATOB2

A fake WatchGuard VPN download site captures the SSL VPN server, login and password in the browser and then serves the genuine signed installer, leaving no malicious file for endpoint tools to flag

Huntress's SOC investigated an incident on 2026-10-07 in which an administrator at a managed service provider searched Bing for a WatchGuard VPN download with a typo in the query and clicked through the standard Bing result redirect to a lookalike site titled "WatchGuard Firebox VPN Client", which Huntress classes as search-engine poisoning rather than malvertising (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Choosing any download option opens a pop-up asking for Server, Login and Password; one unobfuscated JavaScript file of about 150 lines posts the typed values as JSON to a separate collector domain, tagged as the first or second attempt, and always rejects the first submission with an "incorrect data" message so that the victim types again or tries a second set of credentials (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Only after the second submission does the page fetch the real WatchGuard Mobile VPN with SSL installer from WatchGuard's own CDN, an Authenticode-signed file whose digest Huntress recomputed and found unmodified, so there is no trojanized installer or malicious DLL for endpoint defenses to flag (Huntress, 2026-10-13). The victim's browser history showed no download in the observed window, so Huntress judges the user probably did not finish both rounds but may have typed credentials in the first, and Managed Defender flagged the incident 21 seconds after the lookalike domain loaded (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Both domains were registered within the previous two months, few reputation engines flagged either as of 2026-10-08, and the lure domain was offline by 2026-10-13 (Huntress, 2026-10-13). Huntress places the iteration in a campaign that WatchGuard's Secplicity team described in January 2026 as lookalike download sites for WatchGuard, F5, Fortinet, SonicWall and Sophos clients, and that Microsoft tied in March 2026 to a financially motivated actor it tracks as Storm-2561; the new element is that the fake client is gone from the middle (Huntress, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
Administrators and users who find an SSL VPN client through a web search, as an administrator at a managed service provider did here; the lure here impersonates WatchGuard, and Huntress describes the same campaign against clients of five vendors (Huntress, 2026-10-13). The credentials of any VPN account typed into such a page, and the gateway address with them, are in the attacker's hands.
Detection
No malicious file or process reaches the endpoint, so the signal is in web proxy and DNS telemetry (a visit that arrives from a search-result redirect to a domain that is not the vendor's, followed by a JSON POST to a second, recently registered domain; Huntress's Managed Defender did flag the browsing activity) and in VPN gateway authentication logs; Huntress advises watching for SSL VPN logins from hosting providers, unfamiliar ASNs and countries where the account has never connected (Huntress, 2026-10-13).

Triage: a genuine VPN client also asks for server, login and password, but only inside the installed client at connect time; a browser form that collects the three values before any installer has run, on a domain that is not the vendor's, is the signal.

Defender takeaway
If a user typed VPN credentials into a page found through search, reset every affected account and treat the VPN endpoint those credentials belong to as known to the attacker; enforce multi-factor authentication on the VPN, and publish and bookmark the official client download links in internal documentation so staff do not search for them (Huntress, 2026-10-13).
threat15 Oct 03:43Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Huntress

02Trending vulnerabilities3 items

CRITICALCVE-2026-76519exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-76519, Cisco Secure Email Gateway: one crafted email attachment writes files and runs commands as root, exploited in the wild and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 9.8)

Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 describes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway: improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled lets an unauthenticated remote attacker who sends a crafted attachment through the device write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system and run commands as root, and Cisco rates it CVSS 3.1 9.8 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Cisco states that in October 2026 its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation, and that it has directly contacted Cisco Secure Email Cloud customers on whose devices indicators of possible compromise were identified (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14); CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA, 2026-10-14). Cisco gives no workaround; the fix is distributed through the Content Scanner Tools package for every supported AsyncOS release and needs no software upgrade or restart, and it is also in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780, while release 16.0 must migrate to a fixed release (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). It is the second exploited root-level flaw in this product in about four weeks: BleepingComputer notes that last month Cisco warned of CVE-2026-76461, which also lets unauthenticated remote attackers run commands as root (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
A physical or virtual Cisco Secure Email Gateway is exposed when both conditions hold: the File Reputation service is enabled and assigned to a mail policy (web interface, Mail Policies, Incoming or Outgoing Mail Policies, Advanced Malware Protection, "Enable File Reputation" ticked), and the Content Scanner Tools version, shown by the contentscannerstatus command, is earlier than 25.3.0.5525; Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected, and Cisco Secure Email Cloud Gateway customers need take no action (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The attack arrives as an email attachment passing through the appliance, so exposure does not depend on its management interface being reachable (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Start with the appliance's own logs: Cisco's self-check is grep "System Security" system_logs on each cluster member, which returns "Suspected compromise indicator was found", "Security scan did not complete" or "No compromise indicator was found" (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Cisco warns that an attacker with root may remove or hide evidence, so it also recommends cross-checking network and firewall logs outside the device for unexpected uploads from the appliance to external addresses or downloads from malicious addresses (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14); that is egress telemetry from the gateway's own addresses.
Defender takeaway
Confirm Content Scanner Tools 25.3.0.5525 or later on every gateway today, since automatic updates deliver it and only gateways with updates disabled need the manual update, and run the log check on every one; for a virtual appliance with a compromise indicator, Cisco says to keep forensic data before upgrading, because upgrading a compromised instance destroys it, then deploy a new virtual machine on a fixed release, rebuild the configuration without importing an old file and renew credentials and cryptographic material (a physical appliance goes to Cisco TAC), and strongly recommends restoring every member of a cluster that contains a compromised appliance, since the cluster's SSH private keys could be accessed (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: 2026-09-15/cve-2026-76461-cisco-secure-email-gateway-sqli-root-rce

vulnerability15 Oct 03:40Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Cisco PSIRT · BleepingComputer · CISA
HIGHCVE-2026-110447exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-110447, Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server (Nextcloud richdocumentscode app): an unauthenticated command injection in proxy.php, exploited in the wild to plant PHP web shells, fixed in 26.4.303 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Collabora's own advisory, published 2026-10-14, says users of Nextcloud with the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) can be vulnerable through proxy.php: a request can run an operating system command as the web server user, the attack works only while the built-in CODE server is not running (after a restart, an upgrade or a crash), and disabling the app is not sufficient, it must be upgraded to 26.4.303 or later or removed (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14). Users of end-of-life Nextcloud 29 or older should upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app, standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected, and the fix for CVE-2025-66208 does not prevent this flaw (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14). The GitHub Advisory Database record for CVE-2026-110447 says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-14). Field reports came first: on 2026-09-11 a hoster reported on the app's issue tracker that several Nextcloud servers running richdocumentscode 26.4.302 had been compromised since the previous day through requests to proxy.php that carried shell command substitution and an encoded path traversal, with base64 payloads decoded and run through a shell to create PHP web shells in the app directory; on one server the attacker then searched for password-manager databases and cryptocurrency-wallet files, and the reviewed requests showed no archiving or upload commands (issue 354, 2026-09-11). Other administrators report the same compromise, one noticing it because Nextcloud's integrity check failed on an unexpected PHP file (issue 354, 2026-09-11). A reply on the issue says the flaw affects only the Development Edition in the Built-in CODE Server mode that downloads a local AppImage, and a later one that leftover web-shell files must be removed after upgrading (issue 354, 2026-09-11). A Nextcloud forum post of 2026-10-03 told users to update, saying that as far as the poster knew no CVE existed (Nextcloud community forum, 2026-10-03).

Exposure
A Nextcloud server with the "Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server" app at 26.4.302 or older, including one patched for CVE-2025-66208; a restart, an upgrade or a crash that stops the built-in CODE server opens the window, and deactivating the app does not close it (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14).
Detection
In web access logs, requests to the app's proxy.php whose path carries $( command substitution and an encoded ..; in file telemetry, unexpected PHP files in the app directory, which Nextcloud's integrity check flagged on a compromised server; in process telemetry, the web server account starting a shell that decodes base64 and calls out with curl or wget to an external service (issue 354, 2026-09-11). The web shell survives the update, so the post-patch check is the same file and process search, and the reporter says secrets available to the web server account must be treated as potentially affected (issue 354, 2026-09-11).
Defender takeaway
Update the app to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that has it, because disabling it does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app (Collabora Online security advisory, 2026-10-14); then search for dropped PHP files and the request pattern back to at least early September 2026, and on a hit rotate whatever the web server account can read (issue 354, 2026-09-11).
vulnerability15 Oct 03:42Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Collabora Online security advisory · GitHub Advisory Database · CollaboraOnline/richdocumentscode issue 354 · Nextcloud community forum
HIGHCVE-2026-0322exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-0322, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS: code injection in the management interface gives an authenticated attacker root, exploited in very limited attacks and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS-B 8.6)

Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 describes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection (CWE-94) in the management interface of PAN-OS that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run arbitrary code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series); Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected and no special configuration is needed to be affected (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The advisory is tagged as attacked and says very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the management interface (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14), and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA, 2026-10-14). Palo Alto scores it CVSS-B 8.6 with a suggested urgency of highest, says the risk is highest when the management interface is reachable from the internet, and scores it 8.5 when access is restricted to a single jump box (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). It lists no workaround; Threat Prevention IDs 510046 and 510047 give limited coverage and only when management traffic is routed through a data-plane interface and decrypted, and Palo Alto warns that variations of the attack may not be detected (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Fixes ship per train; a unit on 11.2.14 or 11.2.15 had no fixed build when the advisory appeared, and 11.2.16, the fix for those two releases, was published on 2026-10-15 (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The advisory does not say how the attackers obtained the credentials the flaw requires, when exploitation began or who is behind it, and BleepingComputer says it asked Palo Alto when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to reach internal networks (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
Any PA-Series or VM-Series firewall or Panorama (virtual or M-Series) on PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 or 12.2 below the fixed build of its train, with no configuration needed; the exposure is greatest where the management interface accepts connections from outside trusted internal addresses (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). BleepingComputer reads the advisory as requiring existing credentials and network access to the management interface (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Look at authentication and administrator-change records on the management interface, and at inbound connections to the management address in upstream firewall or provider logs, for logins from unfamiliar sources; Palo Alto's advisory FAQ lists three source addresses associated with the limited exploit attempts to compare against (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). Root code execution means an upgrade does not evict an attacker who is already in, and the advisory gives no file or process artifact, so a device that was reachable from untrusted networks before the fix needs a compromise assessment as well as the patch.
Defender takeaway
Take the management interface off every network but trusted internal addresses, with a jump box as the tightest setting Palo Alto describes, and upgrade to the fixed build of each train; units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15 upgrade to 11.2.16, which Palo Alto published on 2026-10-15 (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14).
Update16 Oct 2026 04:08 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvesevidenceactionsbody

Palo Alto Networks published 11.2.16 on 2026-10-15, the fixed build for units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15, which had none when the advisory appeared; its solution table now reads "Upgrade to 11.2.16 or later" for those two releases and every other train keeps the fixed builds already listed (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14). The advisory's exploitation status is unchanged at very limited exploitation, and it still lists no workaround (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: 2026-05-30/cve-2026-0257-palo-alto-pan-os-globalprotect-pre-auth-authen

vulnerability15 Oct 03:41Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Palo Alto Networks PSIRT · BleepingComputer · CISA

03Updates to prior coverage2 items

HIGHexploitedupdatedNATOA2

Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost reported at hundreds of French supermarkets; CERT-FR and NCSC Switzerland say to remove internet exposure

First published 2026-10-13 · open finding →

Improvement15 Oct 2026 03:49 UTCrun 2026-10-15T0256Z-intelsourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

Censys, which scans for Danfoss StoreView control panels, says Danfoss has not confirmed the initial access vector and points to three AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier: CVE-2025-41450 (March 2025), which Censys describes as letting an unauthenticated actor log in as an administrator with a code computed from the current calendar date, and CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452 (August 2025), which it says let authenticated users run commands and disrupt the management interface (Censys, 2026-10-14). Censys maps the firmware by build: below 4.2 carries all three, 4.2.4 fixes only the date-based login and still carries the two later ones, and 4.3.1 or later fixes all three (Censys, 2026-10-14). Its scan counted 1,825 exposed StoreView panels in France on 2026-10-11 and 537 on 2026-10-14, a fall of 71 percent, with builds below 4.2, build 4.2.4 and builds from 4.3.1 leaving at about the same rate, which it reads as operators taking controllers off the internet rather than patching them (Censys, 2026-10-14). Outside France the count fell from 1,166 to 966, and in ten of the twelve countries with the most exposed hosts more than 60 percent of the hosts run a build below 4.3.1, led by Poland at 81 percent and Romania at 80 percent (Censys, 2026-10-14).

Sources: CERT-FR (alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012) · AFP · BFMTV · Infosecurity Magazine · BleepingComputer · CERT-FR (alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012, revised version) · NCSC Switzerland (Security Hub advisory 13054) · Cooling Post · Blick · Censys · CERT-FR (alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012, third version) · Dixell France (Copeland) · Le Monde · SecurityWeek · Cybersecurity Dive · Public Sénat · Le Monde Informatique · Forescout Research (Vedere Labs)
HIGHupdatedNATOA2

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

First published 2026-10-09 · open finding →

Update15 Oct 2026 03:48 UTCrun 2026-10-15T0256Z-intelsourcesevidencesourcing_noteactions

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, says on 2026-10-13 that it currently uses another provider, plans to move to PK Softech's system in early 2027 and is checking whether data from migration tests was affected. Publica's page says as of 2026-10-14 that it has no indications that data from the attack was published on the darkweb.

The City of Zurich's pension fund has commented, and its position differs from the other funds': the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH) says in a notice dated 2026-10-13 that PK Softech was hit at the end of September, that it currently works with another software provider and plans to move to PK Softech's administration system in early 2027, so the attack does not touch the system it uses today, and that it is still clarifying whether, because of tests carried out ahead of that switch, PKZH data is also affected (PKZH, 2026-10-13). It adds that the incident does not affect insured persons' pension assets (PKZH, 2026-10-13). PKZH's concern is that migration tests may have left PKZH data at the supplier; it has not said that they did. Publica's page now carries a status of 2026-10-14 saying that it currently has no indications that data from the attack on its software supplier has been published on the darkweb and that it keeps monitoring the situation; its list of data that could be affected is unchanged (Publica, 2026-10-20). Neither statement says which data left, how the attackers got in or who they are.

Sources: Swiss Federal Administration (admin.ch) · PK Softech AG · watson.ch · Netzwoche · Netzwoche (running story, update of 2026-10-21) · Bernische Pensionskasse (BPK) · Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse (BLVK) · Pensionskasse Post · Inside IT (AWP) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes) · cash.ch (AWP) · Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes), page updated through 2026-10-21 · Cybercrimepolice (cantonal police platform) · SwissCybersecurity.net · Inside IT · NZZ · Blick (SonntagsBlick) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled; summary lines readable) · 20 Minuten · Ticinonline (relaying Corriere del Ticino) · Istituto di previdenza del Cantone Ticino (IPCT, letter to its insured) · Ticinonline · TicinoNews · EDÖB (Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner), press release · Der Bund (Tamedia) · Publica (newsletter of 2026-10-22, Cyberangriff auf Softwarelieferanten: Was wir wissen und was nicht)

04Action items8 items

  • Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.
    FindingPK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had…→
  • If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
    FindingPK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had…→
  • Run contentscannerstatus on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway that has File Reputation enabled in a mail policy and update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525 or later with contentscannerupdate wherever automatic updates are off; the update needs no restart.
    FindingCVE-2026-76519→
  • On every such gateway, and on each member of a cluster, run grep "System Security" system_logs now: on a suspected-compromise message keep the forensic data before upgrading, then follow Cisco's recovery steps (a new virtual machine on a fixed release with a fresh configuration and renewed credentials for a virtual appliance, Cisco TAC for a physical one) for every member of that cluster.
    FindingCVE-2026-76519→
  • Update the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that runs it; disabling the app does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older, which is end of life, upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app.
    FindingCVE-2026-110447→
  • On each such server, search the web access logs back to at least early September 2026 for requests to apps/richdocumentscode/proxy.php that carry $( or an encoded .. in the path, and the app directory for PHP files that are not part of the release; on a hit, treat every secret the web server account can read as exposed and rotate it.
    FindingCVE-2026-110447→
  • Restrict the management interface of every PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama to a jump box or trusted internal addresses now, then upgrade each to the fixed build of its train (11.2.14 and 11.2.15 units to 11.2.16, published 2026-10-15); there is no workaround.
    FindingCVE-2026-0322→
  • On every device whose management interface was reachable from untrusted networks, search management-interface logins, administrator-change records and upstream firewall logs for the three source addresses Palo Alto lists in the advisory's FAQ, and treat a match as a root compromise.
    FindingCVE-2026-0322→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-15T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 4 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Window: gap 24.0 h from 2026-10-14T0255Z-intel, window 26 h, developing-story window 72 h; the container clock agreed with the network date (skew 1 s). Four new entries (Cisco Secure Email Gateway CVE-2026-76519 critical; PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 high; Collabora Built-in CODE Server CVE-2026-110447 high; the fake WatchGuard VPN client site notable) and two changelog records (an update on the PK Softech/Publica entry, an improvement on the Danfoss refrigeration-controller entry). No deep dive: nothing cleared the bar. The previous record's publish_status is ok.

KEV sweep (work/2026-10-15T0256Z-intel/kev-window.txt): four additions dated 2026-10-14; CVE-2026-76519 and CVE-2026-0322 were NOT COVERED and became entries, the AhsayCBS pair (CVE-2026-105133, CVE-2026-105134) was already covered with exploitation stated. No RANSOMWARE rows.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): the one open row, Beyond Gravity, is unchanged (S2 and S4 re-checked: swissinfo, Netzwoche and bluewin of 2026-10-02 to 06 are still the freshest, no vector, actor or data class named, no leak-site listing); it stays held on its stated condition and expires 2026-10-20. No row changed state, so nothing was appended.

borderline-drop lines:

  • borderline-drop: Fortinet October PSIRT batch FG-IR-26-176 to -185 (S1; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 CVE-2026-106173 9.4, FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass CVE-2026-107656 9.6); Known Exploited is No on all ten, the FortiSIEM flaw affects 7.5.0 only and restricting TCP 27918 prevents it, NCSC-NL and CERT-FR only relay it; the 2026-10-14 fire dropped the same set on the same facts, so this is the same call, not a new one.
  • borderline-drop: Juniper Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved October bundle, 153 records (S1; three unauthenticated J-Web paths to root CVE-2026-101956, CVE-2026-101986 and CVE-2026-101954 and unauthenticated overflows at 9.8), a quarterly vendor release, Juniper SIRT and CISA's SSVC record state no exploitation, J-Web needs the web-management service configured, the advisory portal is a JavaScript shell on every transport so only the CNA record (not citable) and one ENISA page were readable, and the Cisco Nexus OAM and Fortinet bundles were judged the same way. Re-gate when an exploitation report, a KEV listing or a CERT or press page that can be cited appears.
  • borderline-drop: Microsoft October Patch Tuesday residual (S1; five Outlook preview-pane RCEs CVE-2026-70242, CVE-2026-97749, CVE-2026-97016, CVE-2026-88156, CVE-2026-70291, about 60 further unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 or above, the .NET WDAC bypass CVE-2026-108398, MessagePack-CSharp CVE-2026-92707), none exploited, all rated Exploitation Less Likely or Unlikely, no public proof of concept for the unauthenticated items; the 2026-10-14 fire dropped this set on identical facts.
  • borderline-drop: Chrome 155 stable, 37 fixes with seven Critical (S1), no exploitation statement, source dated 2026-10-13 20:53Z before the window.
  • borderline-drop: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit and Resecurity on Storm-2990 and Storm-3119 (YAM Store), the Chinese-language phishing-kit and tenant-takeover ecosystem (S3), victims named in Japan, the United States, Australia and India, a takedown narrative with generic mitigations; the one concrete hunt (the PnP Management Shell service principal self-provisioned after a hijacked Global Administrator sign-in) concerns the broker's own hijacked tenants, not a decision for this constituency this week.
  • borderline-drop: ARTEX, an open-source agentic penetration-testing framework abused against South Korean financial firms (S3; Zscaler, CrowdStrike), no constituency nexus, generic SQL injection and authentication bypass on peripheral web applications, and the store already carries several AI-agent intrusion entries.
  • borderline-drop: SlugFest, npm Trusted Publishing slug takeover (S3; Bloom Security), fixed by GitHub on 2026-10-02, no exploitation, exposure only through suppliers that publish npm packages.
  • borderline-drop: XWorm Reborn (Netskope, single source), CyberXero initial access broker (SOCRadar, nine days old, Ukrainian and Polish targets, the WordPress flaw already covered), UAT-6275 and TAG-193 (Talos with Recorded Future Insikt; CIS governments only, a generic WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 Startup-folder chain), Check Point on LiteLLM CVE-2026-35029 and CVE-2026-59823 (fixed 2026-04-17, authenticated, five LiteLLM entries already in the store) (S3).
  • borderline-drop: Offerz, a Swiss voucher webshop whose January order-data copy in a less-monitored test environment was accessed on 2026-10-07 (S2), no public-sector nexus, no vector, incident floor; the transferable lesson (a supplier holding real data of a customer that has not yet moved onto its system) rides the PK Softech update through the PKZH notice.
  • borderline-drop: Wolsfeld fire-service operations centre (Rhineland-Palatinate; single SWR relay of the prosecutors) and Mandurah SES (Western Australia; The Gentlemen listing, one server of pre-2022 records) (S4), no vector, no actor behaviour beyond impact, single source each, incident floor. SRF's blanket line that the Stadt Zürich fund is potentially affected (S2) is narrower in PKZH's own notice; the update carries PKZH's own statement and does not cite SRF.
  • borderline-drop: NCSC.ch hub 13059, Citrix XenServer CVE-2026-79610, CVE-2026-102700, CVE-2026-102701, CVE-2026-79611 (S2, S1); host compromise needs a privileged guest, exploitation unknown. SAP October Patch Day (16 notes, none exploited; the one unauthenticated 9+ item is a Cloud SDK for Python library flaw), NGINX CVE-2026-97205, CVE-2026-93479, CVE-2026-15176 (configuration-dependent, high complexity), Gitea CVE-2026-59774 (fixed 2026-07-27, CVE published only now), AnyDesk "AnyPwn" (aged out), Siemens (third-party components and authenticated items), Ivanti Neurons for Patch Management and Xtraction (9.9 but authenticated), Oracle (the October CPU is dated 2026-10-20) (S1).
  • borderline-drop: n0n maritime extortion batch, Ledger hardware-wallet implants, Femern Link Contractors (Fehmarnbelt tunnel contractor, no vector or actor; re-check next fire), Blueberry Pediatrics (a downstream Metabase victim, already covered), Egide, Medley At-Link, SpeeCAN, Park Dental, Joliet District 86 and the fuitesinfos claims (S4), out of nexus, claim-only or no behaviour.

Single-source: 2026-10-15/fake-watchguard-vpn-client-site-credential-capture is single-source (Huntress is the only source for this iteration; B2). Reduced-confidence inclusions: none.

Contradictions: the Danfoss improvement records that BleepingComputer reports no tie to the 2025 AK-SM 8xxA flaws while Censys points to them without Danfoss confirming the vector and NCSC.ch lists them as alleged; no source confirms a tie, and the entry says so. For the next audit: the verifier read Claroty's own page as saying the code-of-the-day gives a fully authenticated administrative session, as Censys does, so the older entry 2026-08-28/claroty-danfoss-ak-sm-800a-code-of-the-day-rce, which describes CVE-2025-41450 as an information disclosure, probably needs a correction record; this fire did not touch it.

Priority and ground calls: the Cisco gateway flaw is critical on the bar (exploited, unauthenticated root on the mail path, no workaround, compromised Secure Email Cloud tenants contacted by Cisco) although the fix ships as an automatic content update; PAN-OS is high (exploited, root, no workaround, but it needs credentials and management-interface reach); the Collabora flaw was first written notable for its single deployment mode and raised to high after verifier iteration 2: it is exploited, unauthenticated and critical, the web shells survive the update, and Collabora's own advisory says disabling the app does not stop it, so the decision this week is to update or remove it; the high bar asks for plausible exposure, and the store already carries Nextcloud entries for the public sector.

Candidate sources: cyberdaily-au added (S4). Not added: juniper-sirt and f5-security-advisories (S1; both vendor portals are JavaScript shells and no recipe exists, so they would only add standing repair orders), and Netskope Threat Labs and Bloom Security (S3; recipes unverified); the next audit may revisit them. blick-ch promoted to active per promotion_due although S2 judged it general news of limited depth; content_scope: general-news and a 48 h recipe note record that.

Rotation: the digest built, so no source was excluded as a recent attempt; slices ranked on the rotation cursor. S4's pool is 12 records and all were attempted by the previous two fires, so its ten oldest by cursor were allocated anyway.

Coverage gaps: inside-it-ch (article bodies behind the 429 checkpoint; RSS teasers only); fuitesinfos (listing shows 4 of 15 entries); swisspost-cybersecurity (marketing content); srf-news (feed and sitemap reach 36 to 48 h, so the 122 h lookback cannot be served); news-admin-ch (ignores date filters); kaspersky-securelist (no post since 2026-09-24); fortinet-fortiguard-blog (newest 2026-10-05); redcanary (blog moved to zscaler.com, own feed frozen); juniper-sirt (JSA pages are a JavaScript shell); reliaquest (sitemap lastmod bulk re-stamped, confirm every item by page date).

Operational notes: stop-hook nudges to commit arrived mid-run and were not acted on (nothing is committed before Phase 6). The harness offers no TodoWrite tool, so the phase plan lived in these notes. tools/source_health.py ran in Phase 5 and printed one UNSOLVED row, cnil-fr (url repointed, see sources_changed; CNIL's whole site answered a 503 maintenance page). One reader (jina) fetch was spent on a WatchGuard Secplicity page and one on the ENISA EUVD page inside extract's own fallback; neither is cited.

Verification: four independent cold passes (every ledger claim answered each time, 99 to 100 claims). Iterations 1 to 3 returned 12, 5 and 4 findings (the five of iteration 2 all came from the vendor's own Collabora advisory, which no earlier pass had read); iteration 4 returned one F3, a chained CISA citation in the PAN-OS entry. With one truth finding and no F1 or F4 the early exit applies: the fix was applied by the main agent against the saved Palo Alto page and the run publishes with verification_residual_count: 1, the final iteration's count. No CLEAN verdict was reached, so there was no confirmation pass; the Collabora entry (rewritten in iteration 2 and edited again in iteration 3) is the one the next audit should give an independent look. Declined findings: none after iteration 2 (the iteration 1 priority rebuttal was withdrawn in iteration 2).

item.description:
• Ivanti Connect Secure chain: root step patched 29 Oct, CISA lists three flaws; 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 fall short. Ivanti disclosed the exploited Connect Secure authentication bypass CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13; Volexity saw it chained by UTA0576 with a root escalation, CVE-2026-111357, patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Ivanti patched the root step on 2026-10-29 and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30; the Canadian Cyber Centre now lists every build before 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 as affected, which takes in 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5, the builds of 2026-10-13. A patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset. →
  • Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links. Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release. →
  • German portal vendor reports an exploited zero-day and calls it AI-driven; police neither confirm nor deny that. Innocon, the Tangermünde developer of the "digitales Rathaus" citizen portal, said in an MDR report of 2026-10-13 that attackers found and exploited a vulnerability it did not know of in its software, run for Tangerhütte on systems of the state municipal IT provider KID; the portal was taken offline in September and four more communes pulled theirs as a precaution. Innocon says the attackers reached only test accounts and took no real data, and classifies the intrusion as AI-driven because of command speed and on-host tool development, which is the vendor's reading: the state criminal police can neither confirm nor deny it. No CVE, product version or fix is named. →

  3. 03German portal vendor reports an exploited zero-day and calls it AI-driven; police neither confirm nor deny that. Innocon, the Tangermünde developer of the "digitales Rathaus" citizen portal, said in an MDR report of 2026-10-13 that attackers found and exploited a vulnerability it did not know of in its software, run for Tangerhütte on systems of the state municipal IT provider KID; the portal was taken offline in September and four more communes pulled theirs as a precaution. Innocon says the attackers reached only test accounts and took no real data, and classifies the intrusion as AI-driven because of command speed and on-host tool development, which is the vendor's reading: the state criminal police can neither confirm nor deny it. No CVE, product version or fix is named. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 4Updates to prior coverage 3Action items 9

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLENATOB3

Tangerhütte (Saxony-Anhalt): the vendor of the municipal citizen-portal software says attackers exploited a zero-day in it, classifies the intrusion as AI-driven, and four other communes took their portals offline

MDR AKTUELL reports on 2026-10-13 that the vendor of Tangerhütte's "digitales Rathaus" citizen portal says attackers found and exploited a vulnerability in its software that the vendor did not know of and for which no security update existed (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13). The portal, an app-based service that went online in 2020, was taken offline in September, and MDR Sachsen-Anhalt reported on 2026-09-16 that the municipality said it had repelled an attack and gave no technical detail (MDR Sachsen-Anhalt, 2026-09-16). The software runs on systems that the state municipal IT provider KID operates for Tangerhütte; an IT employee noticed irregularities in the morning after the attack began at night, the server was isolated and cut from the internet, and the vendor analysed the secured logs on an offline notebook (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13). Innocon told other affected communes, four of which also took their portals offline as a precaution although there was no sign of an attack on them, and says the attackers reached only test accounts and took no real data (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13). Citizens could use the services only on paper for weeks (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13).

The vendor classifies the intrusion as AI-driven for two reasons: commands were executed faster than copy-and-paste would allow, and the follow-on steps were not prepared in advance but developed on the city's server during the attack, whereas human attackers normally upload their own code and do not change it (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13). That is the vendor's reading of its own logs. The state criminal police are investigating data espionage and can neither confirm nor deny an AI attack, and two professors told MDR the reading is plausible without having seen the logs (MDR AKTUELL, 2026-10-13). No CVE, product version, fixed release or entry vector is named.

Exposure
Municipalities running Innocon's digitales Rathaus, which is used for Tangerhütte and at least four further communes that Innocon informed; whether any Swiss body runs it is not reported. The case matters to communal administrations as a supplier-built citizen portal hosted by a shared municipal IT provider, where the customer cannot patch an unknown flaw itself.
Detection
The vendor's two observations are the pattern to look for in a portal host's logs: commands issued faster than a person could type them, and follow-on scripts written and run on the host within the same session rather than uploaded once.
Defender takeaway
For a citizen portal built on a supplier's software, an exploited unknown flaw leaves isolation as the only lever, and this case shows what worked: isolate the server, copy the logs and analyse them offline, and have the supplier warn its other customers, four of which pulled their portals as a precaution.
incident14 Oct 03:42Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: MDR AKTUELL · MDR Sachsen-Anhalt

02Trending vulnerabilities4 items

CRITICALCVE-2026-104935 +2exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, the root-escalation step was patched on 2026-10-29 and CISA lists all three chain flaws (CVSS 8.6)

Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 in Connect Secure on 2026-10-13 and says it is aware of limited exploitation in the wild (Ivanti, 2026-10-13); Rapid7 describes it as an authentication bypass by spoofing that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, CVSS 8.6 (Rapid7, 2026-10-13), and CISA listed it in KEV the same day (CISA, 2026-10-13). Volexity tracks the operator as UTA0576 and dates exploitation of a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance to 2026-10-03 (Volexity, 2026-10-13).

The chain has three steps. A request to the public login script welcome.cgi names a protected script in an X-DSCGI-PATH header, so the URL passes the authentication check and the header picks the destination. The upload script wu.cgi writes a file to disk before checking that it is a ZIP, and parallel requests run a Perl script before it is deleted. A root escalation then abuses the dsinvoked service's trust in the shared DSCache configuration store (Volexity, 2026-10-13). The first two steps are CVE-2026-104935 and the root step is CVE-2026-111357 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15); Volexity's update banner says Ivanti patched it on 2026-10-29 (Volexity, 2026-10-13). CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30, says each can be chained with the other two, and describes CVE-2026-118527 as a predictable-identifier flaw that lets a remote authenticated attacker upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-30). No source says which step of the chain that is, and it has no public CVE record or fixed build yet.

The exploit leaves no web shell and patches library code in memory only, so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool, which looks for file changes, does not detect it, and Volexity found log entries removed. The operator then went after the Active Directory service account stored on the appliance: LDAP queries for LAPS passwords, BitLocker recovery keys and password attributes, password spraying, and packet capture of plaintext LDAP, HTTP Basic and NTLM traffic (Volexity, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
25.1.1.1 and prior, 25.1.2.2 and prior and 22.8R2.4 and prior are affected by CVE-2026-104935 and 22.7.x and below are not (Rapid7, 2026-10-13). The Canadian Cyber Centre's bulletin, updated 2026-10-30, lists every version before 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 as affected (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-10-13), which takes in 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5, the builds of 2026-10-13; CISA's alert, updated the same day, says the three chain CVEs affect versions 25.1.1.2 and prior, 25.1.2.2 and prior and 22.8R2.5 and prior (CISA, 2026-10-13). Ivanti's advisory could not be read, so per-CVE fixed builds are unconfirmed.
Detection
The appliance's own logs were tampered with, so start upstream: web proxy, load balancer or WAF logs for many requests to welcome.cgi, above all with an X-DSCGI-PATH header or one whose script differs from the URL path. On domain controllers, look for LDAP queries from the appliance's service account for LAPS, BitLocker recovery and password attributes, and spraying from the appliance's address. Patching does not evict an attacker who is already in.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6 now, then treat every appliance that was exposed on an affected build as a compromise-assessment target and rotate what it could reach. Where compromise cannot be excluded, isolate the appliance and preserve its memory and logs before any reset, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on it (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14).
Update16 Oct 2026 04:10 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says Ivanti reports the vulnerability as actively exploited and that CERT-FR itself is aware of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). It puts the response in an order: fully isolate the appliance from both the internet and the internal network, snapshot the file system and memory of a virtual appliance, avoid powering it off so that traces survive, place the logs under seal and analyse the appliance with the Volexity indicators, and only then, on compromise, factory-reset it, upgrade and reset the secrets (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). Its list of secrets to treat as compromised is wider than a password reset: the LDAP and Active Directory secrets, every certificate on the appliance (machine, user-authentication, code-signing and the TLS certificate of the exposed interface), the administration password, stored API keys, the passwords of local accounts including the service accounts used for authentication servers, the Kerberos tickets and other authentication material of those service accounts, and the licence-server authentication (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). CERT-FR adds that running Ivanti's external Integrity Checker Tool needs physical access to the appliance and can interrupt service, and that some threats survive a factory reset (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14). Its affected-systems list names the 22.8Rx builds before 22.8R2.5, the 25.1.1.x builds before 25.1.1.2 and the 25.1.3.x builds before 25.1.3.1 and does not list a 25.1.2.x line; by counting 25.1.3.x builds before 25.1.3.1 as affected it includes 25.1.3.0, a build that Rapid7's table lists as resolved (CERT-FR, 2026-10-14).

Improvement17 Oct 2026 03:34 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencebody

The root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published on 2026-10-15 and rated High on GitHub's advisory database as GHSA-fhw5-mpvj-x89m (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-15). Its description reads "Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.4 mishandles the manner in which the dsinvoked broker trusts DSCache configuration data, leading to privilege escalation to root, as exploited in the wild in October 2026." CVE-2026-96951, Windows Shell: a Mark of the Web bypass exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the 2026-10-13 cumulative updates and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.8)

Microsoft's 2026-10-13 release fixes CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell security feature bypass that Microsoft marks as exploited and not publicly disclosed (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13); CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day, citing evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-10-13). Microsoft says an attacker who exploits it could evade Mark of the Web defenses, by sending a crafted file by email or instant message or enticing the user to click a link or open an attachment (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft's record gives the root cause as improper neutralization of special elements in a command (command injection, CWE-77) (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Rapid7 describes the effect as Windows not showing the dialog that says it protected the PC, because the tag that triggers it is bypassed, calls this the second exploited Windows Shell zero-day this year, and says the flaw also affected Outlook.com, patched in a build several weeks ago (Rapid7, 2026-10-13). Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch while Server 2012 R2 does (Rapid7, 2026-10-13), and Microsoft's record lists no Windows Server 2012 product for this flaw (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2012 R2 through 2025 where users open files or links from mail, chat or the web; the fixed build per release is in the CVE record, and Rapid7 reports no patch for Windows Server 2012.
Detection
Microsoft, CISA and Rapid7 name no actor, payload or victims and no source describes the exploit's behavior, so this is a hunt hypothesis that follows from the mechanism: the failed control is the Mark of the Web tag, so there is no warning dialog for a user to report. Look at mail gateway, chat and endpoint file-origin telemetry for internet-origin files, archives and shortcuts that execute without the usual download warning, and at process lineage from explorer.exe into scripting interpreters and living-off-the-land binaries shortly after a mail or browser download.

Triage: a file a user created or received from a trusted local source also carries no tag; the discriminator is an internet origin (mail, chat or web download) together with the absence of the tag on the opened item.

Defender takeaway
Install the October cumulative update now, ahead of the monthly cycle, on endpoints that open mail and web downloads first; because the tag is the control that failed, attachment blocking and mail-gateway detonation remain the compensating layer until the update is deployed, and Rapid7 reports no patch for Windows Server 2012.

CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)

Microsoft's October 2026 Exchange security updates, released on 2026-10-13, fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow in Exchange Server: an unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted email to an affected server, triggering an internal content-conversion process, with no user interaction (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft rates it Critical (CVSS 8.1, high attack complexity) and Exploitation More Likely, and says exploitation requires a deep understanding of the target environment and is not guaranteed to succeed (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). CVE-2026-70279 is a cross-site scripting spoofing flaw (CVSS 9.3, also Exploitation More Likely): an attacker who persuades an administrator to click a crafted link could act with that administrator's privileges (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft lists neither as exploited or publicly disclosed, and no other source reports exploitation.

The fixed builds are Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM 15.02.2562.056, 2019 CU15 15.02.1748.055, 2019 CU14 15.02.1544.050 and 2016 CU23 15.01.2507.077 (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). The 2016 and 2019 updates are available only to organisations enrolled in the Period 2 ESU program, and October 2026 is the last month those customers receive newly released updates (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13). After October, updates ship for Subscription Edition only, Microsoft's announcements and CVEs stop mentioning 2016 and 2019, and Microsoft says that does not mean those versions are not vulnerable and that it will stop testing them for vulnerabilities (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13); buying Period 2 ESU later only gets an organisation current through this release (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13). Exchange Online customers are already protected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
On-premises Exchange Subscription Edition, 2019 CU14 and CU15 and 2016 CU23 that receive external mail for CVE-2026-70571, and administrator sessions in the web interfaces for CVE-2026-70279. The update also has to go onto machines that only run the Exchange Management Tools (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13).
Detection
No source describes exploitation behavior. Microsoft says a successful attempt is not guaranteed, so, as an inference from the mechanism, a failed attempt would more likely appear as a crash than a shell: watch for crashes and application-log faults of the Exchange transport processes right after inbound mail from outside, and for unexpected child processes of those processes.
Defender takeaway
Install the October update on every Exchange server and management-tools machine, because Microsoft rates both flaws Exploitation More Likely. An organisation still on Exchange 2016 or 2019 without Period 2 ESU has no update for CVE-2026-70571 and no further updates after this one; the choices are enrolling, which ends at October's release, or moving to Subscription Edition. On an Exchange host that also takes the October Windows Server update, do not uninstall that update: Microsoft says the OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum that can follow are not caused by the Exchange security update, and its workaround is to set the Rpc registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and reboot (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Update17 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceactionsbody

Microsoft's Exchange Team has published guidance for Exchange servers that become unstable after the October 2026 Windows Server updates. Since 2026-10-13 it has seen reports of OWA failing with MapiExceptionMdbOffline (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142; event ID 1006 in the Application log), mail queues growing during the day, DAG members unable to reach quorum and a reboot helping only temporarily; Exchange 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition can all be affected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17). It says the issues are not related to installing the October 2026 Exchange security updates and that any Exchange version running on an affected Windows build can be hit; KB5126646 (Windows Server 2025), KB5126655 (2022), KB5126651 (2019) and KB5126868 (2016) can cause the failures after some time, and the impact varies with Exchange load, so some servers may never see a problem (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Microsoft's recommendation is not to uninstall the October 2026 Windows Server updates and, from an elevated command prompt on the Exchange server, to set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc to 65536, reboot, monitor, and raise the limit if the problem recurs; it says this has solved the customer cases it has assisted (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced arbitrary code execution on GitLab CE 19.4.1, published a proof of concept, and found no confirmed exploitation in the wild. A proof of concept went public the same day; its README says the included offsets were tested only against the 19.4.1 CE Linux amd64 image, that other builds need adjusted offsets, and that the generated payload is slightly larger than 2 GiB, needing about 9 GiB of memory on the test host (Rapid7 proof-of-concept README, 2026-10-13). The affected and fixed versions are unchanged.
