Verification & coverage notes

Standard 26 h window (2026-10-13T00:55Z to 2026-10-14T02:55Z), 24.0 h after the 2026-10-13 fire. The container clock agreed with the network date header (skew 0 s) and the first fetch saw the 2026-10-13 run record, so the gap is real. The four sub-agents returned 37 candidate items (S1 12, S2 5, S3 8, S4 12; the Ivanti chain came back from S1 and S3, the refrigeration-controller revision from S2 and S4); five ship as new entries, three become changelog records and the rest are dropped below. This is the first fire to see the 2026-10-13 Patch Tuesday set, which the previous fire flagged as unread: S1 read the MSRC CVRF, Adobe's three server bulletins, Fortinet, Ivanti and SAP from the vendors' own tables. The mechanical KEV diff listed two NOT COVERED additions dated 2026-10-13 (CVE-2026-104935 Ivanti Connect Secure, CVE-2026-96951 Windows Shell) and both are new entries; no RANSOMWARE row. No deep dive. One critical: the Ivanti Connect Secure chain meets every element of the bar (newly disclosed, exploited, an unpatched companion step, defender action to the day).

Published (5):

  • 2026-10-14/cve-2026-104935-ivanti-connect-secure-zero-day-chain-kev (vulnerability, critical): exploited VPN-edge zero-day chain (Ivanti and CISA confirm, Volexity forensics), root step unfixed, invisible to the vendor's integrity tool; PD-11(b). No Swiss victim or deployment is reported, so the relevance ground is the product class on the perimeter of public-sector networks. S1 and S3 both returned it; S1's vendor metadata and S3's Volexity depth were merged. The hub advisory page is unreadable on every transport, so the build table is read through Rapid7 and the entry says so; the Canadian bulletin's different 25.x line label is carried as a stated discrepancy. NCSC.ch had no advisory yet at 03:10Z, so an NCSC.ch post is likely at the next fire.
  • 2026-10-14/cve-2026-96951-windows-shell-motw-bypass-zero-day-kev (vulnerability, high): Microsoft-flagged exploited zero-day on every supported Windows release, KEV-listed; PD-11(b). No actor, payload or victim is public. References the September Windows zero-day entry.
  • 2026-10-14/exchange-oct-2026-su-cve-2026-70571-last-2016-2019-update (vulnerability, notable): unauthenticated crafted-email RCE rated Exploitation More Likely, plus the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 update for ESU customers; PD-11(b) on the mechanics (internet-reachable mail path) and (a) for the ESU cut-off. Not exploited, AC:H, so notable and not high. The four Less-Likely elevation flaws and the earlier CVE-2026-96940 are left out of the entry.
  • 2026-10-14/adobe-october-2026-coldfusion-aem-commerce-unauth-critical (vulnerability, notable): ten unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 across ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce or Magento, Adobe aware of no exploitation; PD-11(b) on the mechanics (no account needed, internet-facing web platforms), same shape as the Campaign Classic and August ColdFusion entries. S1 listed four ColdFusion CVEs; the raw bulletin shows a fifth unauthenticated one (CVE-2026-106621, 9.1), which the entry carries. Magento Open Source 2.4.6 has no listed fix.
  • 2026-10-14/tangerhuette-digitales-rathaus-zero-day-municipal-portal (incident, notable): the vendor of a municipal citizen portal says a zero-day in its software was exploited and four other communes pulled their portals. PD-11(c) on the shared target profile (communal e-government portals hosted by a shared municipal IT provider); single source (MDR), vendor's own account, the AI classification is carried as the vendor's reading with the state criminal police neither confirming nor denying. S2 found the lead through Golem but could not read it; S4 read MDR.

Updated (3), each one record on the existing entry:

  • 2026-10-13/cve-2026-97229-gitlab-ci-regex-compiler-unauthenticated-rce (update, priority stays high): Rapid7 reproduced the code execution on 19.4.1 and published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13 and found no confirmed exploitation; the demonstrated path needs push access to a public project plus an unauthenticated CI lint request. Status moves to poc-public, title and headline drop the unqualified "unauthenticated", the exposure paragraph states the conditions Rapid7 found, and the action now carries Rapid7's interim controls. The sentence that no source reported a proof of concept was rewritten where it stood.
  • 2026-10-13/danfoss-ak-sm-ak-sc-french-supermarket-refrigeration-attack (update, priority stays high): CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, say campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit; NCSC Switzerland's advisory 13054 rates it actively exploited and names AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware. The revision rewrote CERT-FR's guidance (filtering to contractor addresses is now an emergency stop-gap, VPN or protected network is the target), so the two CERT-FR evidence quotes that the live page no longer carries were replaced and the title, summary, exposure, detection and takeaway were rewritten to today's text. S2 and S4 both returned it. The iteration-3 verifier found Blick's French edition, which reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores; the entry now says so and carries the switzerland region, and S2's earlier reading that no Swiss deployment was reported is superseded.
  • 2026-08-28/claroty-copeland-xweb-pro-refrigeration-unauth-root-rce (update, priority stays high): its "no exploitation reported" no longer describes the product family now that CERT-FR reports compromises of Copeland xweb controllers; the record says CERT-FR names no models, flaws or vector and does not tie the compromises to Claroty's findings, so no CVE status moved.

KEV dispositions: CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-96951, new entries above. The CISA catalog page cannot be cited; the per-alert pages were used.

borderline-drop lines:

  • borderline-drop: Microsoft Patch Tuesday rollup beyond the exploited zero-day and Exchange (S1); the October release is the largest yet, but every other unauthenticated network flaw at CVSS 9.0 or above (DNS Server, DHCP Server, IIS, RRAS, Network Policy Server, Message Queuing, QUIC, LSASS, RPC Runtime, iSCSI, Failover Cluster, OpenSSH for Windows, PowerShell, Text Shaping, Windows Error Reporting and the others in S1's table) is rated Exploitation Less Likely or Unlikely, none is exploited or publicly disclosed; five zero-interaction Outlook preview-pane RCEs (CVE-2026-70242, CVE-2026-97749, CVE-2026-97016, CVE-2026-88156, CVE-2026-70291) are also Less Likely and none is exploited, so they ride the regular cycle. The publicly disclosed .NET Framework WDAC bypass CVE-2026-108398 needs a local foothold and the MessagePack-CSharp denial of service (5.3) is a library flaw. The lifecycle facts (Server 2012 and 2012 R2 ESU year 3 ends 2026-10-14, Office 2021 end of support 2026-10-14, Windows 10 commercial ESU year 1 ends 2026-10-13) were not published; the Windows entry states that Server 2012 gets no update.
  • borderline-drop: Cisco Nexus 3000 and 9000 NGOAM and MPLS OAM unauthenticated root RCE (CVE-2026-76485, CVE-2026-76486, CVE-2026-76501, CVE-2026-76465, CVSS 9.8) and License On-Prem (CVE-2026-20328, CVE-2026-76454, 9.1) (S1, lookback; Cisco 2026-10-07, NCSC.ch 2026-10-09), found in internal testing, no exploitation, reachable only through an OAM-enabled interface on the switch rather than the internet, and NCSC.ch already advised the Swiss constituency on 2026-10-09; regular patch cycle with Cisco's disable-the-feature mitigation.
  • borderline-drop: Fortinet October bundle (S1; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 CVE-2026-106173 9.4 on TCP 27918, FortiSandbox authentication bypass), vendor-only, not exploited, narrow affected builds (FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only), Fortinet's workaround restricts the port; the FortiMail zero-day entry is unchanged since 2026-10-07.
  • borderline-drop: Esri Portal for ArcGIS CVE-2026-69227 (S1; 9.8, patched 2026-09-24, CVE published 2026-10-13), a 20-day-old patch, the flaw needs a specific New Member default user type configuration, Esri states no exploitation although its vector carries exploit-code maturity High; no source puts a constituency deployment on the internet.
  • borderline-drop: OTRS CE 6 and Znuny CVE-2026-93582 (S1; 9.4), needs an HTTP Basic Authentication backend, 6.x is end of life, Znuny fixed it on 2026-09-16, no exploitation; AnyDesk CVE-2026-109390 (S1), fixed in 8.0.3 on 2026-06-23, only the CVE id is new; IBM WebSphere Liberty CVE-2026-93909 and CVE-2026-93895 (S1; 9.1), need the samlWeb-2.0 or grpc-1.0 feature, not exploited, interim fix available.
  • borderline-drop: S1's other drops, SAP Patch Day (no pre-auth RCE; the 9.9 flaws need authentication and the 10.0 is a developer library), Siemens and Schneider bundles, Chrome 155 and Firefox 158 (no exploitation statement), Docker Hub CVE-2026-105445, Ghostscript CVE-2026-39919, Commvault CVE-2026-77099, Metabase CVE-2026-103928, Ivanti Xtraction and Neurons Patch for Intune (authenticated).
  • borderline-drop: NCSC.ch advisories 13043 (Veeam Backup & Replication CVE-2025-64393, low-privileged to SYSTEM), 13035 (ILIAS) and 13022 (Zimbra CVE-2026-66911 and CVE-2026-66912, unauthenticated account takeover paths) (S1 catch-up leads; 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-09), all rated exploitation UNKNOWN by NCSC.ch, vendor pages not read this fire, no entry in the store; judged regular cycle on the hub text alone. The next audit should read the Veeam and Zimbra vendor pages, since both products are common in public administrations.
  • borderline-drop: BSI WID-SEC-2026-3757 revision 3 marking the SonicWall SMA1000 flaw exploited (S2); a third national authority restating the status the entry already carries from NCSC.ch; no new fact.
  • borderline-drop: Stadt Olten forged QR stickers on parking meters (S2), fraud against citizens with no SOC decision. Beyond Gravity (S2), no new detail, held in the backlog.
  • borderline-drop: North Korean IT workers, FBI PSA261013 and the CrowdStrike laptop-farm disruption (S3), US employer guidance and a US law-enforcement action, no constituency nexus, existing entries cover the cluster. MITRE ATT&CK v20 (S3), a framework release, not threat activity; the pin is stale (below). Luna Moth Files (S3), an unauthenticated leak of chat logs published about 2026-10-05, SRG calls it fake, no new technique. Fox-IT Cobalt Strike beacon corpus, Check Point LiteLLM CVE-2026-35029 and CVE-2026-59823 (authenticated), Barracuda hidden prompt injection in mail, the Dubrovsky arrest in the ShinyHunters case (S3), marginal for the constituency.
  • borderline-drop: Arcadia SpeeCAN RAIDEN municipal mass-notification breach in Japan (S4), out of region, no vector, no actor; the only lesson (suppliers concentrate contact lists) is generic. Stadt Eichstätt (S4), a Bavarian city with copied data and intact backups but no vector, no actor and no behavior (incident floor). HSZ-BW, Kreiskliniken Kassel, UK Housing Ombudsman, Amadeus heap dump, Ahold Delhaize and U.S.NEXT (S4), no vector or actor, out of nexus, or a single-source misconfiguration note. FTAPI dataset publication (S4; heise 2026-10-12, before the window), mostly marketing material plus an apparent customer list, the entry stays routine. Anthropic's report on unintended model actions with the Philadelphia police statement (S4), awareness only.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): three of the four open rows reached their 2026-10-14 expiry with the condition unmet and are struck: IBM Guardium CVE-2026-85542 (not in KEV catalog 2026.10.13, ACN alert unchanged, IBM's bulletins do not mention it, authenticated), and the SafePay and Payload claims on ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal and Netech (no press link on Ransomware.live, no victim statement). Beyond Gravity stays held on its named condition (a vector, an actor or the data class), expiry 2026-10-20, with nothing new from S2 and S4.

Contradictions and discrepancies carried in the entries: (1) Ivanti: the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security lists the 25.x affected line as 25.2.2 and prior, Rapid7's table of Ivanti's advisory says 25.1.2.2 and prior, and the advisory itself was unreadable. (2) GitLab: GitLab's CVSS carries no privilege requirement while Rapid7's reproduction needs push access to a public project. (3) Danfoss: NCSC Switzerland relays six CERT-FR remediation steps that the revised CERT-FR page no longer lists (it now has a different two-path guidance); the entry follows the live CERT-FR text. (4) Adobe: the ColdFusion summary says priority 2, its solution table priority 1; stated in the sourcing note.

Coverage gaps: hub-ivanti-advisory (JS-only on every transport; read through Rapid7 and Volexity); golem-security (consent wall on article bodies); justice-gov (Akamai and HTTP 401); swissinfo-ger (no feed or search route, jina credit spent); databreaches-net (article pages 403); tenable-research (undated feed served through the reader); vaud-soc-cyber-threat-review (no September edition posted); news-web-nhk (JS-rendered body); hsz-offline-de (HTTP 404 with the notice in the body); kreisklinikenkassel-de (stale snapshot).

Rotation and sources: slices were ranked on the derived rotation cursor (S1 14 standard or candidate records beyond 6 essential, S2 14 beyond 15, S3 14, S4 12); every essential record was attempted. S1 reported that ivanti-psirt, adobe-psirt, cisco-psirt, sap-security-notes and siemens-productcert were not in its slice yet carried the day's primaries; the notes on those records ask to rotate them into S1 on scheduled-release days. Metered reader calls: about six (S2 one, S3 two, S4 three), all fallbacks from extract or a speculative URL. One new candidate source, blick-ch; S3 proposed mitre-attack-updates and S4 scannetsecurity, left for a later fire. The source health sweep probed 242 of 242 records (240 relevant, one stale, one shell), no UNSOLVED item.

For the operator and the next audit, not acted on this fire: (1) the ATT&CK pin is v19.2 while v20 was released 2026-10-13 with nine new Enterprise technique ids and no revocations or deprecations, so existing mappings stay valid but v20 ids cannot be used until python3 tools/attack_data.py --update runs; (2) the Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026 (published 2026-10-01) has no entry in the store; (3) the three NCSC.ch catch-up advisories above.

Verification: five cti-verification iterations, each walking the full claim ledger (176 to 183 claims, every one answered). Iteration 1 returned NEEDS_FIXES (25 findings: 14 truth, 5 editorial, 6 advisory), iteration 2 NEEDS_FIXES (10), iteration 3 NEEDS_FIXES (4 truth), iteration 4 NEEDS_FIXES (3 truth, 1 advisory) and iteration 5 NEEDS_FIXES with two low-confidence F3 findings. Every finding was tested against the cited page and fixed except two declined with reasons: the older Claroty entry's em dashes (pre-existing, normalised at render, outside this fire's own sections) and the out-of-cycle reading of the Adobe priority (the takeaway no longer claims urgency, the entry stays notable). The loop ends on the low-residual early exit of Phase 5.7 rule 5: iteration 5 returned truth plus editorial of 2 with no F1 or F4, both findings were fixed after the return, and no confirmation pass followed, so those two fixes were checked by the gate and the main agent only; verification_residual_count is 2. No double-CLEAN was reached. The defects that kept recurring were statements dated or attributed more precisely than their source (a reproduction date, an interview date, a citation closing the wrong claim), per-CVE bindings the vendor page does not make, and run notes claiming the entries carry something an earlier fix had removed. The Blick finding of iteration 3 (Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores) corrected an earlier "no Swiss deployment" statement. A container restart lost the first iteration-5 spawn and it was respawned once; the working tree survived. Entries from this fire that the next quality audit should read independently: the five new entries and the Danfoss update, since no pass confirmed the final text.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-13
item.description:
• GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex RCE is now on CISA KEV; the public PoC needs push access to a public project. GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation on the strength of Alpine Linux's account of a newly registered account that crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance because it could not rule out code execution; GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, Rapid7 published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13, and the path it demonstrated needs push access to a public project. →
  • ANSSI says the refrigeration attacks used exposure and weak passwords, not published flaws; NCSC.ch rates them exploited. Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware. ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, rather than vulnerabilities researchers had published; no source names an actor, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating. →
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex RCE is now on CISA KEV; the public PoC needs push access to a public project. GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation on the strength of Alpine Linux's account of a newly registered account that crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance because it could not rule out code execution; GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, Rapid7 published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13, and the path it demonstrated needs push access to a public project. →
  2. 02ANSSI says the refrigeration attacks used exposure and weak passwords, not published flaws; NCSC.ch rates them exploited. Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware. ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, rather than vulnerabilities researchers had published; no source names an actor, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 3Action items 6

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

HIGHexploitedupdatedNATOA2

Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost reported at hundreds of French supermarkets; CERT-FR and NCSC Switzerland say to remove internet exposure

Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026; AFP reports from the retailers' statements at least 300 Intermarché or Netto shops and more than 100 Coopérative U outlets, and the Paris prosecutor opened an investigation (AFP, 2026-10-12). BFMTV puts the Intermarché and Netto count at 300, which it says is twice the first estimates of 150 points of sale, and Coopérative U below 100 stores, while Infosecurity quotes 150 Intermarché and 30 Netto stores (BFMTV, 2026-10-12; Infosecurity Magazine, 2026-10-12). BFMTV, writing in the conditional, reports that the attackers are said to have imposed a forced, continuous defrost with the setpoint at 50 degrees, on software older than version 4, heating the equipment for hours (translated from French) (BFMTV, 2026-10-12). CERT-FR's alert, in its revision of 2026-10-13, says it knows of numerous compromises of the remote refrigeration controllers Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series as well as Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and that exposing a management interface to the internet is contrary to good practice (CERT-FR, 2026-10-13). Danfoss told AFP that most affected units are legacy products that no longer receive software or security updates, naming the AK-SM800 and AK-SC355 regulators, and a person close to the Prime Minister said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software from a Danish company and that other countries may be affected (AFP, 2026-10-12). Intermarché told BleepingComputer that the attack reportedly affected a service provider that manages refrigeration systems in stores (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-12), and E. Leclerc told AFP that a cyberattack affected one of its refrigeration equipment suppliers (AFP, 2026-10-12). Infosecurity says the affected stores include those running vulnerable consoles with remote control and no adequately secured communication channel (Infosecurity Magazine, 2026-10-12). ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, above all equipment directly on the internet and administered without particular protection, plus weak passwords, and dismissed analyses that blamed vulnerabilities researchers had published over the previous two years (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21); Le Monde Informatique adds that the systems were reachable without a firewall or network segmentation and that the management interface was protected only by weak passwords (Le Monde Informatique, 2026-10-22). No source names an actor, and none confirms a tie to the 2025 AK-SM 8xxA vulnerabilities that Claroty found: BleepingComputer says no information is available on how the controllers were compromised (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-12) and NCSC Switzerland lists three of them only as alleged to be potentially related (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-13); Censys names the same three as flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and says Danfoss has not confirmed the initial access vector (Censys, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
A Danfoss AK-SM or AK-SC refrigeration controller, or a Copeland or Dixell xweb unit, whose management interface is reachable from the internet, above all legacy units; Danfoss says the current AK-SM800A units that were affected ran outdated firmware (Cooling Post, 2026-10-12), and CERT-FR names no models, flaw or entry vector for the Copeland and Dixell units (CERT-FR, 2026-10-13). Copeland first declined to confirm CERT-FR's finding and has since acknowledged a vulnerability, which, Cybersecurity Dive reports, a Copeland spokesperson confirmed was found in discontinued end-of-life controllers, and says it is working with impacted customers to mitigate the risk; neither article names the flaw (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-15; Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-10-15). Infosecurity reports, without naming them, that supermarkets in Belgium and the Netherlands were also reportedly affected (Infosecurity Magazine, 2026-10-12); Blick reports that Migros confirms using, in a limited number of its Swiss stores, the same Danfoss refrigeration systems that were targeted and says nothing indicates an attack on them, while Aldi and Lidl say they are not concerned and Coop says it was not affected and declines to say whether it uses Danfoss (Blick, 2026-10-13); no source reports a Swiss victim, so ask whoever manages your refrigeration and building services whether a controller sits in your estate. For an AK-SM 800A, Censys maps the firmware to the published flaws: a build below 4.2 carries all three, 4.2.4 fixes only the date-based login and so still carries the two later ones, and 4.3.1 or later fixes all three, with 5.3.2 the current build it lists (Censys, 2026-10-14). For the Copeland and Dixell units, CERT-FR links a Dixell France guide (CERT-FR, 2026-10-16) that carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, in which Copeland acknowledges the vulnerability on a generation of XWEB EVO controllers that is no longer marketed and has reached end of life, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet immediately and says XWEB EVO no longer receives security patches, and that adds Dixell France's own recommendations, among them that XWEB PRO and EVO ship with the same factory Admin account (Dixell France, 2026-10-14). The bulletin names the affected generation but describes no flaw (Dixell France, 2026-10-14). Forescout counts 12,976 internet-exposed service observations on 6,017 public addresses in 99 countries, 7,075 of them Copeland and Dixell XWEB and 4,697 Danfoss StoreView, and finds that 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, run firmware older than 4.3.1 (Forescout, 2026-10-22).
Detection
On the controller, defrost, setpoint and account changes outside a maintenance window; in firewall, provider VPN or ISP logs, inbound connections to the management interface from addresses other than the refrigeration contractor's; CERT-FR accepts filtering to the contractors' source addresses only as an emergency measure and wants access restored through a secure VPN or protected network (CERT-FR, 2026-10-13). For a controller that may have been taken over, CERT-FR's current text is to remove the internet exposure, restart the Danfoss unit or otherwise restore it with a factory reset, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network, reconfigure it and apply the maker's practices, which for Danfoss means updating the firmware, setting the security level to Strict and confirming the default passwords were changed (CERT-FR, 2026-10-16); for a unit not known to be compromised it asks to check the whole configuration, notably the defrost ranges (CERT-FR, 2026-10-16). Le Monde reports that besides raising the defrost setpoint to 50 degrees the attackers lengthened the defrost operation from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late (translated from French), which makes the defrost duration a tamper signal beside the setpoint (Le Monde, 2026-10-12; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-15). Forescout advises correlating remote-access sessions with changes to defrost schedules, alarms, setpoints, users and network configuration, because the abused functions are legitimate and malicious changes resemble routine activity (Forescout, 2026-10-22).

Triage: a defrost cycle is normal; BFMTV reports, citing sector professionals, that installations can be programmed for two hours of defrost per 24 hours, whereas the reported attack is said to be a continuous forced defrost at a 50-degree setpoint held for hours (translated from French) (BFMTV, 2026-10-12).

Defender takeaway
Take any Danfoss AK-SM or AK-SC, Copeland xweb or Dixell xweb management interface off the internet now and restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network, as CERT-FR advises (CERT-FR, 2026-10-13), and ask the contractor whether its own remote access was affected; for the AK-SM800 and AK-SC355, replacement is the lever, since Danfoss says it had long advised supermarkets to move off those models (AFP, 2026-10-12), no fix exists for them according to NCSC Switzerland (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-13), and CERT-FR says a factory reset on an unpatched end-of-life unit removes the compromised instance's persistence but leaves the device vulnerable and almost certainly compromised again (CERT-FR, 2026-10-13). Because ANSSI puts the cause at exposure and weak passwords, a firmware update alone does not close the hole: the public address and the weak or default passwords have to go too, and ANSSI notes that its guidance on industrial systems has put not exposing them directly on the internet first since 2014 (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21).

It lists the Danfoss AK-SM 800 (end of life, no longer patched), the AK-SC 355 (phased out, no longer patched) and the current AK-SM 800A series when it runs outdated firmware, says no fixes exist for the two older models and that Danfoss urges replacing them, and says the attack could affect other sectors, such as healthcare for specialized cooling equipment, so organisations should check whether affected devices are in use (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-13). ANSSI's director general, Vincent Strubel, told the French Senate foreign-affairs committee on 2026-10-21 that the attack rested on elementary security flaws, starting with refrigeration equipment directly on the internet and administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, and he dismissed analyses that tied it to vulnerabilities researchers had published over the previous two years (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21). Its tracking of hacktivist groups counts over 20 claimed attacks on refrigeration systems since January 2026, the most active being the pro-Russian groups Z-Pentest Alliance and NoName057(16) through internet-exposed human-machine interfaces, and its count of exposed services is 12,976 observations on 6,017 public addresses in 99 countries, with 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1 (Forescout, 2026-10-22). Forescout adds that the manufacturers' documentation presents internet remote maintenance through port forwarding as a supported option, so the exposure is not only an accident of configuration (Forescout, 2026-10-22).

HIGHCVE-2026-97229exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-97229, GitLab CE/EE: an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler allows code execution on self-managed servers, has a public proof of concept and is listed by CISA as exploited; fixed in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8, and 19.4.1 does not close it (CVSS 10.0)

GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 (19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8) fixes CVE-2026-97229, an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that, "under certain conditions", could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server through a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration; GitLab scores it CVSS 3.1 10.0 with no privileges required (GitLab, 2026-10-12). Affected are self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2; CERT-EU and BleepingComputer name 19.3.4 as the 19.3 fix, which GitLab's page does not (CERT-EU, 2026-10-12; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-12). The 19.4.1 release of 2026-09-23 fixed two related flaws in the same component (GitLab, 2026-09-23) but is still affected (GitLab, 2026-10-12). NCSC Switzerland and CERT-EU both published advisories on 2026-10-12 (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-12; CERT-EU, 2026-10-12). Rapid7 reproduced the code execution on 19.4.1 and published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13 (Rapid7, 2026-10-13); CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29 on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-10-29), and NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory the same day to active exploitation, citing Alpine Linux (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-29). Alpine says a newly registered account sent crafted CI configurations to its GitLab 19.3.4 on 2026-10-20 and 21, crashing worker processes eight times, four of them partway through the exploit; it found no evidence that code ran, could not rule it out and rebuilt the instance (Alpine Linux, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Self-managed GitLab CE or EE on 19.2.x below 19.2.8, 19.3.x below 19.3.5 or 19.4.x below 19.4.2; GitLab's table starts at 19.2 and lists no earlier branch (GitLab, 2026-10-12). NCSC Switzerland states the prerequisites as network access to the instance and delivery of a crafted regular expression through CI/CD configuration (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-12); Rapid7 found the conditions: an attacker must first commit a malicious CI/CD configuration file and a repository path containing UTF-8 characters to a branch in a public project, which an ordinary account can do by creating a public project where the instance allows it (Rapid7, 2026-10-13), and on instances where new users can self-register and create projects that constraint is removed (Rapid7, 2026-10-13). An instance with open sign-up, or with public projects that untrusted users can write to, is the case to prioritise.
Detection
GitLab's release page lists six detections for exploitation attempts on self-managed instances (GitLab, 2026-10-12). Alpine saw the attack as crashes of GitLab worker processes after crafted CI configurations from a newly registered account, with 502 errors and failed CI jobs, and notes that a successful exploit would leave no crash and no trace in the web logs (Alpine Linux, 2026-10-28); in process-creation telemetry, shells, interpreters or network tools started as children of the GitLab application server processes are the sign of success, and a server where that turns up needs its CI/CD variables, runner registration tokens and deploy keys treated as exposed.

Triage: ordinary CI jobs run shells under the runners; only a shell spawned by the GitLab application server processes themselves matches this flaw, not one started inside a runner job.

Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 19.4.2, 19.3.5 or 19.2.8 now (GitLab, 2026-10-12), or better to 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6 or 19.2.9, the builds of 2026-10-21 that also fix a second CVSS 10 regular-expression compiler flaw, CVE-2026-110264 (GitLab, 2026-10-21), internet-facing instances first as CERT-EU advises (CERT-EU, 2026-10-12), then instances where new users can self-register and create projects, which removes the push-access constraint Rapid7 found (Rapid7, 2026-10-13); the fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab bundles in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby, from source or in a self-built image, needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well, and Alpine's GitLab on 19.3.6 with standard Ruby stayed vulnerable (Alpine Linux, 2026-10-28). CISA lists the flaw as exploited and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation, so an instance reachable on an affected version needs a compromise assessment as well as the upgrade; Rapid7's interim controls (restrict anonymous access to public projects and stop untrusted users creating or writing to public projects) reduce exposure only to the path it demonstrated (Rapid7, 2026-10-13).

  • Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance on 19.2, 19.3 or 19.4 to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 now, preferably to 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 or 19.5.1, which also fix CVE-2026-110264, internet-reachable instances and instances that allow open sign-up or public projects first, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation; where GitLab runs on its own Ruby (a source install or a container image that does not use GitLab's packages) also install Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9, because the fix is a Ruby patch that only GitLab's official packages carry. On any instance that was reachable on an affected version, run the six detections GitLab published on its release page and treat the CI/CD variables, runner registration tokens and deploy keys of any hit, or of an instance where compromise cannot be ruled out, as exposed.
    FindingCVE-2026-97229→
  • Find every RouterOS device whose www or www-ssl service answers from a network you do not trust and upgrade it to the fixed build for its channel: 7.24 or later on v7 stable, 7.23.8 on v7 long-term, 6.49.23 on v6 long-term; where an upgrade has to wait, restrict www and www-ssl under IP > Services to trusted addresses or disable them and manage the router over WinBox, SSH or a VPN.
    FindingCVE-2026-84411→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-13T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 2 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Standard 26 h window (2026-10-12T00:57Z to 2026-10-13T02:57Z), following the 2026-10-12 fire that published one entry. The mechanical KEV diff found no CISA KEV addition inside the window (catalog 2026.10.08) and no RANSOMWARE-flag flip on a covered CVE, and S1 read the catalogue itself and agrees. The four sub-agents returned 20 candidate items (S1 four, S2 eight, S3 four, S4 four); two ship as new entries, three become changelog records, and the rest are dropped below. No deep dive and no critical: the Danfoss incident and the GitLab flaw are high, since neither is shown to be exploited against, or deployed in, the constituency. The Patch Tuesday cycles of 2026-10-13 (Microsoft, Adobe, Fortinet, Ivanti, SAP's own page, the ICS sets) were not yet published when S1 checked at about 03:20Z (Microsoft publishes about 17:00 UTC), so the next fire must read them first (msrc cvrf 2026-Oct, the SAP page, Adobe and Fortinet bulletins); SAP's October CVE records were already public through its CNA and S1 found no pre-auth code execution, no exploited and no publicly disclosed flaw among them.

Published (2):

  • 2026-10-13/danfoss-ak-sm-ak-sc-french-supermarket-refrigeration-attack (incident, high): CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 reports numerous compromises of an internet-exposed controller class, with physical damage in hundreds of French stores and ANSSI saying other European countries may be affected. Relevance ground, stated here and not in the entry: a shared target profile (internet-exposed building and refrigeration controllers, often contractor-managed) under PD-11(c); no Swiss victim is named in any source, so the priority stays at high. It carries the 2026-08-28 Claroty entry in references[]; no source ties the attack to those CVEs, so no record was added there. S2 and S4 both returned it.
  • 2026-10-13/cve-2026-97229-gitlab-ci-regex-compiler-unauthenticated-rce (vulnerability, high): an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 code-execution flaw in self-managed GitLab, an out-of-band critical patch release, NCSC-CH and CERT-EU advisories within hours; PD-11(b) on the flaw's own mechanics (anonymous path to full control of a build server, 19.4.1 still affected), no exploitation reported. S1 and S2 both returned it.

Updated (3), each one record on the existing entry:

  • 2026-10-08/cve-2026-102255-sonicwall-sma1000-workplace-ssrf (update, priority stays high): NCSC Switzerland edited its advisory on 2026-10-12 to record the flaw as actively exploited, citing two honeypot operators (Defused from 2026-10-08, Previdian from 2026-10-09); SonicWall's advisory still says no evidence. The CVE status is not moved to exploited because the evidence is attempts against decoys.
  • 2026-10-10/cve-2026-84411-mikrotik-routeros-web-management-preauth-rce (correction, no float): the entry said the long-term releases were pending; MikroTik's own changelogs show 7.23.8 (2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (2026-10-07) already carry the fix, so the entry was imprecise when published. A correction rather than an update because the releases predate the entry; the vendor notice still reads pending.
  • 2026-10-09/publica-pk-softech-supplier-malware-intrusion-data-outflow (improvement, no float): Publica's own page of 2026-10-08 lists civil status and the IBAN among the data that could be affected, and the AWP wire relays the supplier's "rather small volume" and "may be business data" framing; the entry carried neither and the action now names the IBAN.
  • borderline-drop: P7 DarkSword iOS 18.4-18.7 exploit-kit variant (S3; iVerify 2026-10-08, Report URI 2026-10-09; lookback items); the exploited flaws have been fixed since 2025 and Apple extended iOS 18.7.7 to more devices on 2026-04-01, the kit leaked publicly in March and the 2026-10-10 fire already dropped the chain; the new facts (on-device keychain and wallet theft, delivery through a re-registered analytics domain and brokered traffic) change no decision for a managed fleet on current iOS. One source conflict is left for the audit: Apple's iOS 18.7.7 note does not name CVE-2026-20700, which GTIG says was fixed in iOS 26.3.
  • borderline-drop: Ghostscript CVE-2026-39919 (S3, Wordfence, CVSS 9.8); the exploit chain is build-specific (Wordfence's own exploits failed in 10,240 attempts across ten other environments), no exploitation, not in KEV, EPSS 0.0078, upstream fix 2026-09-08 and distribution advisories since September: regular patch cycle, and no Swiss deployment is established.
  • borderline-drop: ((OTRS)) Community Edition 6 and Znuny CVE-2026-93582 (S1, CVSS 9.4), needs an HTTP Basic backend plus header-to-environment mapping, 6.x is end of life, no exploitation, Znuny listed a matching advisory on 2026-09-16 (its body was not fetched), no Swiss deployment is established.
  • borderline-drop: Magecart fake-Stripe skimmer with a Sepolia smart-contract dead drop, and a ClickFix kit delivering a trojanised Fileside Electron app (S3, Report URI), one self-interested script-integrity vendor, indirect nexus, on-chain C2 resolution and ClickFix already covered.
  • borderline-drop: Anthropic's report on unintended model actions on US government sites (S4, primary 2026-10-09, outside the window), no constituency victim, ordinary web weaknesses, and the AI-agent incident family is already covered by the OpenAI and earlier Anthropic entries.
  • borderline-drop: Ahold Delhaize outage (S4; company release, NOS, BleepingComputer), no vector, actor or behaviour public (incident floor), no Swiss or public-sector nexus; BleepingComputer finds no link to the French refrigeration attack.
  • borderline-drop: FortiBleed Swiss exposure census, 4,313 FortiGate interfaces reachable in Switzerland (S2 and S4; Inside IT, Netzwoche, Risikomonitor; the primary report was not found); an exposure count adds no operational fact to the covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: FTAPI dataset published on The Gentlemen's leak site (S2; heise, 2026-10-12), single source, mostly marketing material plus an apparent customer list; the entry stays routine.
  • borderline-drop: Qilin core-member arrest (S2; NRW, Japan's NPA, lookback); a law-enforcement action that changes nothing defenders do; Ricardo (Swiss Marketplace Group) 890,000-account disclosure (S2, S4), no vector, no actor, no public-sector nexus (incident floor); N0n claim against about 50 maritime and port operators (S4), claim-only.
  • borderline-drop: S1 candidates held below the gate, IBM Guardium siblings, HPE Aruba AOS-S and ClearPass (2026-10-06), AnyDesk Linux CVE-2026-109390 (fixed in June), SAP October rows (CVE-2026-89111 library-level, 89110 and 89107 authenticated, 89108 administrator), ZITADEL, WinBox, HAProxy Data Plane API, phpMyFAQ, SmarterMail, Metasploit msf-ws, Veeam, ILIAS, Cisco Nexus and License bundles, authenticated, administrator-only, library-level or already patched, none exploited, no established constituency exposure.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): all four open rows were re-gated on today's facts and none changed state, so nothing is appended and each stays held on its named condition with its expiry unchanged. IBM Guardium Data Protection CVE-2026-85542 and its four unauthenticated siblings: none is in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.10.08), IBM's bulletin of 2026-10-08 lists CVE-2026-85542 as authenticated with no exploitation statement, ACN's alert is unchanged, no public proof of concept and no constituency deployment surfaced (expires 2026-10-14). SafePay claim on ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal and Payload claim on Netech: ransomware.live shows no press confirmation, S2 and S4 found no Swiss press report and neither victim site carries an incident notice (both expire 2026-10-14). Beyond Gravity: every public account still traces to the single 2026-10-02 company release as relayed by AWP, Inside IT and Netzwoche, with no vector, actor or data class named (expires 2026-10-20). The three rows that expire on 2026-10-14 are struck by the next fire if their conditions are still unmet.

Contradictions and discrepancies carried in the entries: (1) GitLab: CERT-EU and BleepingComputer give 19.3.4 as the 19.3 fix, the vendor page names 19.3.5 and says 19.3.4 had a merge-request page bug; the entry uses the vendor figure. (2) SonicWall: NCSC Switzerland says actively exploited, the vendor advisory says no evidence; both statements are in the entry, with the evidence limited to attempts against decoys. (3) Danfoss: Infosecurity quotes Intermarché at 150 stores while AFP and BFMTV give 300 Intermarché or Netto shops; BFMTV says 300 is twice the first estimate of 150, so the entry says the counts moved during the day. Single-source facts: the forced 50-degree defrost and the "older than version 4" scope are BFMTV's reporting alone.

Rotation: ranking used the derived cursor; 78 standard or candidate records (S1 12, S2 24, S3 42) were set aside as attempted in the previous two fires, and S4's pool of 19 breach and ransomware sources was entirely inside those two fires, so its 14 oldest-cursor records were swept anyway.

Coverage gaps: prodaft (no dated listing reachable on any transport; WebSearch only); zaufana-trzecia-strona (undated listing); ransomware-live (recentvictims capped at 100); sap-security-notes (October page 404 until later on 2026-10-13); hadrian-labs, depthfirst, esentire, socradar, msft-ti and proofpoint (listing or extract quirks, no in-window item). Reader credit: extract fell through to the metered reader on 404 and 403 responses (a not-yet-published SAP page, a GitHub advisory, anydesk.com, fortiguard.fortinet.com and psirt.global.sonicwall.com).

For the next audit: (1) tools/fetch_source.py extract falls back to the metered reader on any 404 or 403, spending credit on URLs that merely do not exist yet; S1 suggests url --direct first for such URLs, and a flag to disable the fallback would remove the cost; (2) CERT-FR ALERT bulletins are not in cert-fr avis-recent: the Danfoss alert was found only through the alert feed, now recorded in the anssi-fr notes, and a recipe subcommand would make it routine; (3) S2 suggests a Swiss-press lookback through the cash.ch sitemaps (recorded in the source notes) and notes that the Zug cantonal ISG consultation runs to 2026-11-09 and that CRA manufacturer reporting applied from 2026-09-11 (ENISA); (4) the Apple iOS 18.7.7 note versus GTIG on CVE-2026-20700 (see the DarkSword drop) if the kit resurfaces.

Source health and verification: the probe covered 242 records (241 relevant, 1 stale) and its UNSOLVED list held one record, ico-uk [needs-demote], a false alarm: the recipe downloads a 5 MB sitemap and a cold fetch passed the 45 s probe budget twice, while the same recipe returned in 3 s once cached. tools/source_health.py now honours a per-source probe_timeout (set to 120 on ico-uk) and tools/test_source_health.py covers it; the snapshot in state/source_health.json still shows the false alarm until the next sweep. Verification so far: iteration 1 (truth 9, editorial 5, advisory 4) found hedges missing from the Danfoss title and summary, an unsupported "no security updates" claim, a MikroTik headline that overstated the changelogs, attribution slips in the SonicWall and Publica records and a missing downtime note; all were fixed or declined with a reason. Iteration 2 (truth 4, advisory 4) found one false negative in the Danfoss Exposure line, a registry summary stating the defrost as fact, and two more hedges; all were fixed except one declined F11, the CISA citation date on the MikroTik entry, which iteration 3 raised again and which is now corrected (the advisory's own number, ICSA-26-272, dates it 2026-09-29). Iteration 3 (truth 1, advisory 4) found two stale statements in these notes and wording slips, all fixed. Iteration 4 (truth 5) found a clause in an older SonicWall update section that Defused contradicted, an affected-version range on the MikroTik entry that ignored the long-term builds, an action line on the Publica entry that overlooked Publica's own statement, a Previdian citation date that was the last-observed date, and an off-by-one source count in these notes; all were fixed. Iteration 5 (truth 0, editorial 1, advisory 5) found no wrong claim: it added the retailers' own framing of the attack as hitting a refrigeration service provider or supplier, which the Danfoss entry now carries with a takeaway asking the contractor whether its own remote access was affected, and four wording and consistency points. The low-residual early exit applies (truth plus editorial is 1, no F1 or F4), so the remediations were applied and the run published without a sixth pass; the provider sentences were checked by hand against the AFP and BleepingComputer pages read this run. Residual: the Danfoss changes made after iteration 5 (headline, provider sentences, trims) have had no independent pass, and the SonicWall status stays patch-available on evidence limited to decoys, which a reader may weigh differently from the Atlassian entry.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-12
item.description: • Bricksforge's Pro Forms upload flaw is exploited without login since 7 October; fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0, related fix in 4.0.1. Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's revised changelog states the flaw was fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0 and lists a related Pro Forms upload fix in 4.0.1 of 2026-10-08; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry. →
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Bricksforge's Pro Forms upload flaw is exploited without login since 7 October; fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0, related fix in 4.0.1. Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's revised changelog states the flaw was fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0 and lists a related Pro Forms upload fix in 4.0.1 of 2026-10-08; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry. →
Trending vulnerabilities 1Action items 1

01Trending vulnerabilities1 item

NOTABLECVE-2026-85097exploitedupdatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-85097, Bricksforge for WordPress: an unauthenticated upload in the Pro Forms module writes attacker PHP into the uploads directory, exploited since 7 October; fixed in 3.1.8.10 and 4.0.0, with a related upload fix in 4.0.1 (CVSS 9.8)

Bricksforge's Pro Forms module checks a file's type when it is first uploaded but trusts the file metadata the client sends when the form is submitted, in particular the url field of the temporaryFileUploads parameter (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). An attacker obtains a nonce from the unauthenticated bricksforge_regenerate_nonce AJAX endpoint, uploads a GIF/PHP polyglot that passes the type check, then submits a form whose file path names that image and whose url ends in a PHP extension; the plugin writes the image's content to the PHP path and one request to it executes the code (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). Versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 are affected (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). The vendor's changelog, revised after the disclosure, states that the flaw was fixed in 3.1.8.10 and in 4.0.0, and lists a related security fix in the same Pro Forms upload area in 4.0.1 of 2026-10-08 (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13); Patchstack also names 3.1.8.10 (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). Dr. Web credits Wordfence with a CVSS score of 9.8 and Patchstack with 10.0 (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09).

Patchstack's telemetry first recorded exploitation attempts on 2026-10-07 at 21:47 UTC, from 63 distinct source addresses, and it calls the activity automated without attributing it (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). Patchstack describes exploitation attempts and says an attacker with execution can deploy web shells, modify site content, read data and persist (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). It counts about 6,000 active installations (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09), Previdian lists it as exploited in the wild and links public proof-of-concept code (Previdian, 2026-10-08), and the flaw is not in CISA's KEV catalog (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09).

Exposure
WordPress sites running Bricksforge versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 (Patchstack, 2026-10-08) with the Pro Forms module active, including sites whose forms have no upload field (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13). Patchstack and Dr. Web bound the affected range at 3.1.8.9 (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09); the vendor states that 4.0.0 already carries the fix, while the related upload issue fixed in 4.0.1 affects every site with Pro Forms active, and the changelog names no 3.x build for that second fix (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13). Bricksforge is not in the wordpress.org plugin directory, so no public version statistics exist, and updates come with an annual licence, so a site with a lapsed licence may not receive the fix (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09).
Detection
In web server and WordPress access logs, POST requests to /wp-json/bricksforge/v1/form_submit or to admin-ajax with the bricksforge_form_submit action that carry a temporaryFileUploads value pairing an image path with a PHP-extension destination, preceded by a call to the nonce endpoint and repeated with changing extensions, case or encodings, from 2026-10-07 onward; in file-integrity and endpoint telemetry, new PHP files in the WordPress uploads tree, the plugin's temporary upload folder first, and web requests to them (Patchstack, 2026-10-08). Patchstack says a site that ran a vulnerable version without protection should have its historical logs and the host reviewed for unexpected PHP files, unusual application activity and unauthorized changes (Patchstack, 2026-10-08); Dr. Web adds a check of the user list for unknown administrator accounts (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09).
Defender takeaway
Update every Bricksforge site to 4.0.1 or later now, since the vendor lists the related Pro Forms upload fix only there; a 3.x site needs at least 3.1.8.10 (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13); where that is not possible, deactivate Pro Forms or the plugin and block PHP execution in the uploads directory (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09). On a site that was reachable and unpatched since 2026-10-07, run the log and file search above, and if code turns up restore from a backup older than 2026-10-07 and change all passwords (Dr. Web, 2026-10-09).
Update19 Oct 2026 21:03 UTCrun 2026-10-18T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Bricksforge has revised its changelog: CVE-2026-85097 itself "was fixed earlier in 3.1.8.10 and in 4.0.0", and the 4.0.1 release of 2026-10-08 fixes a related issue in the same Pro Forms upload area that affects every site with Pro Forms active, including forms without upload fields (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13). The same changelog lists no 3.x build for that second fix, so a site on 3.1.8.10 is protected against the exploited flaw but not shown as covered for the related one; 4.0.1 or later carries both (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13). Version 4.0.2 of 2026-10-13 stops the upload check introduced in 4.0.1 from rejecting about one normal image in sixty and tightens access checks on the plugin's REST endpoints (Bricksforge, 2026-10-13). Previdian now lists the flaw as exploited in the wild, based on third-party reporting, and links public proof-of-concept code (Previdian, 2026-10-08).

vulnerability12 Oct 03:21Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Patchstack · Bricksforge (vendor changelog) · Dr. Web · Previdian

02Action items1 item

  • Find every WordPress site that your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with Bricksforge and update it to version 4.0.1 or later (at least 3.1.8.10 on the 3.x line) now, treating any site that was reachable and unpatched since 2026-10-07 as one to search for dropped PHP files.
    FindingCVE-2026-85097→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-12T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 1 entry published

Verification & coverage notes

Quiet Monday window: the 26 h window (2026-10-11T00:57Z to 2026-10-12T02:57Z) followed a weekend, and the newest item on every authority source (NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL, BSI, CERT-FR, CERT-EU, CERT.at, CISA, ENISA, Europol, OFAC) is dated 2026-10-09 or earlier. The mechanical KEV diff found no CISA KEV addition inside the window (catalog 2026.10.08) and no RANSOMWARE-flag flip on a covered CVE, and S1 read the catalogue itself and agrees. Four sub-agents returned seven candidate items (S1 three, S2 none, S3 one, S4 three), all marked borderline by their authors. One new entry ships and no existing entry changed: no deep dive, no critical. The scheduled vendor cycles (Microsoft Patch Tuesday, SAP, Adobe) land on 2026-10-13 and Oracle's CPU on 2026-10-20, so none fell in this window; Microsoft's early October release has no exploited or publicly disclosed CVE in its structured fields.

Published: 2026-10-12/cve-2026-85097-bricksforge-pro-forms-upload-php-exploited (notable): a pre-auth upload-to-PHP flaw in a paid WordPress add-on, exploited since 2026-10-07 per Patchstack's telemetry, vendor fix available. It is first coverage from a rotational source's lookback (PD-7(d); Patchstack's primary is dated 2026-10-08, outside the 26 h window); no earlier record carries a disposition for it, because the 2026-10-11 S1 raised it from outside its slice. Relevance ground, stated here and not in the entry: an exploited unauthenticated code-execution flaw with a vendor fix clears PD-11(b), the vendor is German and the add-on is sold to site builders in the DACH region, and no source shows a Swiss public-sector deployment, so the priority is notable and the entry is held short.

  • borderline-drop: Ricardo (SMG Swiss Marketplace Group), about 890,000 accounts with names, addresses and phone numbers exposed, announced 2026-10-09 (S4, re-raised from lookback; the 2026-10-11 fire already dropped it), Swiss home region and victim-confirmed, but a private consumer marketplace with no vector, no actor and no public-sector nexus (incident floor); the only mappable technique would rest on the word "vulnerability" alone.
  • borderline-drop: ShinyHunters / FBI portal case, arrest of a Canadian ransomware-negotiation executive and the group's no-release statement (S4, update-of; the 2026-10-11 fire already dropped the arrest), a law-enforcement development with no tradecraft or hardening content, the identity rests on Krebs's sources and court records the FBI has not confirmed.
  • borderline-drop: IDC Frontier IDCF Cloud fourth report of 2026-10-09 (S4, update-of), a response-organisation notice with no technical, scope or recovery fact beyond the covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: expired-domain script hijack delivering the P7 DarkSword iOS chain through a dead analytics tag (S3; Report URI, iVerify), exploitation of the domain re-registration rests on one researcher who sells a script-integrity product, no independent report, no public-sector site named, and the iOS chain was already dropped by the 2026-10-10 fire.
  • borderline-drop: Chrome 155 stable, 247 security fixes, no exploitation statement (S1), already dropped by the 2026-10-10 fire.
  • borderline-drop: "PoC available" tags on CVE-2026-107406 and CVE-2026-84411 (S1), Previdian's tag, and S1's own look at the GitHub repositories shows README-only exploit-sale or lure pages, not exploit code; low confidence, attacker-adjacent URLs, and neither covered entry claims a public proof of concept.
  • borderline-drop: SmarterMail build 9777 (post-authentication, aggregator-only CVE), Apache Struts S2-075 to S2-078 (denial of service or disclosure, no code execution), Zimbra 10.1.21, the NCSC-NL Kiteworks bulletin, Android and Apple bulletins, the EUVD weekend batch, and the Cisco, HPE, IBM Verify, Splunk and Veeam bundles that earlier fires held below the gate, no exploitation, no public exploit, no established constituency exposure (S1).
  • borderline-drop: CloudSEK NEBULA (executive summary only, full report gated, no nexus), Booz Allen OT-lab study of frontier models (lab only, whitepaper gated), Zenity AgentCorruption (patched, vendor disputes the framing), OpenAI's influence-operations report, the MonsterCloud indictment, the Silent Ransom Group leak-origin story, ASOS breach (consumer retailer, vector unconfirmed) (S3).
  • borderline-drop: Swiss leak-site claims with no victim statement or press confirmation (Camandona SA, Hotel Delfino Lugano, Boullard Musique, dd-automation, stuecheli, Rueeggerseg AG); claim-only listings fail PD-6 (S2, S4).
  • out-of-window: Zug draft cantonal Information Security Act and ordinance in consultation since 2026-07-15 (comments to 2026-11-09, S2), a draft with a comment deadline, not an obligation, and 89 days old.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): all four open rows were re-gated on today's facts and none changed state, so nothing is appended; each stays held on its named condition with its expiry unchanged. IBM Guardium Data Protection CVE-2026-85542 and the four related unauthenticated flaws: none is in CISA KEV, IBM's bulletin makes no exploitation statement and no constituency deployment surfaced (expires 2026-10-14). SafePay claim on ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal and Payload claim on Netech: ransomware.live shows no press confirmation, no Swiss press report exists and the victims' own sites carry no notice (both expire 2026-10-14). Beyond Gravity: every public account still traces to the single company statement of 2026-10-02, with no vector, actor or data named (expires 2026-10-20).

Single-source: 2026-10-12/cve-2026-85097-bricksforge-pro-forms-upload-php-exploited: Patchstack is the only observer of the exploitation; Dr. Web restates it, the vendor changelog confirms an upload fix in 4.0.1 without naming the CVE, and the CVE record's assigner (Wordfence) scores it 9.8 where Patchstack scores it 10.0. The CISA enrichment on the CVE record lists exploitation as none, stamped about three hours after the Patchstack article.

Rotation: ranking used the derived cursor; 81 standard or candidate records (S1 27, S2 24, S3 30) were set aside as attempted in the previous two fires, and S4's pool of 19 breach and ransomware sources is smaller than a slice, so nine of its twelve records were swept although the previous two fires had attempted them.

Coverage gaps: apa-ots (no listing or feed route; WebSearch only); swissinfo-ger (the extracted homepage is a stale 2026-09-29 snapshot); cloudsek-triad (executive summaries only; the full report is gated); sentinellabs and proofpoint listings recipes re-confirmed. Reader credit: extract fell through to the metered reader on community.citrix.com, psirt.global.sonicwall.com and source.android.com, and one key rotated on an HTTP 402.

For the next audit: (1) an optional improvement on 2026-10-06/denmark-cpr-population-register-third-party-access-breach: TV 2 Kosmopol, relaying Ritzau on 2026-10-09, says the CPR office's notification states the actor did not use the access for the whole period and that the compromise appears to have stopped on 2026-09-20, which reconciles the minister's ten days with Ritzau's 21 days and 17 hours that the entry sets side by side; (2) S1 suggests a cheap gate for any "PoC available" claim: the unauthenticated GitHub repository search plus the contents API separates exploit code from README-only exploit-sale repositories; (3) S3 flags the DNSSEC root key rollover of 2026-10-11 as a watch item only if a resolver-outage report appears.

Source health: the probe covered 241 records (240 relevant, 1 stale: threatpost, already demoted and handled) and its UNSOLVED list was empty, so no repair was owed this run. Verification: two iterations, no entry dropped. Iteration 1 (truth 4, editorial 7, advisory 3) found attribution and citation slips, the unaccounted-for 4.0.0 release, a missing public proof-of-concept statement and a duplicated action; all but the unreadable VulnCheck listing were fixed. Iteration 2 (truth 1, advisory 2) found one clause attributed to Patchstack that its page does not state, and it was removed. The low-residual early exit applies (truth plus editorial is 1, no F1 or F4), so the residual of 1 was remediated after the last pass and not re-verified.

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Microsoft: a China-aligned implant hides in legitimate software via DLL sideloading and takes modules over WebSockets.
